summary: Deep audit of android-base (generator, template, web, api) plus PeriFlow/VitFleet learnings, research and on-device perf baseline; each area verified

result.summary:
I audited android-base/generator and tools/ without running Gradle. The 116 unit tests pass in about 2 seconds. I generated 159 feature combinations (every preset, each feature on its own, each feature removed from "all", the 18 pairwise sets, and 60 random subsets, each with all 5 languages) and ran static checks on every output: markers, template names, module includes, imports, dropped symbols, version-catalogue aliases, convention plugins, manifest entries, resources, translations and Hilt bindings. None of them found a reference to something that had been stripped, so the marker engine and the template agree for the feature matrix. All the real breakage is in the paths around that matrix.

1. Scaffolded modules and generated lines are renamed twice. Package names like com.example.databaseapp or com.firebaseapp.notes crash generation; com.base.apple becomes com.base.applele; and module database_app under app "Store" turns into :data:datastore.
2. `--icon` writes malformed adaptive-icon XML, so every project generated with a custom icon fails to build. This has been there since the first commit.
3. A valid spec such as features ["auth"] with no feature modules produces an app whose start screen is `error(...)`, so it crashes on launch. CI never builds that case.
4. Validation checks package names against Python's keyword list, so com.global.bank is rejected while com.example.null and java.* are accepted. Kotlin keywords are accepted as module names, which breaks compilation.
5. Signing breaks silently in two ways. If the key password differs from the store password, keytool ignores it but keystore.properties records it, so release signing fails. Non-ASCII passwords are written as UTF-8 and read back by Gradle as ISO-8859-1.
6. add_feature.py adds an untranslated module to multi-language projects, which lint rejects, and puts the new tab first, which silently changes the start screen.
7. In the CLI, `--json` output is not valid JSON. `--out` means the parent folder for zips but the project folder with `--no-zip`, and with `--force` this deleted a sibling project in my test. The wizard only validates at the very end, so one early typo throws away every answer.
8. generate_headless.py does not always fail with JSON, and it treats a string as a list of characters ("home" became modules h, o, m, e). The Go API types its requests, so this only matters for direct callers.

Generated apps also carry dead weight: about 43 unused version-catalogue entries in a lean project, two never-used Gradle plugin files, and leftover strings. The database feature pulls in networking only because of how a build plugin is switched on.

On structure, render.py is an 800-line catch-all whose regex steps silently do nothing if the template changes. That will get in the way of the Compose Multiplatform and SwiftUI generators. The tests have gaps: a mid-file unittest.main() skips 5 tests when the file is run directly, nothing tests icons, headless or add_feature, and CI never builds the standard preset (the website default) or the firebase-off variant files.

The full report includes fix sketches and a plan for adding Kyant liquid glass as an optional generator feature, based on how PeriFlow wires it.

findings.title: Scaffold output and generated blocks are renamed twice; packages/modules containing template tokens break or crash generation
findings.evidence: build.py:48-49 writes scaffold modules (already using spec.package_name) before render.rewrite_all, which applies rename(strip_markers(...)) (render.py:248) to everything incl. generated lines; rename() is a chained str.replace (render.py:115-126). Reproduced: package com.example.databaseapp / com.firebaseapp.notes / com.base_app.demo -> RenderError 'AppConfig.kt not found'; com.base.apple -> 12 files 'package com.base.applele.feature.orders'; com.base.app.demo -> 'com.base.app.demo.demo'; module database_app (app Store) -> include(":data:datastore") with dir data/database_app; app 'Xbaseapp' -> rootProject 'Xxbaseapp' and XxbaseappApplication.
findings.recommendation: Single-pass regex rename (one alternation, mapping dict) applied to template text only: strip_markers(rename(original), ...) so generated lines are never renamed, and run scaffold.write_feature_modules after rewrite_all. Add regression tests for com.example.databaseapp, com.base.apple, module database_app, app Xbaseapp.

findings.title: --icon produces malformed adaptive-icon XML (regex replacement drops capture groups)
findings.evidence: re.sub(r'(<monochrome[^>]*android:drawable=")@drawable/[A-Za-z0-9_]+(")', r"@drawable/ic_launcher_monochrome", text) — ran it on the template's ic_launcher.xml: output line is '    @drawable/ic_launcher_monochrome />', ElementTree: 'not well-formed (invalid token): line 5, column 4'. Present since initial commit be9c689; VitFleet (generated with --icon) carries the hand-correct form.
findings.recommendation: Use r"\g<1>@drawable/ic_launcher_monochrome\g<2>"; add a Pillow-free unit test parsing the rewritten XML; install Pillow in CI and build one --icon project.

findings.title: Valid specs without any tab-providing feature or module generate an app that crashes on launch
findings.evidence: fallback = 'error("Set a start destination: ...")'. Generated features=["auth"]: AppDestinations has empty tabs and 'val start = tabs.firstOrNull()?.key ?: error(...)'; MainActivity.kt:79 reads AppDestinations.signIn at startup (object init throws) and FeatureBindingsModule.kt:18 reads AppDestinations.start. CI matrix always adds feature_modules ["orders"] so it is never built.
findings.recommendation: Refuse such specs in ProjectSpec.validated() or auto-scaffold a 'home' feature module; add a no-modules, no-screens row to the CI Gradle matrix.

findings.title: Kotlin hard keywords accepted as feature module names
findings.evidence: validate_module_name only checks ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ and RESERVED_MODULE_NAMES. Modules 'in','fun','object','null','class' generated 'package com.example.trail.feature.in', 'package com.example.trail.data.null' — compile errors.
findings.recommendation: Share one reserved-segment set (Kotlin hard keywords + Java keywords/literals) between package and module validation.

findings.title: Package validation uses Python's keyword list: rejects valid names, accepts invalid ones
findings.evidence: keyword.iskeyword(segment) or segment in _JAVA_KEYWORDS. Reproduced: com.global.bank and com.example.pass rejected ('reserved word'); com.example.null, com.example.true, com.example.typealias and java.trail.notes accepted and generated ('package com.example.null'). _JAVA_KEYWORDS (spec.py:1005-1012) lacks null/true/false/typealias/typeof.
findings.recommendation: Drop Python keywords; use explicit Kotlin hard keywords + Java reserved words/literals; reject leading 'java' segment; cap package length (~100).

findings.title: Different store/key passwords produce PKCS12 keys that release signing cannot open
findings.evidence: keytool -storetype PKCS12 ignores -keypass ('Different store and key passwords not supported for PKCS12 KeyStores. Ignoring user-specified -keypass value.') but write_keystore_properties records keyPassword=K. Reproduced gen-keys2: KeyStore.getKey(alias, 'keypass222') -> UnrecoverableKeyException. Wizard asks key password separately (prompts.py:465); web sends equal values.
findings.recommendation: Reject key_password != store_password for generated PKCS12 keys in validate_keystore (or write keyPassword = storePassword) and surface keytool warnings.

findings.title: Non-ASCII keystore passwords written as UTF-8 but read as ISO-8859-1 by the template
findings.evidence: _properties_value escapes only backslash and leading spaces; file written UTF-8 (render.py:422); template Signing.kt:28-29 uses Properties.load(inputStream()). Reproduced: password 'pässwörd1' reads back as 'pÃ¤sswÃ¶rd1' -> 'keystore password was incorrect'.
findings.recommendation: Escape non-ASCII as \uXXXX in _properties_value and/or load with reader(Charsets.UTF_8) in Signing.kt.

findings.title: add_feature.py leaves new modules untranslated and makes the new tab the start destination
findings.evidence: On a 5-language project: feature/wallet/src/main/res has only values/ while siblings have values-de..pt-rBR (lint MissingTranslation). register_tabs inserts right after 'listOf(' -> tabs become WalletListKey, SampleListKey, ... and start = tabs.first. generator-spec.json/README not updated by add/remove_feature.
findings.recommendation: Read languages from generator-spec.json and write scaffold translations; insert tabs at the generated-tabs position; update generator-spec.json feature_modules; consider capping tabs at 5.

findings.title: create_project.py --json prints the human summary before the JSON
findings.evidence: prompts.summarise(spec) runs unconditionally before the json branch (:141). Reproduced: stdout begins '\nSummary\n───────'; json.load -> 'Expecting value: line 2 column 1'. AGENTS.md tells agents to use --json.
findings.recommendation: Skip or redirect all human output to stderr when --json is set (summarise, confirm_overwrite, report).

findings.title: --out means parent dir for zip but project dir for --no-zip; --force then rmtree's it
findings.evidence: resolve_destination returns out for --no-zip, out/<Name>.zip otherwise; build.py:84 shutil.rmtree(destination). Reproduced: --out parentdir --no-zip --force deleted sibling parentdir/ExistingProjectA; same --out in zip mode wrote parentdir/JsonCheck.zip and kept it.
findings.recommendation: Give --out one meaning (the project path); refuse --force on a directory holding a different project or home/root.

findings.title: Wizard validates only at the end and asks URL questions against unresolved features
findings.evidence: Module docstring claims it re-asks what validated() rejects, but run_wizard (:494-539) validates once at the end; SpecError exits 1 after ~40 answers. ask_environments(features) checks 'network' in the raw selection (:244), so picking auth/sample alone skips backend URLs. :159 'com.example.' + re.sub(...) or 'com.example.app' precedence bug; :342/:354 silently clamp choices.
findings.recommendation: Validate each answer when typed using per-field validators; resolve_features before dependent sections; fix the precedence.

findings.title: Headless protocol: non-JSON failures and string-as-list coercion
findings.evidence: Bodies [], "x", null, {app_name:5}, {api_base_urls:["x"]} -> tracebacks on stderr, empty stdout (only SpecError/TypeError caught at :95-100). {feature_modules:"home"} succeeded with modules h,o,m,e; {haptics_enabled:"false"} -> haptics on; {version_code:1.5} accepted. Go API types requests, so web is mostly shielded.
findings.recommendation: One try around main; check payload is a dict and type-check each field against a small schema before building ProjectSpec.

findings.title: Keystore passwords passed on keytool argv; --save-spec writes them in plain text
findings.evidence: '-storepass', keystore.store_password, '-keypass', keystore.key_password readable via /proc/<pid>/cmdline, while headless docstring stresses not exposing passwords; create_project.save_spec (:329-336) serialises keystores incl. passwords whereas record.py strips them.
findings.recommendation: Use -storepass:env/-keypass:env with subprocess env; omit or warn about passwords in save_spec.

findings.title: database requires room requires network only because of a convention-plugin gate
findings.evidence: database requires=("room",); room requires network. Template registers androidRoom under <opt:room> (build-logic/convention/build.gradle.kts:81-87); core/database depends only on :core:common. An offline app wanting a DB must ship Ktor + response cache + queue.
findings.recommendation: Gate the registration with <opt:room|database>, own the plugin file accordingly, drop requires=("room",) from database.

findings.title: Generated projects carry dead convention plugins, ~43 unreferenced catalog entries and orphan resources
findings.evidence: AndroidFirebaseConventionPlugin.kt kept when firebase off (70/159 combos), AndroidRoomConventionPlugin.kt when room/database off (63/159) — not in Feature.files. libs.versions.toml has 4 markers: bare project has 43/93 libraries and 5/13 plugins unreferenced. forms off leaves 11 validation_* strings (translated too); push off leaves drawable/ic_notification.xml.
findings.recommendation: Add the plugin files to feature ownership (expression-based ownership for room|database), fence TOML entries and validation strings with markers, add ic_notification.xml to push.files.

findings.title: Module names that collapse to the same Pascal name produce conflicting imports
findings.evidence: order_history and order__history both accepted; AppDestinations.kt imports OrderHistoryListKey and 'R as OrderHistoryR' twice (lines 7-10 of generated file).
findings.recommendation: Reject '__', trailing '_', and pascal() collisions in validation.

findings.title: No length limits: long packages crash with OSError (uncaught in CLI)
findings.evidence: 8x28-char segment package -> OSError [Errno 36] File name too long at core/database/schemas/<pkg>.core.database.AppDatabase; create_project.py:137 catches only RenderError. Windows MAX_PATH is far tighter.
findings.recommendation: Cap package (~100) and app_name (~30) lengths; catch OSError/TranslationError/TypeError in the CLI.

findings.title: App display name restricted to ASCII letters/digits/space/._-
findings.evidence: Mom's Kitchen, Tom & Jerry, Café Olé, Rocket 🚀, 2048 Game, Say "Hi" all rejected; apply_app_name (render.py:376-403) inserts the name unescaped, which is why.
findings.recommendation: Separate display_name (any Unicode, XML/aapt-escaped) from derived identifier forms (NFKD->ASCII with fallback).

findings.title: Marker engine silently tolerates mismatched/unclosed/unknown markers
findings.evidence: Mismatched close just 'continue's (:85-87); no unclosed-at-EOF check; unknown feature names always stripped; <opt:!a|b> unsupported (_INLINE_ELSE excludes '|', line kept with marker). Template currently clean (0 issues, 47 files, 518 markers) but nothing enforces it.
findings.recommendation: Raise RenderError with path:line; validate names against FEATURES_BY_KEY; add a unit test scanning template/; add block-level else markers.

findings.title: collapse_blank_runs reformats 114 marker-free files
findings.evidence: Applied to every text file; e.g. blank line after 'sealed interface AppResult<out T> {' removed; catalog/build.gradle.kts changed. Makes regenerate-and-compare diffs noisy and contradicts the test's own 'reformatting code nobody asked it to touch'.
findings.recommendation: Only collapse around regions strip_markers actually removed.

findings.title: Line endings rewritten: gradlew.bat CRLF->LF on Linux; everything CRLF on Windows
findings.evidence: template/gradlew.bat has 94 CRs, generated has 0; read_text/write_text use universal newlines (render.py:189, 234, 255), so a Windows CLI run would write CRLF gradlew into the zip (the failure .gitattributes documents).
findings.recommendation: read_text(newline="") / write_text(newline="") everywhere to preserve endings.

findings.title: Stripping leaves unused imports and orphan comments in generated code
findings.evidence: AppDestinations.kt unused import R (34 combos) and AppIcons (30); ProfileScreen Row (profile on, media off); FeatureBindingsModule AppDestinations; KtorNetworkClientTest JsonPrimitive/buildJsonObject (room off); orphan '// Settings sits last…' and '// ── tooling ──' headers.
findings.recommendation: Move the imports/comments inside the matching <opt:> blocks in the template; promote the unused-import check to a unit test.

findings.title: Silent-no-op regex appliers tied to exact template text
findings.evidence: apply_feel replaces one exact line 'AppTheme(mode = themeMode, hapticsEnabled = settings.hapticsEnabled) {'; apply_fonts/apply_accent/_apply_on_brand/_list_languages return silently when file/pattern missing. Works today (verified) but any template rename silently drops user choices; test uses a fake AppRoot.kt.
findings.recommendation: Count substitutions and raise on zero; replace regexes with explicit <generated:…> placeholders declared per target.

findings.title: render.py/spec.py are god modules with Android paths baked in
findings.evidence: render.py (804 lines) holds markers, rename, copy, overlay, AppConfig, fonts, feel, strings, keystores, zip, git and ~220 lines of colour science (:587-804); prompts imports private _to_argb; catalogue imports render for find_keytool; spec.py 1028 lines mixes data, presets, validation; spec->translations->scaffold->spec cycle broken by lazy import.
findings.recommendation: Split into genkit/core (spec, graph, markers, rename, packaging), genkit/android adapter, genkit/brand.py; keep target-specific substitution points declared in the template, ready for CMP/SwiftUI targets.

findings.title: Test suite and CI gaps (mid-file unittest.main, unused fixtures, missing coverage)
findings.evidence: unittest.main() at line 779 precedes RecordTest/CommitStampTest/CompileSdkTest/BrandContrastTest: direct run executes 98 tests vs 103 via -m unittest. tests/spec_keys.json and tools/feature_combinations.py unused by any test/CI. No tests for icons, headless, add_feature, zip, keystores, scaffold+rename. CI Gradle matrix (none/lean/everything/all) never builds the standard preset, a zero-module project, or the firebase-off variant files. Stale ktlint/detekt justifications at :182, :196, :216.
findings.recommendation: Move unittest.main to EOF; add tests/test_consistency.py from .overhaul/scratch-gen/check.py+hilt.py+markers.py over presets and pairwise sets; add standard and no-module rows to CI; delete or use spec_keys.json; fix stale comments.

findings.title: Generated README gives commands that fail and describes absent features
findings.evidence: 'py add_feature.py orders --project . --tab' and 'py remove_feature.py' run from the project root, where the scripts do not exist (template AGENTS.md correctly says python3 path/to/generator/add_feature.py); Structure lists catalog/ (:81) and onboarding/sign-in gates (:99) unconditionally; four blank lines at :181-184.
findings.recommendation: Point at the generator path, render structure/gates from the enabled features, use python3 consistently.

findings.title: Presets/defaults disagree; 'Everything' omits 7 features; duplicated defaults
findings.evidence: Everything excludes applock, composemetrics, coverage, database, depsanalysis, licenses, playstore. Feature.default set vs standard preset: analytics default-on but not in standard; browser/language/profile in standard but default-off. catalogue.py:185-198 duplicates ProjectSpec defaults; catalogue fontSuggestions differs from prompts.FONT_SUGGESTIONS.
findings.recommendation: Derive wizard defaults from the standard preset (single source), rename or complete 'Everything', reference ProjectSpec defaults in the catalogue.

findings.title: Dead code and stale/contradictory comments
findings.evidence: RenderResult never constructed (wrong type hint at create_project.py:344); Feature.implied_only never true but handled in 7 places; _TEMPLATE_ONLY points at nonexistent catalog/src/test/screenshots; duplicate executable tables (render.py:202-203 vs :516); remove_feature.normalise keeps a self-described 'Unreachable' branch; generate_headless.py:33/:104 cite explanations the docstring lacks and 'nine render steps'; prompts.ask_password docstring contradicts itself; spec.py:641 'Signing' header over MOTION_STYLES.
findings.recommendation: Delete the dead symbols/branches, fix or remove the stale cross-references, keep comments to the why.

findings.title: 'Reuse the dev key for staging' generates a different key
findings.evidence: replace(shared, name='staging') makes generate_keystores run keytool again (render.py:472-505) producing a new key pair with the same alias/password.
findings.recommendation: Copy dev.jks to staging.jks when reuse is chosen.

missed: generator/genkit/scaffold.py:131-135 with :104-105 — when network is on, the scaffolded data module declares 'data class {Name}Item(val id: Int, val title: String)' without @Serializable, but DefaultRepository calls networkClient.get<List<{Name}Item>>(). That reaches NetworkJson.decodeFromJsonElement<T> (template core/network/NetworkClient.kt:48-52), and kotlinx has no serializer for the class. Every response, even '[]', fails with SerializationException, which is wrapped as AppResult.Failure(NetworkException.Serialization), so every generated feature module shows its error state once a real backend is set. Verified in generated out/lang data/orders/.../OrdersRepository.kt; the template's own SampleDto.kt is @Serializable. CI does not catch it because the scaffolded tests use a fake repository.

template/.gitignore:30 ('/*.json') ignores generator-spec.json; verified with git check-ignore on a generated project ('.gitignore:30:/*.json generator-spec.json'). record.py:5-6 says the file 'is meant to be committed', and readme.py:140-141 tells users it is 'safe to commit' and to use it for regenerate-and-compare. With --git (render.py:555 'git add .') the initial commit leaves it out, and a normal 'git add .' does too, so the record is lost on clone.
adopt: Port the Kyant backdrop liquid glass from PeriFlow as an optional generator feature 'liquidglass'. Own core/designsystem foundation/Glass.kt, foundation/LiquidInteraction.kt, foundation/ProgressiveBlur.kt, component/navigation/GlassBottomBar.kt and component/navigation/GlassRail.kt (periflow-android/core/designsystem/src/main/kotlin/com/jorwen/periflow/core/designsystem/...). Fence the TOML entries kyant-backdrop/kyant-shapes (periflow-android/gradle/libs.versions.toml:43-44,78-79) and the designsystem dependency (core/designsystem/build.gradle.kts:26) with <opt:liquidglass>. Keep the isRenderEffectSupported() fallback (Glass.kt:149, GlassBottomBar.kt:102).

Add a block-level else marker to strip_markers (e.g. // <opt-else:x> with //~ prefixed lines). Call sites like PeriFlow's AppNavigationRail.kt:51 (LiquidGlassRail) need a multi-line glass-off body without the drift-prone variants/ whole-file copies.

Turn the scratch checkers into generator tests: /home/crazyhusir/Documents/projects/tools/.overhaul/scratch-gen/check.py (static consistency: includes, imports, dangling symbols, libs aliases, convention plugins, manifest, resources, translations, unused imports), hilt.py (binding graph) and markers.py (template marker balance and unknown names). Run them over the presets plus the tools/feature_combinations.py sets in tests/test_consistency.py; it takes about 20 s with no Gradle.
Replace genkit/render.py:115-126 rename() with a single-pass alternation regex applied before strip_markers, and move scaffold.write_feature_modules after rewrite_all (genkit/build.py:47-49).
Fix genkit/icons.py:164 to r"\g<1>@drawable/ic_launcher_monochrome\g<2>". VitFleet's committed app/src/main/res/mipmap-anydpi-v26/ic_launcher.xml shows the intended output.
Share one reserved-identifier set (Kotlin hard keywords + Java keywords/literals) between validate_package_name and validate_module_name (genkit/spec.py:917-947), replacing Python's keyword module.
Write keystore.properties with \uXXXX escapes (genkit/render.py:425) and pass keytool passwords via -storepass:env/-keypass:env (render.py:485-496).

Split genkit into core / android adapter / brand modules, with template-declared <generated:…> substitution points instead of regexes over AppRoot.kt, Palette.kt, AppColors.kt and AppFonts.kt. This prepares for the Compose Multiplatform and SwiftUI targets.

Extend the CI Gradle matrix (.github/workflows/ci.yml:84) with the standard preset (the website default), a no-modules/no-screens spec, and analytics+flags with firebase off, so the variants/firebase-off files actually compile.

result.summary:
The template's build system is good at its core. It has real convention plugins, configuration and build cache on, non-transitive R, one version catalogue, build-time module-tier enforcement, unit tests only on devDebug, and R8 full mode with resource shrinking. The Compose compiler is already optimal for Kotlin 2.4.20: strong skipping, IntrinsicRemember, OptimizeNonSkippingGroups and PausableComposition are all on by default.

Four kinds of problems remain.

1. Broken or misleading wiring. The baseline-profile feature cannot generate a profile for the 4-flavour app; PeriFlow's commit 11e50cd says "The benchmark module never ran". Even if it did, the profile would not reach prod or playstore, because mergeIntoMain is not set. Dependency analysis is configured to fail the build, while the generated README says it only prints, and nothing runs it. Crashlytics uploads mapping files on every release build; VitFleet already fixed this.

2. APK weight nobody asked for, measured on the PeriFlow and VitFleet release APKs:
   - No localeFilters: 83 unused locales are 35% of VitFleet's resource entries.
   - ABI splits produce 5 APKs to save about 50 KB, since all native code totals 69 KB.
   - push forces all of Firebase. Analytics measurement alone is about 666 KB of dex and brings AD_ID and AdServices permissions.
   - Lottie and biometric each pull in appcompat (about 190 KB of dex). Biometric also pulls fragment 1.2.5 from 2020.

3. Build-time waste from conventions that assume every module needs everything. Hilt-testing and kspTest run with zero Hilt tests. androidTest Compose dependencies are added with zero androidTest sources. includeAndroidResources is on everywhere, though only one module uses Robolectric. A dead :core:model, plus unused Coil and lifecycle dependencies, are injected into every feature. Guard tasks have no outputs, so they re-run on every build. :core:network depends on the Compose :core:devtools, which puts the 10 kLOC design system on every data module's critical path.

4. AGP 9 hygiene. Five gradle.properties flags are deprecated, redundant, or opt-outs that AGP 10 will enforce. One more line (android.sync.suppressAgpWarnings) exists only to hide the warnings about them. Also: an obsolete ksp.useKSP2, a kotlin-android alias that breaks built-in Kotlin, empty room-ktx and lifecycle-viewmodel-ktx shells, and Room configured through absolute-path KSP args, which breaks build-cache relocation.

Estimated release APK sizes: about 3.3 MB for the 'none' preset, about 4.4 MB for 'standard', and about 7.5 MB for 'everything'. Liquid glass (Kyant backdrop 2.0.1 plus shapes 1.2.1) is cheap at about 19 KB of dex in PeriFlow. It ships no baseline profile or R8 rules, so smooth first frames depend on fixing the app baseline profile and making it walk the glass, navigation and tab paths. A FrameTimingMetric benchmark should be added so FPS can be measured. VitFleet's manifest flag enableOnBackInvokedCallback should be adopted to get predictive back on Android 13–15.

findings.title: Baseline profile cannot be generated for the 4-flavour app and would never reach prod/playstore
findings.evidence: defaultConfig has no missingDimensionStrategy while :app has the 'environment' dimension with 4 flavours (Flavors.kt:9-23). app/build.gradle.kts:105-108 calls baselineProfile(project(":benchmark")) with no mergeIntoMain, and BaselineProfileGenerator.kt:38 targets com.base.app.dev. PeriFlow commit 11e50cd: 'The benchmark module never ran: with no flavour chosen the app's four were ambiguous… the app merges the result into main so every flavour ships it.' No baseline-prof.txt is committed in the template.
findings.recommendation: Add missingDimensionStrategy("environment","dev") to :benchmark, and baselineProfile { mergeIntoMain = true; saveInSrc = true } to :app. Split the generator into a narrow startup rule and a journey rule (tabs, push/pop, scrolling over glass). Use a Gradle Managed Device instead of useConnectedDevices. Add a FrameTimingMetric benchmark.

findings.title: No localeFilters: 83 unused library locales ship in every APK
findings.evidence: aapt2 dump configurations finds 99 locale configs in VitFleet's app-prod-release.apk and 98 in PeriFlow's. In VitFleet, 4,153 of 11,715 resource values (35%) belong to 83 locales the app does not ship; it ships en and hi, and en-rXC (pseudo-locale) is included. resources.arsc is stored uncompressed at 1.86 MB. Only generateLocaleConfig is set.
findings.recommendation: Have the generator emit androidResources { localeFilters += listOf("en", <spec.languages>) }. This is the AGP 9 replacement for resourceConfigurations.

findings.title: push forces all of Firebase, including Analytics measurement (~666 KB dex)
findings.evidence: push requires=('firebase',), and firebase requires=('analytics','flags') at spec.py:169. resolve_features({'push'}) returns ['analytics','firebase','flags','push']. Measured R8 dex in VitFleet: gms.measurement 270 KB + gms.internal.measurement 396 KB, crashlytics 137 KB, sessions 33 KB, messaging 36 KB, remoteconfig 26 KB. FCM only needs firebase-messaging.
findings.recommendation: Split firebase into firebase-core (plugin + json, implied only), push (messaging), crashlytics, firebase-analytics and remote-config. Move AppMessagingService into :core:notification so :app has no Firebase dependencies.

findings.title: Dependency analysis is set to fail, the docs say it only prints, and nothing runs it
findings.evidence: onAny { severity("fail") }. The readme.py _DEPS_NOTE says 'It prints rather than fails', and spec.py:400 says 'Printed on every pull request', but generated projects have no CI. The comment at lines 101-103 promises a design-system api exemption that no config provides. CI runs check, and buildHealth is not hooked into check. The C6/C7 unused dependencies would fail it.
findings.recommendation: Use severity("warn"), or clean the conventions first and then gate. Add buildHealth to the CI 'all' entry. Switch to the com.autonomousapps.build-health settings plugin.

findings.title: Crashlytics uploads mapping files on every release build, including CI
findings.evidence: Applies com.google.firebase.crashlytics with no mappingFileUploadEnabled control. VitFleet commit 2ef1f33 fixed it, with the comment: 'a network call from every local and CI build, and one that cannot succeed with the placeholder google-services.json'. CI's assembleProdRelease runs with Firebase on in the everything and all presets.
findings.recommendation: Port VitFleet's gate: buildTypes.configureEach { configure<CrashlyticsExtension> { mappingFileUploadEnabled = providers.gradleProperty("crashlyticsUpload").orNull.toBoolean() } }

findings.title: Deprecated or redundant gradle.properties flags, with warnings deliberately suppressed
findings.evidence: AGP 9.4.1 BooleanOption.kt: useAndroidX is Deprecated (removal in 10.0, l.555). nonFinalResIds is Deprecated (l.541). enableResourceOptimizations is SoftlyEnforced(9.0) (l.418). nonTransitiveRClass is already the default (l.85). disallowKotlinSourceSets=false is an experimental opt-out enforced in AGP 10 (l.376-382). Line 33 android.sync.suppressAgpWarnings=UNSUPPORTED_PROJECT_OPTION_USE hides those warnings. On line 23, KSP 2.3.12 itself says 'KSP1 is no longer available… ksp.useKSP2 property will be removed'. kotlin.incremental and ksp.incremental are defaults.
findings.recommendation: Delete lines 20, 22, 23 and 25-33 in the template, PeriFlow and VitFleet. Then read the output of --warning-mode all.

findings.title: Room configured through absolute-path KSP args, which breaks build-cache relocation
findings.evidence: arg("room.schemaLocation", "${projectDir}/schemas") puts an absolute path into the KSP task inputs, and the schema output is undeclared. Line 21 also adds androidx-room-ktx, whose 2.8.5 classes.jar contains only META-INF/androidx.room_room-ktx.version.
findings.recommendation: Apply the androidx.room Gradle plugin with room { schemaDirectory("$projectDir/schemas") } and drop the room-ktx dependency.

findings.title: ABI splits produce 5 APKs per release to save ~50 KB, and outputs depend on task names
findings.evidence: All native code is libandroidx.graphics.path.so plus libdatastore_shared_counter.so, 69 KB across 4 ABIs. PeriFlow's split APKs are 8.81 MB against 8.91 MB universal. Splits switch on when a task name contains 'Release', so PeriFlow's dev/benchmarkRelease has 5 APKs while VitFleet's has 1. 32-bit x86 is still included. CI's assembleProdRelease packages 5 APKs per matrix entry.
findings.recommendation: Delete configureAbiSplits and ReleaseArtifacts.kt (dist tasks). Play serves per-ABI from the AAB.

findings.title: Lottie and biometric pull in appcompat; biometric also pulls fragment 1.2.5 (2020)
findings.evidence: lottie-6.7.1.pom depends on appcompat 1.6.1. biometric-1.1.0.pom depends on fragment 1.2.5 (compile) and appcompat 1.2.0 (runtime). androidx.appcompat is 190 and 191 KB of dex in PeriFlow and VitFleet, with 459 appcompat.widget seeds in VitFleet. LockActivity.kt:19 uses FragmentActivity, which arrives only transitively at 1.2.5. VitFleet pinned fragment 1.9.1 with the comment 'biometric alone would pull fragment 1.2.5 from 2020'.
findings.recommendation: Declare androidx.fragment explicitly and move applock into :core:applock, as VitFleet did. Take lottie out of the everything preset, or offer a Compose-native renderer.

findings.title: Firebase Analytics merges AD_ID and AdServices permissions
findings.evidence: Both apps' merged release manifests contain com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID, ACCESS_ADSERVICES_AD_ID and ACCESS_ADSERVICES_ATTRIBUTION; PeriFlow also has ACCESS_ADSERVICES_TOPICS and READ_GSERVICES. The template removes none.
findings.recommendation: In the firebase-analytics feature, add tools:node="remove" for these permissions and google_analytics_adid_collection_enabled=false unless the app serves ads.

findings.title: Dead :core:model module is wired into every data and feature module
findings.evidence: grep finds com.base.app.core.model only in core/model itself (Paged.kt and its test). It is still wired as api(":core:model") in the data convention and as implementation in the feature convention (AndroidFeatureConventionPlugin.kt:18). core/model/build.gradle.kts:3,7 applies the serialization plugin and json, with no @Serializable.
findings.recommendation: Delete it, or make it the real JVM home for shared domain types. Either way, remove it from the conventions.

findings.title: Conventions inject dependencies and plugins the modules never use
findings.evidence: coil-compose is in every feature, but no feature imports coil3. lifecycle-runtime-compose (l.25) is unused in features. core:coroutines (l.22) is used only by settings. serialization-json (l.24): features use core only. Data convention l.21-22 adds coroutines and datastore to modules that do not import them. The serialization plugin and json are unused in core/datastore:4,16 and core/notification:4,17. The Hilt plugin is applied in core/ui:4 with no DI. app:90 lifecycle-process is unused (no ProcessLifecycleOwner). app:101 coil-compose is unused. benchmark:40 espresso is unused.
findings.recommendation: Reduce the conventions to the true minimum and let modules declare the rest. Make coil-network-okhttp runtimeOnly.

findings.title: Test plumbing added to every module: zero Hilt tests, zero androidTest sources
findings.evidence: There are 0 @HiltAndroidTest and no src/androidTest anywhere, and only 12 of ~28 modules have src/test. Yet testImplementation(hilt-testing) and kspTest(hilt-compiler) go into every Hilt module. Compose.kt:59,69-70 adds androidTest compose deps and ui-test-manifest. AndroidCommon.kt:53-56 and JvmLibrary:27-29 set failOnNoDiscoveredTests=false only to tolerate the empty test tasks.
findings.recommendation: Enable hostTests and deviceTests per module from file("src/test") and file("src/androidTest") existence (DeviceTestBuilder API). Add test dependencies only when the module has tests. Move hilt-testing to the modules that use it.

findings.title: includeAndroidResources is on for unit tests everywhere, though only one module uses Robolectric
findings.evidence: isIncludeAndroidResources = true is set globally. Only core/database uses Robolectric (AppDatabaseMigrationTest.kt:14,19), and it re-sets the flag itself at core/database/build.gradle.kts:15.
findings.recommendation: Default it to false and let Robolectric modules opt in.

findings.title: Guard tasks declare no outputs, so they re-run on every build and are never cached
findings.evidence: VerifyComposeUsageTask (wired to preBuild at Compose.kt:97), VerifyModuleDependenciesTask (ModuleGraph.kt:81-114, preBuild at :50-51) and CheckComposeStabilityTask (ComposeStability.kt:116) declare inputs only. Gradle never treats a task without outputs as up to date, so every assembleDevDebug re-reads all Kotlin sources in every module.
findings.recommendation: Add an @OutputFile marker written on success, and mark the tasks @CacheableTask.

findings.title: :core:network depends on the Compose :core:devtools, chaining all data modules behind the design system
findings.evidence: Network imports only DevToolsLog and NetworkExchange (116 LOC, non-UI; NetworkRecording.kt:3-4, HttpClientModule.kt:9). core/devtools applies Compose and depends on :core:designsystem (64 files, ~10 kLOC). devtools is on by default.
findings.recommendation: Move the log and model types into a non-UI :core:devtools:log module, or declare a NetworkRecorder interface in network and bind it from :app.

findings.title: No predictive-back opt-in, so Android 13–15 get no system back animation
findings.evidence: The <application> tag has no android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback. VitFleet commit 00baeaf ('smooth push, pop, back gesture and tab switches… predictive back is enabled on Android 13 – 15') added it at VitFleet manifest line 17.
findings.recommendation: Add android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="true" to the template's <application>.

findings.title: Four flavours where prod and playstore differ only by signing key; 15 app variants with baselineprofile
findings.evidence: The PLAYSTORE KDoc says 'Identical to [PROD] in every respect except the key it is signed with.' Both have no id suffix. The baselineprofile plugin adds benchmarkRelease and nonMinifiedRelease per flavour, as VitFleet's outputs show for all 4 flavours: 7 + 8 = 15 variants.
findings.recommendation: Keep dev, staging and prod, and select the release key with -PreleaseKey. Adopt PeriFlow and VitFleet's gradleProperty URL overrides, with the WS URL derived from the API URL.

findings.title: R8 app rules repeat library rules, and the AppNavKey -keep is broader than needed
findings.evidence: Lines 24-28 repeat the rules bundled in kotlinx-serialization-core-jvm-1.11.0.jar (META-INF/com.android.tools/r8/*.pro). Lines 32-35 repeat AGP's proguard-common.txt. Lines 49-51 repeat OkHttp's own rules. Nav keys are registered statically via subclass(X::class, X.serializer()) (NavKeySerialization.kt:13-27), so their class names need not be kept. VitFleet seeds.txt: 1,273 of 1,593 kept app members are Companion/serializer members.
findings.recommendation: Reduce to -keepattributes SourceFile,LineNumberTable, -renamesourcefileattribute and the Play dontwarn. Verify with a release process-death test. Put any genuinely needed nav rule in core/navigation consumer rules.

findings.title: dist tasks share one output directory, and the docs claim the bundle is included
findings.evidence: Both dist<V>Apks and dist<V>Bundle write outputs/dist/<variant> (l.48, 57). The APK task runs deleteRecursively() on it, and the bundle task appends to checksums (l.186-189). dist<V> depends only on the APK task (l.60-65), yet docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:637 says it 'copies every APK and the bundle'.
findings.recommendation: Delete along with ABI splits, or give each task its own directory and fix the doc.

findings.title: Compose stability check forces reports on every compile of designsystem and core:ui
findings.evidence: reportsDestination is set unconditionally for the two largest Compose modules when composemetrics is on. gradle.properties:35-36 says reports are left off 'because it costs ~15% build time'.
findings.recommendation: Enable reports only when check/recordComposeStability is requested, or behind -PcomposeReports.

findings.title: kotlin-android plugin alias in the catalogue, unusable under AGP 9 built-in Kotlin, plus other unused aliases
findings.evidence: kotlin-android is unused; the conventions rely on AGP built-in Kotlin (AndroidCommon.kt:67-72). Also unused: androidx-lifecycle-runtime-ktx (77), work-testing (136), paging-testing (149), test-core (166), test-rules (168), mockk-android (176). lifecycle-viewmodel-ktx (used at core/common:17) is an empty 2.11.0 shell. Feature-owned aliases are not fenced with opt markers.
findings.recommendation: Delete the unused aliases and fence feature-owned aliases with # <opt:x>.

findings.title: META-INF/*.version stripped from debug builds, which affects Layout Inspector
findings.evidence: excludes += "/META-INF/*.version" applies to every variant. Android Studio's inspector reads androidx.compose.ui_ui.version to detect Compose.
findings.recommendation: Apply the exclude to release variants only, via androidComponents.onVariants.

findings.title: Library modules with no resources still run Android resource processing
findings.evidence: 14 modules have no src/main/res: core analytics, coroutines, database, datastore, devtools, flags, navigation, network, testing, and all 5 data modules. The AGP API LibraryAndroidResources.enable exists (LibraryAndroidResources.kt:25).
findings.recommendation: Set androidResources.enable = file("src/main/res").exists() in the library convention.

findings.title: Benchmark module hard-codes SDK levels the generator never rewrites
findings.evidence: compileSdk = 37, targetSdk = 37 and Java 17 are set inline. render.apply_build_settings rewrites only AppConfig.kt (render.py:284-308).
findings.recommendation: Add a small android.test convention that reads AppConfig, or use AGP's settings-level compileSdk/minSdk.

findings.title: CI never builds the minSdk<26 desugaring path, never runs buildHealth, and keeps no reports
findings.evidence: The generated spec always uses default SDKs, so spec_minimal.json (min 24, target 36) is only in the manual AGENTS steps. There is no buildHealth step, no upload-artifact of build/reports, and ABI splits run in assembleProdRelease. JDK 17 blocks Robolectric SDK 36+ (AppDatabaseMigrationTest.kt:86).
findings.recommendation: Run 'none' with min_sdk 24 and target_sdk 36. Add buildHealth to the 'all' entry, upload reports on failure, and consider JDK 21.

findings.title: Repository content filtering applies to plugins only
findings.evidence: pluginManagement filters google() by group (l.16-22); dependencyResolutionManagement's google() (l.31) does not.
findings.recommendation: Copy the same content { includeGroupByRegex } block to dependencyResolutionManagement.

findings.title: Stability config lists kotlinx.collections.immutable, which the compiler already knows and the project lacks
findings.evidence: KnownStableConstructs in compose compiler 2.4.20 already includes ImmutableList and PersistentList. The library is absent from the catalogue, yet ComposeStability.kt:164-166 tells users to use PersistentList.
findings.recommendation: Add kotlinx-collections-immutable to the catalogue (api in designsystem) and drop the redundant conf line.

findings.title: getDefaultProguardFile comment is false; release block duplicated in catalog
findings.evidence: The comment claims it is only reachable from a build script, but CommonExtension.getDefaultProguardFile exists (AGP API CommonExtension.kt:533). catalog/build.gradle.kts:19-26 repeats the block, and :14-15 re-sets versionCode/Name. AndroidCommon.kt:22 useSupportLibrary and AndroidLibraryConventionPlugin.kt:24 isMinifyEnabled=false are no-ops. ModuleTier.APP is unreachable.
findings.recommendation: Move the proguard config into the application convention and delete the no-ops and dead branches.

findings.title: Heap sizes oversized for a 15 GB machine and for CI
findings.evidence: -Xmx6144m plus metaspace 1536m, and kotlin.daemon -Xmx3072m, for about 10.5 GB in total.
findings.recommendation: Start at -Xmx4g and a 2g Kotlin daemon, then measure with --scan.

result.summary: I audited all of template/core/designsystem (about 10,030 LOC) and template/core/ui file by file, and diffed each file against PeriFlow and VitFleet. Framework behaviour was checked against the foundation 1.12.1 sources, and the glass claims against the Kyant backdrop 2.0.1 sources. The "unnecessary ripple" the user hates comes from AppTheme, which provides a grey full-bounds AppIndication overlay as the global LocalIndication. Every appClickable uses it, and so does every implicit selectable/toggleable overload, which covers bottom-bar and rail items, tabs, segments, and checkbox/radio/switch rows. Filled buttons stack three press effects: scale, a pressed-colour crossfade and the overlay. The floating bottom bar is an opaque Material-style card. Screen content never scrolls under it (the nav host pads root screens by the bar's full height), its selected pill is 1.15:1 against the surface, and its pill, icon scale and colour animations read state during composition. So the bar recomposes every frame of every tab switch, which feeds the "pushy" feel. The template has no liquid glass. PeriFlow's Kyant implementation teaches the right lessons: content glass is drawn rather than sampled, there is one scene recording, and the lens at rest samples only the tab layer. It still needs fixes before porting: coroutines launched per pointer event and per animation frame, composed {}, the tab row composed twice, and no fallback for battery saver, thermal throttling or low-RAM devices. The report gives an opt-in `glass` feature design with a GlassPolicy. Motion mixes springs and tweens without semantics: the sheet spring with a hard-coded stiffness drives indicators and switch thumbs, tracking() is dead, and quick taps "pop" instead of dipping. PeriFlow already fixed the quick-tap problem with a Modifier.Node. Several functional bugs are confirmed, most of them still present in both apps. AppWheelPicker captures its value and callback stale, so the time picker resets the minutes when you change the hour. A stepped AppSlider cannot be dragged slowly, and touching it to scroll sets its value. AppPullToRefresh reads isRefreshing stale and can trigger a second refresh. AppCurrencyField's caret drifts: typing 1234567 shows 12,345.76. Back closes AppBottomSheet with no animation. The AppTopBar title runs under a second action. The dark-mode skeleton shimmer is invisible. AppTooltip's pop never plays. Tapping an open swipe row activates it. MessageHost is not lifecycle-aware. On accessibility, unchecked controls and field outlines are 1.1–1.7:1 and white on the dark danger colour is 3.08:1. Icon buttons are 36–44dp and a chip's remove target is 15dp. Text-field labels are outside the field's semantics, and focusRing is never used. At least 2,681 LOC of components ship in every generated app but are used only by the catalog, and there is dead code plus several inaccurate comments. The full report has per-component iOS-polish verdicts, a missing-components list, a port-back table from PeriFlow and VitFleet, and code sketches for the PressFeedback node, SwiftUI-style spring tokens, the deferred-read bottom bar, GlassPolicy and the wheel and slider fixes.

findings.title: Global grey AppIndication overlay on every touchable (the 'unnecessary ripple')
findings.evidence: `val indication = remember(resolved) { AppIndication(resolved.contentPrimary) }` then `LocalIndication provides indication` (:87). AppIndication draws a full-bounds rect at 0.09 alpha (foundation/AppIndication.kt:74-83). It is used by appClickable (Modifiers.kt:127), and implicitly by `selectable(selected, role, onClick)` in AppBottomBar.kt:264-268, AppTabRow.kt:68-72 and AppSegmentedControl.kt:87-92, and by toggleable/selectable in AppSelection.kt:65,149,213. foundation 1.12.1 Selectable.kt:83 confirms that this overload reads LocalIndication.current.
findings.recommendation: Provide a no-op indication by default. Add an explicit PressFeedback {None, Scale, Dim, Highlight} on a single Modifier.Node-based `pressable`. Use Highlight only for list, menu and action-sheet rows, and pass `indication = null` for bars, tabs, segments and selection rows.

findings.title: Filled buttons stack three press effects (scale + colour crossfade + overlay)
findings.evidence: `animateColorAsState(if (pressed) style.containerPressed else style.container)` is passed into AppClickableSurface, which also applies `pressScale` and `appClickable` with LocalIndication (foundation/AppSurface.kt:87-100). Primary goes accent→accentPressed, gets a 9% contentPrimary film, and scales to 0.96 with an overshoot.
findings.recommendation: Use one effect per component: Scale for filled buttons and Dim for text, ghost and icon buttons. Drop the overlay. If a pressed fill remains, draw it in the draw phase.

findings.title: Press scale pops instead of dipping on quick taps; composable modifier factory
findings.evidence: Release immediately runs `scale.animateTo(motion.pressOvershoot, motion.pressPop())`. In scroll containers, Press and Release arrive together for quick taps, so the control grows to 1.02–1.045 and never dips. Each instance costs `remember { Animatable }` + LaunchedEffect + graphicsLayer (:22-63). PeriFlow fixed this with PressBounceNode, which finishes the dip first (PF foundation/PressBounce.kt:92-100).
findings.recommendation: Port PeriFlow's PressBounceNode (Modifier.Node, LayoutModifierNode, read only in placeWithLayer). Replace pressPop with an under-damped release() spring and add compactPressScale.

findings.title: Every tap buzzes by default
findings.evidence: `haptic: HapticEffect? = HapticEffect.Tap` and the comment "Every control gets a haptic by default". Tap maps to KEYBOARD_TAP (AppHaptics.kt:61). iOS reserves haptics for toggles, selection, detents and outcomes.
findings.recommendation: Default to haptic = null. Keep Select, Toggle, Tick, Threshold and Confirm on the specific controls.

findings.title: Floating bottom bar is an opaque card that content never scrolls under
findings.evidence: FloatingBar is `AppSurface(shape = pill, elevation = overlay)` with a solid surface. NAV/AppNavHost.kt:162 pads root entries by occupiedHeight (64 + 24dp + nav bar). The selected pill is accentSubtle on white at 1.15:1. The pill uses the sheet spring (:164; damping 0.68 in Bouncy), edge icons scale on the press spring (:255-259; damping 0.42 in Bouncy), and the selectedIcon filled-glyph promise (:47-51) is unfulfilled because the icon set has no filled variants.
findings.recommendation: Use LocalBottomBarInset so root screens draw under the bar and only scrolling content pads. Make the bar translucent or glass, use a no-bounce 'selection' spring for the pill, add filled tab icons, and use a short tween for show and hide as PeriFlow does.

findings.title: Bottom bar and rail recompose every frame of a tab switch
findings.evidence: `.offset(x = x)` with `val x by animateDpAsState` (:162-169, also :185 and AppNavigationRail.kt:95,111). `Modifier.scale(iconScale)` (:284). tint, labelTint and pill come from animateColorAsState and are passed as Color into AppIcon and AppText (:229-252). All are read in composition while NavDisplay animates the incoming screen.
findings.recommendation: Read animated values only inside offset {}, graphicsLayer {} and drawBehind {}. Add ColorProducer overloads to AppText and AppIcon and pass `{ tint.value }`.

findings.title: No liquid glass in the template; PeriFlow's version needs perf fixes before porting
findings.evidence: BarTreatment has only Docked, Floating, Minimal and Chunky. PeriFlow problems: LiquidInteraction.kt:178-183 launches a coroutine per drag event, :198-202 launches one per animation frame, :249 and GlassBottomBar.kt:155 snapTo in launch per move, Glass.kt:137 uses `composed {}`, GlassBottomBar.kt:224-239 composes the tab row twice, and there is no battery-saver, thermal or low-RAM fallback. Every Kyant drawBackdrop is an Offscreen layer (DrawBackdropModifier.kt:257), which confirms PeriFlow's choice of drawn content glass.
findings.recommendation: Add an optional `glass` generator feature (Kyant backdrop 2.0.1 + shapes 1.2.1), orthogonal to design_style. Include GlassStage, a GlassPolicy (Live on API 31+, lens on 33+, Frosted under saver, thermal or low-RAM, user 'Reduce transparency'), drawn content glass cached with drawWithCache, and a single drag coroutine. Gate it with Macrobenchmark FrameTimingMetric.

findings.title: AppWheelPicker settle collector captures value and callback stale; time picker resets minutes
findings.evidence: `LaunchedEffect(listState, items, placed) { snapshotFlow{...}.collect { (scrolling, index) -> if (!scrolling && index != selectedIndex) onSelectedChange(index) } }`. selectedIndex and onSelectedChange are frozen at launch. AppTimePicker.kt:260,275,286 passes lambdas closing over minuteIndex and periodIndex, so changing the hour after the minutes re-emits the initial minutes. The code is identical in PeriFlow and VitFleet.
findings.recommendation: Read both through rememberUpdatedState inside the collector, and key the centeredIndex derivedStateOf on items.

findings.title: AppSlider: stepped drag is stuck, and touch-to-scroll sets the value
findings.evidence: `emitFraction(fraction + delta / travel)` uses the last composed and snapped fraction, so deltas below half a step never accumulate. `detectTapGestures(onPress = { emit(it.x) })` (:129-131) fires on down: TapGestureDetector.kt:132-136 consumes the down and calls onPress immediately.
findings.recommendation: Mirror AppRangeSlider: track the absolute pointer position in awaitEachGesture, snap only on output, and commit a tap on up or after touch slop.

findings.title: AppPullToRefresh reads isRefreshing stale and launches a coroutine per scroll event
findings.evidence: `remember(thresholdPx, maxPullPx) { object : NestedScrollConnection {... isRefreshing ...} }` (:66,76) means a pull during a refresh calls onRefresh again. `scope.launch { offset.snapTo(...) }` runs per event (:57,68). onPreFling suspends the fling on `offset.animateTo(restingPx)` (:79). `offset.value` is read in composition (:98-99).
findings.recommendation: Port VitFleet's version: rememberUpdatedState(isRefreshing), mutableFloatStateOf while dragging with Animatable only to settle, content follows the pull, and a minimum acknowledgement.

findings.title: AppCurrencyField caret drifts when a grouping comma appears
findings.evidence: `value = formatMinorUnits(minorUnits, fractionDigits)` in a String BasicTextField. foundation BasicTextField.kt:819-823 keeps the old selection via `textFieldValueState.copy(text = value)`. A simulation of typing 1234567 gives '12,345.76'. The placeholder never shows because the value is never empty.
findings.recommendation: Use the TextFieldState API with an OutputTransformation for grouping (store raw digits), or the TextFieldValue overload with the selection forced to the end.

findings.title: AppBottomSheet: Back skips the exit animation, double dismiss, recomposes every frame
findings.evidence: `Dialog(onDismissRequest = onDismissRequest, ...)` so Back removes the sheet instantly, while the drag and scrim paths animate (:68-76). dismiss() can run twice. `progress` is computed from `offsetY.value` in composition (:81-85). The dismiss tween ignores fling velocity. There is no nested scroll and there are no detents.
findings.recommendation: Route Back through an idempotent animated dismiss, compute progress inside graphicsLayer, and use a velocity-aware spring. Merge VitFleet's nested-scroll and IME insets with PeriFlow's AppDetentSheet hoisted state and detents.

findings.title: AppTopBar title runs under a second action
findings.evidence: `val titleEnd = edge + slot` reserves one 44dp slot, and the title Column is an overlay independent of the actions Row (:83-108). VitFleet fixed it, with the comment "The title takes what the icons leave".
findings.recommendation: Lay the non-centred title out in the Row with weight(1f). For a centred title, reserve max(start, end) slot widths. Add a scroll-linked large-title collapse and scroll-edge fade.

findings.title: Dark-mode skeleton shimmer is invisible but still allocates a brush every frame
findings.evidence: In dark, highlight = surfaceVariant = Ink700 and base = skeleton = Ink700 (AppColors.kt:115,151). `progress` is read inside the drawWithCache cache block (:58-69), so the cache invalidates every frame and builds a new Brush. Each skeleton owns its own InfiniteTransition (:43-52).
findings.recommendation: Add a skeletonHighlight token. Build the brush once and translate it in onDrawBehind. Share one shimmer timeline through a CompositionLocal and respect reduce motion.

findings.title: AppSwipeToAction: tapping an open row activates it (comment says otherwise); RTL broken; no a11y actions
findings.evidence: The close-on-tap clickable is on the parent (:161-168), and a clickable child consumes the up first. Actions use Arrangement.End (:92), which mirrors in RTL, but translationX and `coerceIn(-revealPx, 0f)` (:130) do not. There are no customActions semantics. snapTo runs in a launch per drag event (:126-132).
findings.recommendation: Intercept taps in PointerEventPass.Initial while the row is open. Mirror the offset for RTL. Expose semantics customActions. Track the drag in mutable state and settle with a spring carrying velocity.

findings.title: MessageHost consumes a Channel outside the lifecycle; messages are lost in background
findings.evidence: `LaunchedEffect(messages) { messages.collect { current = it } }` on `_messages.receiveAsFlow()` (core/common MviViewModel.kt:46-47). MviScreen uses repeatOnLifecycle for effects but not for messages.
findings.recommendation: Collect with repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED). Add a queue, swipe-to-dismiss and a content transition between messages.

findings.title: Motion tokens are incoherent: sheet spring reused for indicators, hard-coded stiffness, dead tracking(), tween spatial moves
findings.evidence: `spring(dampingRatio = sheetDamping, stiffness = 460f)` is the same for every style. sheet() drives the bar, rail and tab pills, switch thumbs, segment pill, pager dots, accordion chevron, dialog and menu. tracking() (:149-150) has no callers. Sheet dismiss, snackbar, FAB, accordion and month slide use tweens. STAGGER_OFFSET_PX is in px (AppTransitions.kt:136).
findings.recommendation: Use SwiftUI-style precomputed specs: stiffness = (2π/duration)², damping = 1 − bounce. Tokens: press, release, selection, spatial, emphasis per style. Keep tweens for colour and opacity only.

findings.title: Animated values read in composition across overlays and fields; OTP caret keeps the frame clock alive
findings.evidence: rememberInfiniteTransition always runs, and `.alpha(caretAlpha)` (:175) recomposes at frame rate while focused. Also: AppDialog.kt:81-82 and AppDropdownMenu.kt:63-64 use `.scale(scale).alpha(alpha)`, AppListPieces.kt:95 uses `.rotate(rotation)`, busyOverlay uses `.alpha(alpha)` (AppTransitions.kt:244), AppSwipeToAction.kt:161 checks `offset.value != 0f`, and AppButton.kt:114 reads the shadow sink.
findings.recommendation: Move reads into graphicsLayer, offset or draw lambdas. Create the caret transition only in the focused, next-box branch. Use derivedStateOf for boolean thresholds.

findings.title: AppText/AppIcon cannot defer colour; no autoSize
findings.evidence: Only `color: Color`, with a new merged TextStyle on every recomposition (resolve(), :73-91). AppIcon allocates ColorFilter.tint each recomposition, and its clearAndSetSemantics when contentDescription is null is redundant (AppIcon.kt:31). Both apps independently added `autoSize: TextAutoSize?`.
findings.recommendation: Add ColorProducer overloads (BasicText supports them) and a `tint: () -> Color` icon variant. Add autoSize.

findings.title: Contrast failures: white on dark danger and success, non-text controls under 3:1, accent-as-text unchecked
findings.evidence: `content = Color.White` on DangerDark #F0666D is 3.08:1. AppBadge.kt:37 has the same white on danger. AppListPieces.kt:279 has a white check on SuccessDark at 1.89:1. borderStrong ring on white is 1.53:1 (AppSelection.kt:52,138), field border is 1.25:1, and switch off-track is 1.13:1. findings.title: Touch targets below 48dp; chip remove is 15dp nested in the chip
findings.evidence: `AppIcon(Close, size = 15.dp, modifier = Modifier.clickableNoIndication(...))` sits inside a 34dp chip (:58). AppClickableSurface passes `minTouchTarget = 0.dp` (AppSurface.kt:99), so icon buttons are 44/36dp. Segments are 40dp, tabs 46dp, and an unlabeled checkbox or switch is 22dp or 46x28dp.

findings.title: Text-field label and placeholder outside field semantics; settings switches unlabeled
findings.evidence: The label AppText and placeholder are siblings of BasicTextField (:97-126), so TalkBack announces only "Edit box". Settings.kt:270-275 uses `AppListItem(trailing = { AppSwitch(...) })` without a label, which gives an unlabelled 46x28 switch and a separate title node.
findings.recommendation: Move label, placeholder and icons into decorationBox, which also makes the whole container focus the field. Add an AppToggleRow with row-level toggleable(Role.Switch) and merged semantics.

findings.title: focusRing token unused; the only focus cue is a 6% overlay
findings.evidence: `val focusRing: Color` has no usages outside AppColors. AppIndication FOCUSED_ALPHA = 0.06f (AppIndication.kt:84).
findings.recommendation: Add a focus-ring node (an outline in focusRing drawn on FocusInteraction) shared by pressable and text fields.

findings.title: Root screens padded by the full bar height, so floating or glass chrome has nothing behind it
findings.evidence: `.background(AppTheme.colors.background).padding(bottom = inset)` with inset = AppBottomBarDefaults.occupiedHeight() (AppShell.kt:221). PeriFlow switched to `CompositionLocalProvider(LocalBottomBarInset provides inset)` (periflow AppNavHost.kt:161-166).
findings.recommendation: Move LocalBottomBarInset and LocalTopBarInset into the design system. Root screens draw full height and lists add the inset to contentPadding.

findings.title: Catalog-only components ship in every generated app (≥2,681 LOC)
findings.evidence: Used only by catalog/: AppTooltip, AppRangeSlider, AppSlider, all of datetime, AppAnimatedCounter, AppStepIndicator, AppOtpField, all of AppSpecialFields, AppFloatingActionButton, AppSwipeToAction, AppTabRow, AppExpandableText, AppDropdownMenu, plus most of AppDataDisplay and AppListPieces. spec.py owns no designsystem component files.
findings.recommendation: Tier into core components (always) plus generator feature groups (forms, pickers, data, feedback) owned as whole files in spec.py. The catalog requires all of them.

findings.title: Dead APIs and dead slots
findings.evidence: None of these have callers in the template: bounceClick (Modifiers.kt:67), AppResponsiveGrid (AdaptiveLayout.kt:82), staggeredIn (AppTransitions.kt:123), AppMotion.tracking (:149), focusRing, MessagingSurface (MessageHost.kt:54), asStringOrEmpty (UiTextExt.kt:15), AppUserAvatar (AppNetworkImage.kt:46). The AppScaffold bottomBar and floatingAction slots are also unused, and the FAB placement ignores the nav-bar inset and the bar it claims to clear (AppScaffold.kt:71-81).

findings.title: AppNetworkImage uses SubcomposeAsyncImage, and each loading image runs its own shimmer
findings.evidence: `SubcomposeAsyncImage(model = url, ..., loading = { AppSkeleton(...) })`. Coil documents SubcomposeAsyncImage as slow for lazy lists.
findings.recommendation: Use AsyncImage or rememberAsyncImagePainter with painter placeholders and a shared shimmer, plus a crossfade.

findings.title: TypeVoice asks for FontWeight.Black that is never downloaded; cargo-cult includeFontPadding; wrong KDoc

The Bold voice display styles therefore render identically to Neutral. AppTypography.kt:47-48 suppresses the deprecation for includeFontPadding=false, which is the default since Compose 1.5. The KDoc says "Fifteen styles" for 17 fields (AppTypography.kt:13).
findings.recommendation: Add Black to the downloaded weights, or use ExtraBold. Remove the PlatformTextStyle. Fix the comments. Consider aligning the scale with iOS Dynamic Type for the SwiftUI and CMP generators.

findings.title: Fixed heights on text-bearing chrome clip at large font scales
findings.evidence: Fixed heights: `.height(AppTheme.sizes.topBarHeight)` 56dp with title + subtitle; AppBottomBar.kt:118,147 (60/64dp); AppTabRow.kt:53 (46dp); AppSegmentedControl.kt:51 (40dp); rail ItemHeight 68dp; wheel items 40dp. findings.recommendation: Use heightIn(min = …) and let the chrome grow, or cap the label scale.

findings.title: Icons: no autoMirror, no filled variants, eager init of 67 vectors
findings.evidence: `ImageVector.Builder(name, 24.dp, 24.dp, 24f, 24f)` with no autoMirror, so ArrowLeft and ChevronLeft are wrong in RTL. StarFilled is the only filled glyph. `object AppIcons` has 67 eager vals plus a catalog-only `all` list (:515).
findings.recommendation: Set autoMirror on directional icons, add filled variants for tab icons, use lazy backing fields, and move `all` to the catalog.

findings.title: AppTooltip pop-in never plays; empty click action exposed to accessibility
findings.evidence: `AnimatedVisibility(visible = true, enter = transitions.popIn, exit = transitions.popOut)` is composed only while visible, so enter never animates and exit never runs. `combinedClickable(onClick = {}, onLongClick = ...)` at :46-53 adds a no-op click action.
findings.recommendation: Use MutableTransitionState(false) with targetState = true. Use pointerInput(detectTapGestures(onLongPress)) plus semantics onLongClick instead of combinedClickable.

findings.title: rememberReduceMotion is read once and never observed
findings.evidence: `remember(context) { Settings.Global.getFloat(..., TRANSITION_ANIMATION_SCALE, 1f) == 0f }` is queried per caller and not updated when the setting changes. The skeleton shimmer and OTP caret ignore it.
findings.recommendation: Provide one observed value (a ContentObserver on ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE) from AppTheme as a CompositionLocal.

findings.title: AppTimeline connector has a fixed 44dp height
findings.evidence: `.height(CONNECTOR_HEIGHT)` with `CONNECTOR_HEIGHT = 44.dp` (:342), independent of the row content height.
findings.recommendation: Draw the connector in the row's drawBehind, or use IntrinsicSize.Min.

result.summary: Tab switches and push/pop feel "glitchy and pushy" in the template for several confirmed reasons. Each tab's NavDisplay sits inside AnimatedContent(selectedIndex), so every tab switch throws away the outgoing tab and rebuilds the incoming one from scratch on the frame of the tap. The same switch cross-fades two full-screen alpha layers: the outgoing tab fades out over 135 ms while the incoming fade-in is delayed 90 ms, so the background shows through by up to 30%. PeriFlow measured this exact code at 12.4% janky frames (p99 117 ms) and got to about 4% (p99 61 ms) by keeping tabs composed and switching instantly. The bottom bar's visibility is tied to stack depth and runs on its own vertical, underdamped sheet spring. It moves perpendicular to the screen slide, starts rising mid-pop, and only returns after a predictive back gesture has finished. Push and pop fade the outgoing screen to alpha 0.72. That renders it offscreen every frame and makes it look pale in the light theme. The slide spring takes about 466 ms to settle although 95% of the movement is done by 238 ms. Predictive back scrubs that same spring, so with the finger 30% across the screen is already 77% of the way out, and the Bouncy style overshoots. A back gesture taken during a push re-targets NavDisplay's running SeekableTransitionState, which the template does not guard against. Other structural causes: the host is called from two layout branches, so a width-class change disposes every tab and clears its ViewModels; content slides over the rail; the sign-in and sign-out hand-off swaps hosts with racy duplicate mechanisms; modal slides overshoot and open a gap at the bottom; and the bar items flash and recompose on every frame. Outside navigation proper, there are high-severity bugs. The app lock can be bypassed by pressing Home on the lock screen and returning within 30 s. MainActivity's standard launch mode plus the singleton channel navigator split navigation commands between two Activity instances after widget, notification or link taps. Deep links are re-applied on every recreation and skip the onboarding and sign-in gates. The Play update flow re-prompts on every resume and restarts without asking. PeriFlow (KeptTabs with per-tab lifecycle and back dispatcher, slide-only push, linear predictive pop, BackHold, LocalBottomBarInset, system bar icons that follow the app theme, chrome-only Kyant glass) and VitFleet (single host call site, FullScreenKey, root-key tab routing, applyWhileStarted plus singleTop, PendingDeepLink) already fixed most of these. PeriFlow still measures and animates hidden tabs, keeps three AppShell branches and ties the bar to stack depth. VitFleet's .underneath() z-index hack is dead under NavDisplay 1.1.7. The report gives a target design with code sketches: KeptTabs v2, a persistent or root-following bar, critically damped slide-only transitions, a single entry-point source, a deep-link pipeline, and lock and system-bar fixes. It also explains how to ship Kyant liquid glass as an opt-in feature that keeps a high frame rate.

findings.title: Every tab switch disposes and rebuilds the incoming tab, and cross-fades two full-screen alpha layers
findings.evidence: AnimatedContent(targetState = state.selectedIndex, transitionSpec = NavTransitions.tabSwitch(motion)) { index -> StackDisplay(entries = tabEntries[index]) } (lines 99-106). The outgoing tab's NavDisplay and screen composition leave composition, and the incoming tab is composed from nothing on the frame of the tap. tabSwitch (NavTransitions.kt:105-113) fades in after a delay of `instant` and fades out over instant+instant/2, so the window shows through by up to 30% at t=90 ms (scratch/tabfade.py), and both tabs render offscreen for alpha. During the 135 ms overlap both NavDisplays register back handlers. PeriFlow commit a8aedb0 measured this exact code: 12.4% janky (p99 117 ms), then about 4% (p99 61 ms) after the fix.
findings.recommendation: Replace it with KeptTabs (PF core/navigation/KeptTabs.kt), including the per-tab TabLifecycle capped at CREATED and a per-tab NavigationEventDispatcher. Make the switch instant and delete NavTransitions.tabSwitch and TAB_ENTER_SCALE. Improvements over PeriFlow: measure only the active tab, provide LocalTabVisible so infinite animations pause, clear focus on switch, and drop kept tabs on resetAll.

findings.title: Bottom bar visibility is tied to stack depth and animates on its own vertical, underdamped spring
findings.evidence: `val onRoot = state.current.size == 1; val showBar = alwaysShowBar || onRoot` (175-176). The AnimatedVisibility enter is slideInVertically(motion.sheet()) { it } + fadeIn (230), and sheet() is spring(sheetDamping 0.86, or 0.68 in Bouncy; AppMotion.kt:54,121,145). On a programmatic pop the stack changes first, so the bar rises while the screen is still leaving. On a predictive pop the stack changes only when the gesture completes (NavDisplay.kt:559-565), so the bar arrives after the screen has gone. PeriFlow dec4ff5 describes it as 'read as the screen arriving twice' and only shortens the tween.
findings.recommendation: Make the bar stay visible at every depth by default (the iOS default), with every entry inset through LocalBottomBarInset. For FullScreenKey destinations (VitFleet), translate the bar with the root entry's horizontal offset in the draw phase (BarAnchor plus graphicsLayer, clipped at the incoming edge) instead of using AnimatedVisibility. Never fade the bar, which matters especially when it is glass.

findings.title: Predictive back scrubs the spring-based pop, so the screen runs ahead of the finger and Bouncy overshoots
findings.evidence: `predictivePopTransitionSpec = { _ -> ... NavTransitions.pop(motion) ... }` (126-129). pop uses motion.navigation(), which is a spring. NavDisplay maps progress linearly onto play time (NAV3 NavDisplay.kt:748-752). Computed: at gesture progress 0.3 the slide is 77% complete (Standard) and 81% (Bouncy, navigationDamping 0.86 at AppMotion.kt:55), and Bouncy overshoots. PeriFlow eb2d1ee: 'a third of the swipe put the screen nine tenths of the way out and it shivered'. Modal entries are also spring-based (metadataFor line 187).
findings.recommendation: Port PeriFlow's NavTransitions.predictivePop (a tween with LinearEasing) and VitFleet's predictivePop with a 0.92-0.94 scaleOut, plus modalPredictiveDismiss. Route them through a predictivePopForStyle used both in metadataFor and in StackDisplay.

findings.title: No guard for a back gesture taken while a push is still settling, so the screen vanishes or snaps
findings.evidence: StackDisplay (109-131) passes the gesture straight to NavDisplay, which calls transitionState.seekTo(progress, previousScene) while animateTo(scene) is running (NAV3 NavDisplay.kt:748-757). The push spring settles in about 466 ms (Standard, scratch/spring_seek.py). PeriFlow 84a9483 and 8943957 report that the new screen 'slid the wrong way, paused and snapped' and that a cancelled swipe re-slid it in.
findings.recommendation: Port PF core/navigation/BackHold.kt (StackMotion, ReportSceneMotion, HoldBackWhileMoving) with BackHoldTest. Shorten the push settle to about 350 ms (critically damped, stiffness around 600-700) so the hold window shrinks.

findings.title: App lock can be bypassed: press Home on the lock screen and return within 30 s
findings.evidence: onHidden() stamps lastVisibleAt from MainActivity.onStop (AppLock.kt:24-26, MainActivity.kt:212-215). Starting the opaque LockActivity stops MainActivity, so the stamp records the moment the lock appeared. LockActivity is noHistory (AndroidManifest.xml:126-132), so Home finishes it. On return, shouldLock() returns false because elapsed < GRACE_MILLIS (lines 29-34). PeriFlow's AppLock locks at once unless the app itself sent the user away (PF app/lock/AppLock.kt:41-54).
findings.recommendation: Add a pendingUnlock flag that is set whenever the lock is shown and cleared only by unlocked(), and check it first in shouldLock(). Adopt PeriFlow's justUnlocked and own-action grace logic. Add a unit test for the Home-on-lock-screen case.

findings.title: Standard launch mode plus a process-singleton channel navigator splits commands between two MainActivity instances
findings.evidence: MainActivity has no launchMode (44-48). Widget taps (widget/AppWidget.kt:69 actionStartActivity<MainActivity>()), notification taps (AppNotifications.kt:105-113 PendingIntent.getActivity) and external links start a new instance. Both instances collect `Channel(BUFFERED).receiveAsFlow()` (AppNavigator.kt:40-41) from LaunchedEffects with no lifecycle gate (AppNavHost.kt:56-58, AppShell.kt:171-173), so each command goes to only one of them. onNewIntent (MainActivity.kt:219-223) never fires in standard mode. VitFleet documents the same failure at VF core/navigation/AppNavigator.kt:66-71.
findings.recommendation: Set android:launchMode="singleTop" (as VitFleet does) and call setIntent in onNewIntent. Collect commands with VitFleet's applyWhileStarted(lifecycle), or scope the navigator to the Activity (ActivityRetained).

findings.title: Deep link is re-applied on every onCreate (rotation, process-death restore, launch from Recents)
findings.evidence: `handleDeepLink(intent)` runs unconditionally in onCreate, so the restored stack gets the linked screen pushed again. VitFleet fixed it at VF MainActivity.kt:164-169 with `savedInstanceState == null && (intent.flags and FLAG_ACTIVITY_LAUNCHED_FROM_HISTORY) == 0`. PeriFlow has the same bug (PF MainActivity.kt:231).
findings.recommendation: Gate on a fresh launch and not from history. Hold links in a PendingDeepLink (VF deeplink/PendingDeepLink.kt and its test) that is consumed once.

findings.title: Deep links skip onboarding and sign-in and land on whichever tab is selected; tab roots are pushed as bar-less copies
findings.evidence: handleDeepLink calls navigator.navigate(key) (225-228) into whatever host exists: OnboardingKey, SignInKey, or the selected tab (AppShell.kt:171-173 applies to state.current). `items` with no id resolves to SampleListKey (DeepLinkResolver.kt:33-35), a tab root, which is then pushed as a non-root entry without the bar or the inset. Sign-in later calls resetTo(start) (AuthNav.kt:44,50) and the link is lost.
findings.recommendation: Hold the link until the tabbed shell is up (VitFleet MainActivity.kt:136-141). Route it with ShellState.apply (VF AppShell.kt:81-99): a root key selects its tab, and other keys select their owning tab through registry metadata before the push.

findings.title: Push and pop fade the outgoing screen, which renders offscreen every frame and turns pale in light theme
findings.evidence: `+ fadeOut(tween(motion.medium), targetAlpha = 1f - motion.outgoingDim)` (30-33), mirrored as fadeIn on pop (43-46), and modal fades at 67-70 and 79-82. The light window background is #F7F8FA (values/colors.xml:4). The 250 ms fade ends long before the roughly 466 ms spring. VitFleet NavTransitions.kt:25-29: 'fading a screen towards the window colour reads as it turning pale'. PeriFlow a8aedb0: 'rendered all of it offscreen each frame for nothing visible'.
findings.recommendation: Use slide only: delete the alpha from push, pop and modal and remove outgoingDim. If depth is wanted, draw a 10 dp edge-shadow gradient in drawBehind on the incoming entry. Move every full-screen slide to a critically damped spring of stiffness around 600-700 (settles in about 350 ms).

findings.title: Modal slide-in uses an underdamped sheet spring, opening a gap at the bottom; Bouncy navigation overshoots against its own rule
findings.evidence: slideInVertically(animationSpec = motion.sheet(), initialOffsetY = { it }) (59-62), where sheet() is spring(sheetDamping, 460f) (AppMotion.kt:145-146). Overshoot is 0.5% for Standard (about 12 px on 2400 px) and 5.4% for Bouncy (about 130 px), so the screen underneath shows below the modal. AppMotion.kt:55 sets Bouncy navigationDamping = 0.86f, although line 123 says 'A long travel with any bounce in it reads as unstable'.
findings.recommendation: Use damping 1 for every full-screen translation (add an AppMotion.screen() spec) and keep bounce for presses, pills and lenses only.

findings.title: The host is called from two layout branches, so a width-class change disposes every tab and clears all their ViewModels
findings.evidence: `if (AppTheme.windowSize.width >= WindowWidth.Medium) { Row { AppNavigationRail; TabbedNavHost(...) }; return@Box }` (195-216), else TabbedNavHost in the Box (218-225). Different call sites are different compositions. On dispose, rememberViewModelStoreProvider calls provider.clearAllKeys() when the lifecycle is >= CREATED (NAV3 RememberViewModelStoreProvider.kt:156-157).
