findings.title: In rail mode, the parallax of push and pop draws content over the navigation rail
findings.evidence: Row(rail, TabbedNavHost.weight(1f)) with no clip (196-213). findings.title: The sign-in and sign-out hand-off swaps hosts with a hard cut and runs two racing mechanisms
findings.evidence: AppRoot branches on tabs.isEmpty() (52-86), and entryPoint() depends on tokenStore.isAuthenticated (MainActivity.kt:123-129, 239-247). If ResetTo lands first, the single stack pushes SampleList (ViewModel #1, request #1), then the branch swap composes it again in the shell (ViewModel #2, request #2) with no transition. The entry identity is derived from the token and settings flows; wrap it in key(identity), as VitFleet's MainActivity.kt:133-160 does, inside a single short crossfade. Remove resetTo from auth and onboarding completion and remove the signedOut collectors from AppRoot. Move Startup into a ViewModel.

findings.title: System bar icons and the splash follow the system night mode, not the in-app theme

findings.title: Bottom inset only on tab roots, applied as raw padding: pushed and single-stack screens sit under the nav bar, IME padding is double-counted, and nothing scrolls under the floating bar

findings.title: Baseline profile and benchmarks never exercise navigation, so first tab switches and pushes run unoptimised

result.summary:
The MVI base (`core/common/mvi/MviViewModel.kt`) is small, but it handles events in a serial queue with a *suspending* `handleEvent`. The reference sample, the generated scaffold and the auth/licences ViewModels all run network I/O inside `handleEvent`. While that runs, Back taps, keystrokes in controlled text fields and Retry all wait until the request returns or times out. VitFleet's 249 `launchLatest` and 113 `launchWork` calls show its authors had to work around this default. The same queue makes the double-submit guard in `FormState.submitting` unreachable, so pressing IME Done twice sends two requests.

The generator's `feature_modules` scaffold is broken at runtime. It decodes JSON into a class with no `@Serializable`, so every load shows "Something went wrong". It also navigates to a detail key it never registers, so the first tap on a row crashes.

`NetworkMonitor` is a cold `callbackFlow`, and the network client calls `.first()` on it for every request. Each call registers a system NetworkCallback; Android caps apps at about 100. VitFleet fixed this with `shareIn` and a Robolectric test. The template also refuses to send any request unless Android marked the network VALIDATED, which breaks on networks where Android's connectivity check is blocked.

The data layer is plain "repository returns `AppResult`". There is no offline-first `Flow` example, `AppResult.Failure` is a bag of eight optional fields, and both real apps had to bolt typed error codes onto it. Profile saves a photo-picker URI without persisting read permission, so the avatar breaks after process death. Profile and all auth forms lose typed input on process death. Settings shows default values for a frame because of a cargo-cult `stateIn(WhileSubscribed)`.

Module boundaries hold in the template but fail at real-app scale. PeriFlow moved cross-feature nav keys into `core:navigation`. VitFleet hand-writes cross-feature link ports in a 292-line `:app` DI module, and dumped 3,679 lines of generated DTOs into `core:model`, which 18 feature modules import directly. I recommend keeping a tightened flat "compact" mode as the default and adding an opt-in "modular" mode (`feature:x:{api,impl}`, `data:x:{api,impl}`, optional `domain:x`) with matching ModuleGraph rules.

Dead code is substantial: `core:model` is imported by nothing, 6 of 8 `AppResult` helpers are unused, 5 of 9 `Validators` are unused (yet translated into 5 languages), `MviTestScope` is unused in all three codebases, `mockk` is an unused `api` dependency, and the Main dispatcher qualifiers are unused. `feature/auth` (991 lines) and `data/auth` have zero tests. Every preset ships the sample features, and PeriFlow deleted all of them by hand.

findings.title: Suspending serial event queue blocks Back/typing/Retry behind I/O in reference code
findings.evidence: init { viewModelScope.launch { for (event in events) { handleEvent(event) ... } } } with `protected abstract suspend fun handleEvent` (line 69). SampleListViewModel.kt:33-48 ("The reference ViewModel") awaits repository.items() inside handleEvent while a controlled AppSearchField(value=state.query) is on screen (SampleListScreen.kt:56-59, AppTextField.kt:127-130) so keystrokes are dropped; SampleDetail.kt:69-86 BackClicked waits behind load(); SignUp.kt:76-81, PasswordReset.kt:74-79, Licenses.kt:68-73 and generator/genkit/scaffold.py:249-269 do the same. VitFleet works around it with 249 launchLatest + 113 launchWork.
findings.recommendation: Make handleEvent non-suspending (Main-thread ordering already gives atomicity) and offer explicit policies: launchLatest(key, debounce), launchExclusive(key) for submit, launch {}. Update sample, scaffold and all template VMs; add a test that Back is handled while a load is in flight.

findings.title: Scaffolded :data:x decodes into a non-@Serializable model; every request fails at runtime
findings.evidence: `networkClient.get<List<{class_name}Item>>(path = ITEMS_PATH)` with `data class {class_name}Item(val id: Int, val title: String)` (lines 131-135) and no @Serializable. The serialization plugin 2.4.20 intrinsic inserts a runtime noCompiledSerializer call (SerializationJvmIrIntrinsicSupport.insertNoCompiledSerializerCall), so it compiles; decodeResult's runCatching (core/network/NetworkClient.kt:45-58) turns it into NetworkException.Serialization. spec_full.json (network + orders/wallet) builds, and tests use fakes, so nothing catches it.
findings.recommendation: Generate remote/{X}Dto.kt (@Serializable) plus a toDomain() mapper like data/sample, and add a generator test asserting @Serializable and decoding a JSON fixture.

findings.title: Scaffolded feature navigates to an unregistered DetailKey and crashes on first row tap
findings.evidence: Route: `is {X}Effect.OpenDetail -> navigator.navigate({X}DetailKey(effect.id))`; the nav module registers only entry<{X}ListKey> (lines 440-442) and its KDoc says "{X}DetailKey has no screen yet" (line 431). AppNavHost.kt:148 calls registry.destinationFor(key), which throws `error("No destination registered ...")` (NavRegistry.kt:85-89).
findings.recommendation: Scaffold a detail screen (VM + route + entry<DetailKey>(pane = NavPane.Detail)), or emit no OpenDetail effect until one exists.

findings.title: Cold NetworkMonitor registers a system NetworkCallback on every request
findings.evidence: `override val isOnline: Flow<Boolean> = callbackFlow { ... registerNetworkCallback(request, callback) ... awaitClose { unregisterNetworkCallback } }.flowOn(ioDispatcher)` is cold. KtorNetworkClient.kt:84,135,166 call `networkMonitor.isOnline.first()` per request, per IO failure and per completion. VitFleet fixed it with shareIn(..., WhileSubscribed(5_000, replayExpirationMillis = 0), replay = 1), noting that "the system allows an app only about a hundred at once", and added ConnectivityNetworkMonitorTest asserting a single registration.
findings.recommendation: Backport the VF shareIn on @ApplicationScope plus its Robolectric test; consider exposing a synchronous current value for pre-flight checks.

findings.title: Requests refused pre-flight unless Android marks the network VALIDATED
findings.evidence: NetworkRequest requires NET_CAPABILITY_VALIDATED (lines 65-68) and the seed uses hasCapability(VALIDATED) (83-86). KtorNetworkClient.kt:84-86: `if (!networkMonitor.isOnline.first()) return unreachable(outgoing, deviceIsOffline = true, ...)` returns without sending. On networks where Android's connectivity probe is blocked (corporate, some VPNs and regions) the app is permanently offline.
findings.recommendation: Never gate requests on the monitor: always attempt, classify IOException, and use the monitor only for UI hints and replay triggers (or gate on NET_CAPABILITY_INTERNET only).

findings.title: FormState.submitting double-submit guard is unreachable; IME Done can send duplicate auth requests
findings.evidence: `if (!canSubmit()) return null; isSubmitting = true; try { block(values()) } finally { isSubmitting = false }`. With the serial queue, a second Submit is only read after `finally` resets isSubmitting. AppButton disables itself while loading (AppButton.kt:120), but KeyboardActions(onDone = { onEvent(Submit) }) in SignIn.kt:195, SignUp.kt:198 and PasswordReset.kt:178 stays live; busyOverlay only consumes pointer events (AppTransitions.kt:237-258).
findings.recommendation: Use launchExclusive("submit") or drop Submit in onEvent while form.isSubmitting; add a VM test that a double Submit sends one request.

findings.title: Profile stores a photo-picker URI without persistable permission; avatar breaks after process death
findings.evidence: `rememberMediaPicker { uris -> uris.firstOrNull()?.let { onEvent(ProfileEvent.PhotoPicked(it.toString())) } }` → ProfileRepository.setPhoto stores the string in DataStore (ProfileRepository.kt:50-52). The PickVisualMedia launcher (MediaPickerController.kt:61-63) never calls takePersistableUriPermission; the OpenDocument launcher at lines 69-83 does, with the comment "Without this the URI is readable until the process dies and then is not".
findings.recommendation: Copy the picked image into app-private storage via core:media and store that path (survives backup and avoids the grant cap); at minimum take persistable permission for image picks.

findings.title: No cross-feature navigation contract: real apps leak keys into core or hand-wire Links in :app
findings.evidence: permits(): FEATURE -> listOf(":core:", ":data:") with no api modules. PeriFlow moved shared keys into core/navigation/Destinations.kt ("A feature may not depend on another feature, so the key lives here ... Registered by :feature:log"). VitFleet hand-implements per-feature XLinks ports in app/di/FeatureBindingsModule.kt (292 lines, 16 providers).
findings.recommendation: Compact mode: a generated shared-destinations file plus a test that every key has exactly one registration. Opt-in modular mode: feature:x:api (NavKeys and contracts, pure Kotlin) and feature:x:impl, with ModuleGraph rules permitting impl → other features' :api only.

findings.title: core:model is dead yet attached to every module; in VitFleet it became a 3.7k-line DTO dump imported by features

VF core/model/api/ApiModels.kt is 3,679 lines of generated DTOs, imported by 18 feature modules (36 places in feature/accounts alone).
findings.recommendation: Remove core:model from the template and conventions, or give it a written charter (cross-domain ids and value types only, never DTOs) enforced by a lint or Konsist test.

findings.title: Typed input lost on process death in Profile and all auth forms; FormState contradicts the 'complete UiState' contract
findings.evidence: ProfileViewModel has no SavedStateHandle although name/bio are edited fields (lines 16-25), contrary to the persistState KDoc "Only for what the user typed" (MviViewModel.kt:96-99). Auth VMs keep fields in a Compose-state FormState with no SavedStateHandle (SignIn.kt:77-80), and routes pass `form = viewModel.form` beside state (SignIn.kt:147), contradicting UiContracts.kt:7-9 ("UiState ... is complete ... no second source of truth"). VF abandoned FormState (0 uses).
findings.recommendation: Fold form fields into UiState with pure validation and persistState, or give FormState a saveIn(SavedStateHandle); add persistState to Profile.

findings.title: AppResult.Failure is an untyped bag of optional fields; both apps re-invented typed errors
findings.evidence: Failure has message, cause, code, fieldErrors, isOffline, rawBody and queued; Success carries fromCache and cachedAtEpochMillis. AuthMessages.kt:12-16 switches on raw 401/429; PF added `errorCode: String?`; VF wrote ApiError.kt parsing rawBody with 35 code constants. AuthRepository.persist (AuthRepository.kt:109-122) calls tokenStore.save, which can throw from KeystoreCipher.encrypt, escaping an AppResult-typed API.
findings.recommendation: Introduce sealed AppError (Offline, Timeout, Http(status, apiCode, fieldErrors, message), Decode, Unexpected) parsed once in core:network's ResponseUnwrapper; move freshness out of the universal result; wrap storage failures in AppResult.

findings.title: Forever-collectors launched in init; cargo-cult stateIn(WhileSubscribed) causes default-value flash in Settings
findings.evidence: `launchWork { settingsStore.settings.stateIn(this, SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(SUBSCRIBE_TIMEOUT_MILLIS), AppSettings()).collect { ... } }`: the only subscriber is the collect itself, so WhileSubscribed never stops, and the initial AppSettings() renders defaults before stored values (switches animate on open). ProfileViewModel.kt:45-51 and SearchViewModel.kt:51 collect DataStore flows for the VM's lifetime; PF TodayViewModel launches 8 such collectors in init.
findings.recommendation: Add a base-class `Flow<T>.observe(stopAfter = 5.s) { reduce }` driven by `_state.subscriptionCount`, and make it the canonical load pattern in sample and scaffold (also removes `init { onEvent(Load) }`).

findings.title: Impl classes and DTOs are public and there is no domain layer; at scale ViewModels absorb business rules on wire DTOs
findings.evidence: `class DefaultSampleRepository` is public, as are DefaultSearchRepository, DefaultFeedRepository and DefaultAuthRepository, and the DTOs SampleDto and FeedPostDto. VF feature/trips/LoadForm.kt is 1,309 lines, with a ViewModel of about 765 lines operating on TripsTripDto (`TripsTripDto.toForm()`, `LoadForm.loadedKl()` pricing/quantity rules); VF feature:daily depends on 5 data modules.

findings.title: Auth flows and data:auth untested; MviTestScope helper unused everywhere; misnamed delay helper in the only MVI test
findings.evidence: feature/auth (991 main lines), data/auth, feature/settings, onboarding and feed have 0 @Test; data/feed tests only nextPage, not load()/getRefreshKey. MviTestScope.test{} has 0 uses in the template, PeriFlow and VitFleet. MviViewModelTest.kt:58 `private suspend fun advanceUntilIdleCompat() = delay(SETTLE_MILLIS)` plus an unused outer SLOW_MILLIS (line 62).
findings.recommendation: Add VM tests for sign-in/up/reset (success writes tokens, 401 message, 422 field errors, single request on double submit), AuthRepository expiry with an injected clock, and Back-during-load. Delete MviTestScope or make the sample use it; use advanceUntilIdle.

findings.title: UiMessage is a data class: an identical message twice is swallowed and dismissed early
findings.evidence: `data class UiMessage(...)`; MessageHost stores it in mutableStateOf<UiMessage?> (MessageHost.kt:24), which uses structural equality, and keys the timeout on LaunchedEffect(current) (line 30). VF wrapped each showing in a non-data `Shown` class ("'Saved' emitted twice is two showings ... it vanished on the first one's").

findings.title: Messages collected without lifecycle awareness; they can time out while the app is stopped
findings.evidence: `LaunchedEffect(messages) { messages.collect { current = it } }`, whereas effects in MviScreen.kt:46-53 use repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED) on Main.immediate.

findings.title: Settings: version piped through LaunchedEffect into a public mutator; magic theme indices in events; dead BackClicked
findings.evidence: `LaunchedEffect(appVersion) { viewModel.setAppVersion(appVersion) }` although SettingsAppInfo is already injectable (SettingsNav.kt:34-40), so the first frame shows an empty version. `ThemeSelected(val index: Int)` maps 0/1/2 in two places (lines 70-75, 128-135). SettingsEvent.BackClicked/NavigateBack (lines 97, 101, 158, 194) is never sent; the screen has no back button.

findings.title: Navigation delayed behind a DataStore fsync
findings.evidence: `is SearchEvent.ResultClicked -> { repository.remember(currentState.query); emitEffect(SearchEffect.OpenResult(event.result.id)) }`: the push waits for DataStore edit (write plus fsync).
findings.recommendation: Emit the navigation effect first, then persist in launchWork.

findings.title: Single shared session DataStore file across domains; AppSettingsStore is a cross-feature god store
findings.evidence: @SessionDataStore (one Preferences file) is used by AuthTokenStore (AuthTokenStore.kt:38), ProfileRepository (line 32) and SearchRepository (line 48), with keys namespaced only by convention ("profile.name", "search.recent"). Every edit rewrites and fsyncs the whole file. feature/settings and feature/onboarding reach into core:datastore's AppSettingsStore directly.
findings.recommendation: One DataStore file per domain, each registered as a SessionScopedStore; move preferences to a data:preferences domain or per-feature files.

findings.title: Convention plugins over-attach dependencies; paging-runtime pulls RecyclerView and LiveData into a Compose app
findings.evidence: Every data module gets api core:common/core:model plus implementation core:coroutines/core:datastore/core:network/serialization-json (lines 19-29), even data:profile (no network) and data:feed/sample (no DataStore); data/auth/build.gradle.kts:10-11 re-adds core:datastore. data/feed/build.gradle.kts:11 `api(libs.androidx.paging.runtime)`, whose 3.5.1 module metadata depends on androidx.recyclerview and lifecycle-livedata-ktx.

findings.title: Dead code in core:common/coroutines/testing and features
findings.evidence: Unused: AppResult flatMap/fold/onSuccess/onFailure/getOrDefault/resultOf (only map and getOrNull are imported); LoadState.isInitialLoading/isTerminal; UiText.Composite/Empty/orUiText; showMessage(String); LONG_DURATION_MILLIS; NoEffect (test only); Validators maxLength/phone/matches/numericRange/none (their strings translated in 5 languages); @MainDispatcher/@MainImmediateDispatcher; mockk api dependency (0 users); search_remove_recent string.

findings.title: i18n: English literal in the data layer, developer message in translatable strings, resolved strings in state
findings.evidence: `title = title.trim().ifBlank { "Untitled" }`; auth_google_not_configured is "... Add the web client id to auth_google_server_client_id." (feature/auth strings.xml:27); SignInEvent.GoogleFailed(val message: String) → UiText.Dynamic (SignIn.kt:61,89).

findings.title: core:common is Android-bound, blocking reuse by the planned CMP/SwiftUI generators
findings.evidence: UiText.resolve(context: Context) with @StringRes ids; AppLogger uses android.util.Log; NetworkMonitor uses ConnectivityManager plus a manifest permission; R.string in AppResultMessages and Validators; api lifecycle-viewmodel-savedstate.

findings.title: Inconsistent file layout and navigation wiring across reference features
findings.evidence: SearchResultRoute calls `navigator::navigateUp` directly in UI, while SampleDetail routes Back through event and effect; SearchRoute takes an onOpenResult lambda while SampleListRoute takes navigator; sample splits Contract/VM/Screen/Routes for the list but uses one file for detail; auth and settings put keys and DI in one *Nav.kt file; SearchResult.kt clashes with data.search.SearchResult; Feed and Profile declare empty effect interfaces instead of NoEffect.

findings.title: Comment quality: false claim, duplicated KDoc, what-comments
findings.evidence: KDoc claims "a validator that returns 'no error' and one that was never run are different things", but ValidationResult has only Valid/Invalid. Onboarding.kt:49-59 has two KDoc blocks around @Immutable. `/** Sign in. */` (SignIn.kt:71), `/** Create an account. */` (SignUp.kt:58). The same 6-line strings.xml header is copied into 4 features.

findings.title: handleEvent runs synchronously inside subclass constructors in production but queued in tests

On Main.immediate, trySend resumes the receiver in place, so handleEvent runs during construction up to its first suspension; MainDispatcherRule uses StandardTestDispatcher (MainDispatcherRule.kt:20-22), which queues instead. A property declared below init would be read uninitialised.

missed: template/core/designsystem/src/main/kotlin/com/base/app/core/designsystem/animation/AppTransitions.kt:248-252 — busyOverlay does not reliably block its content, although its KDoc (line 235) says it 'Dims and blocks its content'.
