result.summary:
The devtools API-log badge cannot be dragged. In DraggableBadge (core/devtools/.../DevBadge.kt:64-85), the detectDragGestures lambda adds each per-event delta to `x` and `y`. Those are plain `val` copies of the offset, captured when the composition ran. `pointerInput(bounds, badge)` never restarts during a drag: Compose 1.12.1 resets only on a key change or a call-site class change. So every move computes defaultPosition + thisEventDelta, and the badge jitters in place. PeriFlow and VitFleet ship the identical file, so both apps have the bug. The fix is to read the state inside the lambda and the offset{} block, and to clamp at placement time; code is in the report. The same family of bug makes a stepped AppSlider undraggable at normal speed, because each delta is added to the snapped value and rounds back. busyOverlay consumes taps in the Main pass, after the children have already handled them, so it does not block the sign-in and sign-up forms. Several features are silently broken or off:
- The WebSocket never connects: PlainClient has no WebSockets plugin, so webSocketSession throws and retries forever. Both apps fixed this.
- POST_NOTIFICATIONS is never requested, so pushes are never shown on Android 13+.
- The analytics opt-out toggle is never applied to Firebase Analytics or Crashlytics.
- Remote Config refresh() is never called.
- The app lock can be bypassed by pressing Home on the lock screen and reopening within 30s.
- A finished flexible Play update restarts the app with no prompt, contradicting its own comment.

Auth and session handling can leak data between accounts:
- Ktor's bearer-token cache is never cleared on sign-out or sign-in, so the next user's requests carry the previous user's token. VitFleet fixed this.
- A refresh that completes after sign-out writes the tokens back.
- A 408 or 429 from the refresh endpoint signs the user out.
- The push registration, app database and widget state survive sign-out.

On the network path, NetworkMonitor.isOnline is a cold callbackFlow. Each of the up to three first() calls per request registers and unregisters a NetworkCallback: binder cost, and a TooManyRequestsException risk. VitFleet fixed it with shareIn. Bodies are parsed twice, and an empty 204 success fails to decode. The template documents that as a call-site workaround; PeriFlow fixed it at the source. There are three OkHttp clients, and only one has certificate pins, so the refresh-token call is unpinned. Errors from the Room response cache escape the AppResult contract, and that table has no size limit. Queued offline mutations are dropped on any 4xx (including 429 and 408), and a corrupt queue row can crash the app on every reconnect. In dev and staging release builds the devtools recorder stores sign-in passwords and refresh-token bodies, and it never records failed requests. On weight: push forces Firebase Analytics, Crashlytics and Remote Config. WorkManager ships with no workers. Glance pulls WorkManager and Room and initialises them at every cold start. The room cache is on by default alongside the OkHttp cache. lifecycle-process is unused, and most of core/media has no caller. The full report has file:line evidence, root-cause notes, code sketches and a list of fixes from PeriFlow and VitFleet to port back.

findings.title: Devtools badge does not drag: drag lambda adds per-event delta to a stale captured position
findings.evidence: L64-65 `val x = if (offsetX.isNaN()) startX else offsetX` is a value copy. L76 `.pointerInput(bounds, badge) { detectDragGestures { change, drag -> offsetX = (x + drag.x)... } }`. Compose UI 1.12.1 SuspendingPointerInputFilter.update() (~L619-665) resets the coroutine only on a key change or a handler-class change, and bounds/badge do not change during a drag, so the first lambda (x = startX) runs forever. `drag` is the per-event delta, so offset = startX + delta on every event and the badge jitters in place. PeriFlow and VitFleet DevBadge.kt are identical apart from the package line.
findings.recommendation: Read state inside the lambda: `offsetX = currentX() + drag.x`, where currentX() reads the delegated state and clamps. Use pointerInput(Unit). Read the offset inside `.offset { }` (layout phase) and clamp there as well, so rotation cannot strand the badge. Restore the 48dp touch target (remove minTouchTarget = 0.dp at L91). Optionally spring-snap to the nearest edge on drag end. Add a Compose UI test that swipes and asserts the bounds moved.

findings.title: Badge offset is not clamped at placement; rotation strands it off-screen
findings.evidence: The offsets are rememberSaveable (L57-58) but bounds are remember (L59). Clamping happens only inside the drag callback (L81-84); `.offset { IntOffset(x.roundToInt(), y.roundToInt()) }` applies the raw value. x and y are also read in composition, so every drag frame recomposes.
findings.recommendation: Clamp inside the offset lambda against the current bounds and badge size, and read state only in that lambda.

findings.title: Stepped AppSlider cannot be dragged slowly (delta added to the snapped value)
findings.evidence: L67 `val fraction = ((value - valueRange.start) / span)` (already snapped). L137 `emitFraction(fraction + delta / travel)`. With steps=9 (catalog CatalogComponents.kt:235) half a step is about 50px, while one move event's delta is a few px, so the value rounds back to the same step every time. A continuous slider also loses deltas that arrive before the parent recomposes.
findings.recommendation: Track the absolute finger position as AppRangeSlider does (AppRangeSlider.kt:132-155, fractionAt(change.position.x)), or accumulate an unsnapped raw fraction during the drag (set it from fraction in onDragStarted).

findings.title: busyOverlay does not block children: it consumes in the Main pass, after the children
findings.evidence: `Modifier.pointerInput(Unit) { awaitPointerEventScope { while (true) { awaitPointerEvent().changes.forEach { it.consume() } } } }` uses the default PointerEventPass.Main. HitPathTracker.dispatchMainEventPass dispatches Main to the children before this node, so a child clickable fires. Used on SignIn.kt:174 and SignUp.kt:160 to stop input while submitting.
findings.recommendation: Use awaitPointerEvent(PointerEventPass.Initial) and consume. Add semantics { disabled() } as well.

findings.title: Swipe-to-action and bottom sheet recompose on every frame and launch a coroutine per drag delta
findings.evidence: `val progress = ... offsetY.value / sheetHeight` is read in composition (L81-87). AppSwipeToAction.kt:126-131 runs `scope.launch { offset.snapTo(...) }` per delta, and L160-168 has `if (offset.value != 0f)` in composition. The sheet's draggable has no nested-scroll hand-off.
findings.recommendation: Compute alpha inside graphicsLayer. Use derivedStateOf for the open/closed check. Move to AnchoredDraggableState. Port PeriFlow AppDetentSheet's NestedScrollConnection.

findings.title: WebSocket never connects: PlainClient lacks the WebSockets plugin
findings.evidence: providePlainClient (L54-65) installs no WebSockets, and AppWebSocket.kt:50 uses @PlainClient. Ktor 3.6 builders.kt:34 `plugin(WebSockets)` throws 'Plugin WebSockets is not installed'. AppWebSocket catches Throwable (L94-96) and retries forever. VitFleet HttpClientModule.kt:58-59 added install(WebSockets) with the comment 'without the plugin the upgrade fails'. VitFleet also had to filter websocket calls out of the ResponseObserver recorder, which otherwise tore the socket down every second.
findings.recommendation: Build a dedicated realtime client with install(WebSockets) { pingInterval = 20.seconds }, no recording and no HTTP timeouts. Port VitFleet's AppWebSocket changes: reset backoff only after the first frame, @Volatile and @Synchronized connect/disconnect, close only the socket captured at disconnect, refresh the token per attempt. Gate reconnects on connectivity and the process lifecycle.

findings.title: Ktor bearer token cache never cleared: the previous user's access token is sent after an account switch
findings.evidence: install(Auth) { bearer { loadTokens { ... } } } uses the default cacheTokens=true. Ktor AuthTokenHolder.loadToken returns the cached value ('Hot path'). `grep clearToken` finds nothing in the template. SessionCoordinator clears only the DataStore. VitFleet BearerTokenCache.kt:12-17 documents the same bug ('every call after a switch carried the old company's token') and clears via authProvider<BearerAuthProvider>()?.clearToken().
findings.recommendation: Bind a SessionScopedStore that calls clearToken(), and drop the cache on every token save. Better: replace the Auth plugin with PeriFlow's HttpSend interceptor plus an AuthTokenProvider seam (no token cache in Ktor, ktor-client-auth no longer needed).

findings.title: Refresh race resurrects a signed-out session; 408/429 from refresh signs the user out
findings.evidence: L117-124 calls tokenStore.save(...) after refresh with no check that the session is unchanged, so a sign-out during the refresh is undone and MainActivity's combine(settings, isAuthenticated) re-enters the signed-in shell. L128 `if (result.code in REFUSED_RANGE) endSession(...)` with REFUSED_RANGE = 400..499 (L198) includes 408 and 429. VitFleet SessionTokens.kt fixes all three (mutex, stale check, 'neither overwrite it nor end it', only 401 ends).
findings.recommendation: Adopt VitFleet's SessionTokens as the single refresh path for HTTP and the socket. End the session only on 401 (or a server-specific code).

findings.title: NetworkMonitor.isOnline is cold: register/unregister a NetworkCallback up to 3 times per request
findings.evidence: `override val isOnline: Flow<Boolean> = callbackFlow { ... registerNetworkCallback ... awaitClose { unregisterNetworkCallback } }` with no sharing. KtorNetworkClient.kt:84, :135 and :166 call `networkMonitor.isOnline.first()`. Android caps an app at about 100 callbacks (TooManyRequestsException), and line 84 is outside any try. VitFleet fixed it with shareIn(WhileSubscribed(5000, replayExpirationMillis=0), replay=1) and the comment 'the system allows an app only about a hundred at once'.
findings.recommendation: Share the flow in ApplicationScope (shareIn/stateIn). Also drop the pre-flight 'not VALIDATED → refuse' gate (it breaks captive portals and VPNs) and let OkHttp fail.

findings.title: Empty success body (204) fails decoding; the template works around it at the call site
findings.evidence: `NetworkJson.parseToJsonElement(result.data.body)` throws on "". AuthRepository.kt:79-82: 'decoding an empty body into `Unit` fails at the JSON parse'. delete<Unit>/post<_,Unit> return Failure(Serialization) on success. PeriFlow added parseBody (blank → JsonObject(emptyMap())).
findings.recommendation: Adopt PeriFlow's parseBody in both decode paths and remove the call-site workaround.

findings.title: Every response parsed twice; request bodies serialised twice; Dispatchers hard-coded
findings.evidence: bodyAsText() (KtorNetworkClient.kt:157), then parseToJsonElement (L46), then decodeFromJsonElement (L49). Requests go encodeToJsonElement (L146) and then ContentNegotiation serialises the tree. withContext(Dispatchers.Default) at L44 and L71 breaks the core/coroutines rule that dispatchers are injected.
findings.recommendation: Fast path: decodeFromString(deserializer, body) when the unwrapper is passthrough; for envelopes, decode an Envelope serializer once. Encode request DTOs straight to text. Inject the default dispatcher.

findings.title: Response-cache read/write exceptions escape AppResult; cache table unbounded
findings.evidence: responseCache.fresh (L78) and responseCache.put (L173-175) are outside any try. cached_responses.body is unbounded TEXT (ResponseCache.kt:63-69). Rows over the ~2MB CursorWindow throw SQLiteBlobTooBigException, and a full disk throws SQLiteFullException, turning a successful call into an exception. There is no eviction.
findings.recommendation: Wrap both calls in runCatching, skip bodies over a size cap, and add LRU/TTL eviction. Or drop the Room cache and rely on the OkHttp HTTP cache.

findings.title: Three OkHttp clients; certificate pins only on the authenticated client
findings.evidence: HttpClient(OkHttp) at L59 and L84 each build an OkHttpClient. Coil's default loader (coil-network-okhttp, no ImageLoader configured) builds a third. certificatePinner is applied only at L89, so the refresh-token POST (KtorTokenRefresher on @PlainClient) and the WebSocket handshake are unpinned.
findings.recommendation: Provide one @Singleton OkHttpClient: OkHttp.create { preconfigured = shared } for Ktor and OkHttpNetworkFetcherFactory(callFactory = { shared }) for Coil. Move pins to network_security_config <pin-set> so every client and WebView gets them.

findings.title: Devtools recorder stores passwords/refresh tokens in dev and staging release builds; never records failures
findings.evidence: recordExchanges = buildDevEnvironment().visible (AppModule.kt:30), which is true for non-prod release builds. `is TextContent -> content.text` captures sign-in and refresh JSON. DevToolsLog.redacted() scrubs only headers (L38-40). The panel shows bodies in a SelectionContainer. `failure = null` is hard-coded (L37), so timeouts and DNS errors never appear. Debug Logging at LogLevel.BODY (HttpClientModule.kt:188-195) sanitises only Authorization. PeriFlow added a credential-path filter to Logging.
findings.recommendation: Filter credential endpoints and redact JSON fields (password, *_token) in both the recorder and Logging. Record failures from sendWithRetries or an HttpSend interceptor. Lower the memory budget (CAPACITY=200 × 128KB bodies).

findings.title: Offline queue drops user mutations on any 4xx; 5xx head-of-line blocks forever; crash on a corrupt row
findings.evidence: `if (result.code !in REFUSED_RANGE) return; ... queue.remove(queued.id)` with 400..499 drops on 408, 429 and 401. Replays happen only on an offline→online flip (L221), with no timer. toRequest (L242-247) can throw (valueOf/decodeFromString) inside appScope.launch (BaseAppApplication.kt:96), and ApplicationScope has no CoroutineExceptionHandler (CoroutinesModule.kt:73-78), so the process crashes. The destructive migration (NetworkModule.kt:97) deletes queued writes, described as 'safe'.
findings.recommendation: Port VitFleet's queue: refused entries kept with the server's answer, MOMENTARY_REFUSALS {401,408,426,429}, a growing retry timer, a pass Mutex, passOrRetry try/catch, NETWORK_MIGRATION_1_2. Add a logging CoroutineExceptionHandler to ApplicationScope.

findings.title: POST_NOTIFICATIONS is never requested: pushes never shown on Android 13+
findings.evidence: post() returns early when !hasPermission. notificationsPermission (core/media/AppPermissions.kt:131-136) and rememberPermission have no callers outside core/media (grep). Target SDK 37, so the system never prompts on its own. PeriFlow added the request in Onboarding.kt:86-95 and NotificationSettings.kt:141.
findings.recommendation: Ask in onboarding or at first relevant use (behind the push feature marker), and offer a settings row. Move the permission helper into core:notification.

findings.title: A push without a link has no tap action; push registration not cleared on sign-out
findings.evidence: `contentIntent = message.data["link"]?.let(::deepLinkIntent)` exists only under opt:deeplink. AppNotifications.kt:105-115 sets a PendingIntent only when one is provided, so tapping does nothing. SessionCoordinator never unregisters FCM or tells PushTokenSink, so the next account on the device gets the previous one's pushes.
findings.recommendation: Default to the launcher intent. Add a SessionScopedStore that unregisters the installation with the backend (or FirebaseMessaging.unregister()).

findings.title: Analytics opt-out toggle is cosmetic; tracker seam unused; Crashlytics has no opt-out
findings.evidence: Settings.kt:137 writes analyticsEnabled; nothing calls AnalyticsTracker.setEnabled (grep: no injection of AnalyticsTracker anywhere). CrashlyticsReporter has no setEnabled. With firebase on, Firebase Analytics auto-collects after the user opts out. The KDoc 'The binding used in debug builds' (L32-35) is false. PeriFlow added CrashlyticsReporter.setEnabled.
findings.recommendation: Collect settings.analyticsEnabled in Application and apply it to both the tracker and crash reporting. Consider collection off until consent. Add a navigation screen-view hook or remove the seam.

findings.title: Every AppLogger.e becomes a Crashlytics non-fatal
findings.evidence: `AppLogger.reporter = { message, throwable -> if (throwable != null) crashReporter.recordException(throwable, message) else crashReporter.log(message) }`. Expected failures (KtorNetworkClient.kt:119 'Request failed', ImageCompressor 'Image compression failed') flood non-fatals.
findings.recommendation: Send e() as a breadcrumb and call recordException explicitly where an error is unexpected.

findings.title: push forces Firebase Analytics + Crashlytics + Remote Config
findings.evidence: push requires=("firebase",) (L189); firebase requires=("analytics", "flags") (L169) and ships analytics, crashlytics and config (AndroidFirebaseConventionPlugin.kt:13-19).
findings.recommendation: Split into google-services core, push (messaging + installations only), crashlytics, firebase-analytics and remote-config features.

findings.title: Remote Config never fetched; FeatureFlags has no consumer and is not observable
findings.evidence: grep FeatureFlags outside core/flags finds only Gradle files, so refresh() is never called and values never activate. core/devtools/build.gradle.kts:18-20 depends on :core:flags without using it. LocalFeatureFlags overrides (L24-29) are unreachable through the interface and backed by a plain mutableMapOf.
findings.recommendation: Call refresh() at startup, add observe(flag): Flow, use addOnConfigUpdateListener, and put a Flags override tab in the devtools panel (giving that dependency a purpose).

findings.title: App-lock bypass: the lock screen restarts the grace timer
findings.evidence: MainActivity.onStop → appLock.onHidden() sets lastVisibleAt (MainActivity.kt:212-215; AppLock.kt:24-26). When the opaque LockActivity covers MainActivity, MainActivity stops and the timer restarts. Press Home on the lock (noHistory finishes it, manifest L126-132) and reopen within 30s: shouldLock() sees elapsed < GRACE_MILLIS and returns false, so the app is open without authentication. PeriFlow AppLock.kt:21-54 fixed this with justUnlocked and an own-action grace.
findings.recommendation: Adopt PeriFlow's AppLock, or better, an in-activity Compose lock layer driven by ProcessLifecycleOwner that starts locked (also fixes the content flash). Add JVM tests for the state machine.

findings.title: App content visible before the lock appears (KDoc claims otherwise)
findings.evidence: KDoc L199-202: 'content is never on screen — even for a frame'. The code is `lifecycleScope.launch { if (appLock.shouldLock()) startActivity(...) }`, which suspends on DataStore, so MainActivity draws first and LockActivity's transition reveals the content.
findings.recommendation: Use an in-activity overlay whose locked state is decided synchronously (rememberSaveable plus process lifecycle), or keep the splash/condition until the decision is made.

findings.title: Flexible Play update restarts the app under the user; update prompt and review counter run on every resume
findings.evidence: L190-191 comment 'Asking rather than restarting under the user', then L192 `is AppUpdateResult.Downloaded -> appUpdates.install(result)`, which calls completeUpdate() (PlayStorePrompts.kt:46-48, KDoc 'never on its own'). repeatOnLifecycle(RESUMED) (L171-176) re-launches the update dialog on every resume and calls reviewPrompt.onLaunch (KDoc 'Call once per launch') on every resume. PeriFlow has the same code.
findings.recommendation: Show a Restart prompt or install on onStop. Store a dismissedUpdateVersion (PeriFlow AppSettingsStore). Check updates and count launches once per process.

findings.title: Session teardown misses Ktor token cache, app DB, push registration, widget state and in-flight GETs
findings.evidence: Only SessionScopedStore multibindings are cleared. No binding exists for Ktor's bearer cache, the AppDatabase (core/database DatabaseModule has none; PeriFlow adds clearAllTables()), FCM, the Glance HEADLINE state (AppWidget.kt:43,100) or the InFlightRequests map. runCatching at L53 also swallows CancellationException.
findings.recommendation: Register stores for each of these. Consider PeriFlow's 'wipe on uid change' rule.

findings.title: Undecryptable token leaves the user stuck 'signed in'; Keystore opened per call with a key-generation race
findings.evidence: isAuthenticated = contains(ACCESS_TOKEN) && contains(REFRESH_TOKEN), while KeystoreCipher.decrypt returns null on failure (KeystoreCipher.kt:29-39). loadTokens then returns null, so oldTokens==null means no endSession (HttpClientModule.kt:114) and every call 401s forever. secretKey() (L41-60) loads the KeyStore on every op, unsynchronised, so two first callers can each generate the key.
findings.recommendation: Treat a decrypt failure as signed out (clear and emit false). Cache the SecretKey in a synchronized lazy.

findings.title: FileProvider exposes the entire cacheDir (incl. the OkHttp cache of authenticated responses)
findings.evidence: `<cache-path name="uploads" path="." />` while the file's own comment says 'Deliberately not path="."'. Caused by ImageCompressor.compressToFile writing to the cacheDir root (ImageCompressor.kt:104).
findings.recommendation: Write uploads to cacheDir/uploads and declare path="uploads/".

findings.title: Camera capture lost after process death; avatar persists a temporary photo-picker URI
findings.evidence: `var pendingCameraUri by remember { mutableStateOf<Uri?>(null) }` is not saveable, so when the camera app kills the activity the result is dropped (L85-91). ProfileScreen.kt:123-125 plus ProfileRepository.kt:50-52 store uri.toString() from PickVisualMedia, whose grant is temporary.
findings.recommendation: Use rememberSaveable for the URI. Copy the avatar into filesDir with the existing ImageCompressor/ImageCompression.Avatar, or takePersistableUriPermission.

findings.title: Media module: capture limits never applied, misleading docs, most helpers unused
findings.evidence: recordVideo KDoc 'limits applied *at capture*' (L47), but captureExtras() (L141-145) is never called and videoSettings (L54) is only a remember key. VideoTranscoder.kt:73-74 tells devs to 'constrain capture with MediaPicker.recordVideo'. ImageCompressor, VideoTranscoder, VideoProbe and rememberPermission have no callers. Orientation is applied only when stripMetadata (ImageCompressor.kt:73); TRANSPOSE/TRANSVERSE unhandled; up to 3 ARGB bitmaps at once.
findings.recommendation: Trim to the picker plus one compressor (ImageDecoder.setTargetSize on API 28+, Default dispatcher), or make the documented behaviour true.

findings.title: Glance widget drags in WorkManager + Room and initialises them at every cold start
findings.evidence: glance-appwidget-1.2.0.module runtime deps include androidx.work:work-runtime-ktx. WorkManagerInitializer removal is fenced by <opt:workmanager> (L19-42), so widget-on/workmanager-off initialises WorkManager (and its Room DB) via App Startup. AppWidgets.setHeadline is never called.
findings.recommendation: Always remove WorkManagerInitializer and initialise on demand. Offer a RemoteViews widget for a one-line display.

findings.title: WorkManager feature ships with zero workers and adds KSP to core:network
findings.evidence: work-runtime-ktx, hilt-work and ksp(hilt-compiler) under opt:workmanager; grep for CoroutineWorker/HiltWorker finds nothing in the template.
findings.recommendation: Remove it, or make the queue replayer a real HiltWorker and keep the dependency only there.

findings.title: room feature (Room response cache) on by default duplicates the OkHttp cache; database requires it
findings.evidence: OkHttp Cache 50MB (L158-161) plus the Room cached_responses table. spec.py: room default=True and in the Standard preset; database requires=("room",) (L316), so an app cannot have a database without the network cache.
findings.recommendation: Rename room to offline-cache, turn it off by default, use one cache, and make database independent.

findings.title: Unused lifecycle-process dependency
findings.evidence: implementation(libs.androidx.lifecycle.process); grep ProcessLifecycleOwner finds nothing. Its App Startup initializer still runs.
findings.recommendation: Use it for the app lock and socket lifecycle, or remove it.

findings.title: AppDatabase: new apps start at v2 with a reference migration; not cleared on sign-out; REPLACE named upsert
findings.evidence: VERSION = 2 with MIGRATION_1_2 for the reference notes table. Only schemas/2.json exists, and the test hand-writes the v1 SQL and does not validate the schema. NoteDao.upsert uses OnConflictStrategy.REPLACE (Note.kt:31). No SessionScopedStore. AndroidRoomConventionPlugin passes room.schemaLocation as a KSP arg.
findings.recommendation: Start at v1, use @Upsert, bind clearAllTables() as session-scoped, and switch to the Room Gradle plugin with MigrationTestHelper.

findings.title: Dead pre-O notification code (minSdk 26)
findings.evidence: `if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < Build.VERSION_CODES.O) return` (L63) and toCompatPriority with a KDoc about pre-O devices (L133-143), while AppConfig.MIN_SDK = 26. notificationsPermission returns INTERNET below 33 (AppPermissions.kt:135).
findings.recommendation: Delete the dead branches and return null for 'no runtime permission needed'.

findings.title: Request latency budget ~90s; Timeout exception never produced; isOffline doc mismatch
findings.evidence: 30s request/15s connect/30s socket per attempt × 3 attempts (RetryPolicy maxRetries=2). NetworkException.Timeout (NetworkModels.kt:91) is never constructed: HttpRequestTimeoutException is an IOException and becomes Unknown. AppResult.isOffline is documented as including timeouts but is false for them.
findings.recommendation: Add an overall deadline for user-initiated calls, map timeouts explicitly, and drop the unused exception types.

findings.title: User-Agent with raw Build.MODEL can contain non-ASCII and break every OkHttp request
findings.evidence: userAgent = "${APPLICATION_ID}/${VERSION_NAME} (Android ${RELEASE}; ${MANUFACTURER} ${MODEL})". OkHttp rejects non-ASCII header values with IllegalArgumentException, which is caught as Unknown on every request.
findings.recommendation: Sanitise to printable ASCII.

findings.title: No tests for auth refresh, token cache, 204, WebSocket, app lock, badge drag, stepped slider, busyOverlay
findings.evidence: The test list covers only retry, cache and queue. 'a request the server refuses is dropped' encodes the data-loss behaviour.
findings.recommendation: Add JVM/Robolectric and Compose UI tests for each of these bugs.

missed: template/core/designsystem/src/main/kotlin/com/base/app/core/designsystem/component/list/AppSwipeToAction.kt:138 - full-swipe destructive commit is unreachable with 1-2 actions. offset is clamped to -revealPx (L80 revealPx = 84dp*actions.size, L130 coerceIn(-revealPx,0f)), but commit needs travelled > rowWidth*0.55 (L138). On any phone row (>=328dp) that is >=180dp, and the catalog (CatalogLists.kt:111) uses 2 actions = 168dp, so the 'full swipe triggers it' behaviour promised in the SwipeAction KDoc (L43-44) never happens.

template/core/designsystem/src/main/kotlin/com/base/app/core/designsystem/component/overlay/AppBottomSheet.kt:50-55 - Dialog gets onDismissRequest directly and DialogProperties leaves dismissOnBackPress at its default true. A back press or predictive back therefore removes the sheet instantly, skipping the slide-out in dismiss() (L68-76): an abrupt pop, against the polish goal.

template/core/network/src/main/kotlin/com/base/app/core/network/websocket/AppWebSocket.kt:97-99,112-119 - disconnect() cancels the connection job and then launches `session?.close()` on IO, while the cancelled job's finally sets `session = null` without closing `opened`. Both run on the multi-threaded IO pool, and `session`/`connection` are plain non-volatile vars, so close is often skipped. The session lives in the HttpClient's own scope (Ktor builders.kt launch), so the socket stays open after disconnect().

template/core/designsystem/src/main/kotlin/com/base/app/core/designsystem/component/selection/AppRangeSlider.kt:134-150 - awaitFirstDown() then drag(down.id){ change.consume() } consumes every move from the first pixel, with no touch slop or orientation check. A range slider inside a vertically scrolling screen steals the vertical scroll (the parent's slop detector sees consumed changes) and moves the thumb instead.

template/core/network/src/main/kotlin/com/base/app/core/network/NetworkRecording.kt:35 + template/core/devtools/src/main/kotlin/com/base/app/core/devtools/DevToolsLog.kt:46-47 - on dev and staging release builds the ResponseObserver reads every response body fully into a String (bodyAsText, including large or binary downloads) before truncation. The log keeps up to 200 exchanges x (128K-char request + 128K-char response), roughly 50-100MB of heap in the worst case. DevToolsPanel.kt:250-270 also lays out a 128K-char body as one non-lazy Text inside SelectionContainer.

template/app/src/main/kotlin/com/base/app/BaseAppApplication.kt:92 + template/core/notification/src/main/kotlin/com/base/app/core/notification/PushTokenRegistrar.kt:21-29 - the installation ID goes to PushTokenSink only at process start (and in onRegistered), regardless of auth state. Nothing re-submits it after sign-in, so a sink that posts to an authenticated endpoint fails before sign-in and only links the device to the account on the next cold start.
adopt: VitFleet core/network/src/main/kotlin/com/vitfleet/app/core/network/auth/BearerTokenCache.kt: clears Ktor's bearer cache (clearToken) as a SessionScopedStore and on every token save. Or PeriFlow core/network/.../auth/Authentication.kt + AuthTokenProvider.kt: HttpSend interceptor replacing the Ktor Auth plugin (drops ktor-client-auth; no in-Ktor token cache)
VitFleet core/network/.../auth/SessionTokens.kt: mutex-serialised refresh that respects token rotation, never resurrects a signed-out session, and ends the session only on 401
VitFleet core/common/.../network/NetworkMonitor.kt: shareIn(WhileSubscribed(5000, replayExpirationMillis=0), replay=1) so requests reuse one NetworkCallback registration

VitFleet core/network/.../di/HttpClientModule.kt:58-59 install(WebSockets), plus NetworkRecording.kt `filter { !call.request.url.protocol.isWebsocket() }`, plus websocket/AppWebSocket.kt hardening (reset backoff after first frame, @Volatile/@Synchronized, close only the captured socket, per-attempt path/headers)
PeriFlow core/network/.../realtime/RealtimeHttpClient: a separate WebSocket client without REST timeouts or recording

VitFleet core/network/.../ResponseCache.kt: queue keeps refused entries with the server answer, MOMENTARY_REFUSALS {401,408,426,429}, growing retry timer, pass Mutex, passOrRetry try/catch, owner scoping, NETWORK_MIGRATION_1_2 instead of a destructive drop
PeriFlow core/network/.../NetworkClient.kt parseBody (blank body → {} so 204 decodes into Unit/defaults), per-request timeoutMillis, RawBody
PeriFlow core/network/.../di/HttpClientModule.kt Logging filter excluding credential endpoints; DefaultRequest app-version header
PeriFlow app/src/main/kotlin/com/jorwen/periflow/lock/AppLock.kt: justUnlocked plus own-action grace (closes the lock-screen grace-timer bypass)
PeriFlow core/analytics CrashlyticsReporter.setEnabled (isCrashlyticsCollectionEnabled) and an AnalyticsTracker contract with setEnabled/flush
PeriFlow core/database/.../di/DatabaseModule.kt: database.clearAllTables() bound as a SessionScopedStore
PeriFlow feature/onboarding/.../Onboarding.kt:86-95 and feature/you/.../NotificationSettings.kt:141: POST_NOTIFICATIONS request flow
PeriFlow core/notification AppNotifications public (lock-screen-safe) version and app/push/NotificationTaps.kt
PeriFlow core/datastore AppSettingsStore.dismissedUpdateVersion plus ui/UpdatePrompts.kt: ask once per version instead of nagging on each resume
PeriFlow core/designsystem/.../overlay/AppDetentSheet.kt: NestedScrollConnection hand-off between sheet drag and inner scroll
PeriFlow app/.../session/SessionCoordinator.kt: wipe account data when the signed-in uid changes (keeps guest→account upgrades) and reconnect realtime
Within the template itself: AppRangeSlider's absolute-position gesture (AppRangeSlider.kt:132-155) is the right model for fixing AppSlider and similar delta-based drags

result.summary:
The benchmark module in the template cannot work as generated. `:benchmark` targets the flavoured `:app` but picks no flavour (no `missingDimensionStrategy`), so Gradle cannot tell which app variant to test. PeriFlow's commit 11e50cd confirms this ("The benchmark module never ran … ambiguous"), and VitFleet still ships the broken copy. Even with that fixed, three more problems remain:
- **Release builds would not ship the profile.** The app does not set `mergeIntoMain`, and the plugin defaults to per-variant profiles for apps, so `prodRelease` and `playstoreRelease` would carry none.
- **The profile records only onboarding.** Onboarding and auth are on by default, there is no hook to skip them, and the app has no test tags, so the recorded path ends at the onboarding screen.
- **No frame-timing tests exist** in any of the three projects: nothing measures tab switching, push/pop, predictive back, scrolling or glass, which are exactly what the overhaul wants to make smooth.

PeriFlow's hand-written walk failed silently (`?: return@forEach`, a bounded loop with no assertion). Its committed profile, described as covering every tab, contains no `TodayScreen`, no `AppShell` and zero `com/kyant` classes, so the liquid-glass draw path is not pre-compiled. The profile also put the whole walk into the startup profile: `baseline-prof.txt` and `startup-prof.txt` are both 36,575 lines. The KDoc names tasks that do not exist (`:benchmark:generateBaselineProfile`, `connectedBenchmarkAndroidTest`), one comment describes scrolling that never happens, and espresso and ext-junit are unused dependencies.

The catalog is clean and readable, but it does not show "every component, in both themes and all four styles", which its own subtitle claims:
- **Missing components and tokens:** 11 public components or helpers are never shown (NavigationRail, AppDialog, the picker dialogs, SnackbarHost, the skeleton parts, TwoPane, ResponsiveGrid, ClickableSurface, all press-feedback modifiers), along with 11 colour tokens, 3 shapes, `labelSmall`, every size token and every motion token. Most disabled states are missing too.
- **Feel page bug:** it nests an `AppTheme` that discards the dark/light mode and design style the user picked.
- **Wrong default style:** a generated project's catalog opens in Utility/Standard, because `apply_feel` only rewrites `AppRoot`.
- **Loading overlay demo is broken:** `AppLoadingOverlay` is laid out as a small masonry tile instead of covering the screen.
- **Smaller bugs:** the RTL layout is not mirrored, edge-to-edge insets are wrong, and the crossfade shows the window background mid-transition.
- **No accessibility checks:** there are no RTL, font-scale or reduce-motion toggles, and the Robolectric screenshot suite that covered light, dark and 2.0× font was deleted, leaving dead generator config behind.

Architecturally, the push/pop and tab-switch transitions are `internal` to `:core:navigation`, so the catalog cannot show, tune or benchmark the transitions the overhaul must fix; they should move to the design system. Nothing keeps the catalog in step with the design system: PeriFlow's catalog shows none of its liquid-glass work and never wraps a page in a `GlassStage`, so its glass bar has only ever rendered as the frosted fallback there. The report proposes a generator-side coverage test, a glass catalog section with a JankStats readout, a set of FrameTimingMetric benchmarks, and asserting UiAutomator journeys driven by test tags.

findings.title: Benchmark module cannot resolve the flavoured :app (no missingDimensionStrategy)
findings.evidence: defaultConfig has no flavour choice while :app has the 'environment' dimension with dev/staging/prod/playstore (build-logic Flavors.kt:9-23). The baselineprofile producer plugin copies only build types into the test module (BaselineProfileProducerPlugin.kt:165-190 in plugin 1.5.0). PeriFlow commit 11e50cd: 'The benchmark module never ran: with no flavour chosen the app's four were ambiguous.' PeriFlow's fix is at periflow/benchmark/build.gradle.kts:18-20. VitFleet's copy is still identical to the template's.
findings.recommendation: Add missingDimensionStrategy("environment", "dev") with a why-comment, and add a device-free CI step that compiles the module (./gradlew :benchmark:assembleBenchmarkRelease) in the 'all' matrix entry.

findings.title: Baseline profile and startup benchmark stop at onboarding in default projects
findings.evidence: collect { pressHome(); startActivityAndWait(); device.waitForIdle() }. On a fresh install, MainActivity.kt:239-246 routes to OnboardingKey or signIn before any tab, and onboarding and auth both default to True (spec.py:256,277). The template has no testTag or testTagsAsResourceId (zero grep hits) and no ReportDrawn, so UiAutomator can only match localized text and StartupTimingMetric cannot report TTFD.
findings.recommendation: Add a benchmark-only start gate: an intent extra honoured only when !BuildConfig.IS_SHIPPABLE that marks onboarding complete and installs a fake session. Set testTagsAsResourceId at the root and testTag("tab_$i") on bar and rail items. Add ReportDrawnWhen on the start tab. Have the journeys use By.res.

findings.title: No FrameTimingMetric benchmarks for tab switch, push/pop, predictive back, scroll or glass
findings.evidence: The only metric is StartupTimingMetric, with StartupMode.COLD only. No FrameTimingMetric, TraceSectionMetric, runtime-tracing or JankStats exists in the template, PeriFlow or VitFleet. PeriFlow's only glass FPS evidence is a code comment, Glass.kt:142: 'measured: two in three frames missed on a mid-range phone'.
findings.recommendation: Add TabSwitchBenchmark, PushPopBenchmark, PredictiveBackBenchmark (edge swipe) and ScrollBenchmark, plus GlassBenchmark (parameterized glass on/off) behind // <opt:liquidglass>, each with FrameTimingMetric and CompilationMode None vs Partial. Add WARM and HOT startup. Optionally add compose runtime-tracing with TraceSectionMetric. Run them on a physical mid-range device; CI only compiles them.

findings.title: PeriFlow's 'every tab' profile journey failed silently and recorded only onboarding
findings.evidence: tap(tab) ?: return@forEach skips missing tabs and repeat(MAX_ONBOARDING_STEPS) gives up without failing; both use By.text. The committed baseline-prof.txt has only TodayKey/TodayNavModule/Hilt keys for feature/today (no TodayScreenKt, no TodayViewModel), the same for the other tabs, zero AppShell classes and zero com/kyant classes. The only glass entry is GlassKt.drawnGlass.
findings.recommendation: When porting the journey shape into the template, make every step assert (error(...) if a tab or screen is not found) and use By.res test tags. Add a post-generation check that baseline-prof.txt contains AppShellKt and, with liquid glass on, com/kyant/backdrop.

findings.title: Feel page's nested AppTheme discards the selected theme mode and design style
findings.evidence: AppTheme(motionStyle = style, hapticsEnabled = haptics) { ... } relies on the defaults mode = ThemeMode.System and designStyle = Utility (AppTheme.kt:35,41), and the palette is re-resolved from those (AppTheme.kt:48-50). With Dark + Social picked on a light-mode phone, the 'Try it' and 'The vocabulary' groups render in light Utility. LocalAppMotion is internal (AppMotion.kt:166), so there is no motion-only override.
findings.recommendation: Add a public ProvideAppMotion(style, hapticsEnabled) { } to the design system that provides only LocalAppMotion and LocalAppHapticsEnabled, and use it in place of the nested AppTheme.

findings.title: Generated catalog ignores the project's design_style and motion_style
findings.evidence: mutableStateOf(AppDesignStyle.Utility); AppTheme(mode, designStyle) is called without motionStyle; CatalogFeel.kt:32 uses AppMotionStyle.Standard. generator/genkit/render.py:328-365 (apply_feel) only rewrites app/.../ui/AppRoot.kt. PeriFlow hand-edited both defaults to Bloom/Fluid.
findings.recommendation: Have the generator write the style once into a design-system AppBrand { designStyle; motionStyle } object, use it as the AppTheme defaults, and read it from both AppRoot and CatalogApp. apply_feel then rewrites one constant.

findings.title: Screen transitions are internal to :core:navigation, so the catalog cannot show or tune them
findings.evidence: internal object NavTransitions holds push, pop, modal and tabSwitch, using only Compose animation and AppMotion. The catalog depends only on :core:designsystem (catalog/build.gradle.kts:30). Its own navigation is a plain crossfade (CatalogApp.kt:84-92) and the bottom bar is a static strip (CatalogComponents.kt:367-379).
findings.recommendation: Move the specs to core/designsystem/animation/AppScreenTransitions.kt as a public API, keeping the NavDisplay wiring in :core:navigation. Add a catalog 'Navigation' section: a mini shell with bar or rail and tab switching, a list→detail push/pop, and a PredictiveBackHandler, all under the motion-style selector.

findings.title: Catalog claims every component but omits 11 components or helpers and most disabled states
findings.evidence: The subtitle reads 'Every component, in both themes and all four styles', and web/frontend/components/hero.tsx:56 says 'catalog app that shows every component'. Never referenced: AppNavigationRail, AppDialog, AppDatePickerDialog, AppTimePickerDialog, AppSnackbarHost, AppPagerIndicator, AppSkeleton/Line/Circle, AppTwoPane, AppResponsiveGrid, AppClickableSurface, pressScale/bounceClick/clickableNoIndication/appClickable/disabledAlpha, offsetShadow. Disabled is shown only for the primary AppButton, AppCheckbox, AppSwitch and AppTextField; it is missing for AppIconButton, AppChip, AppRadioButton, AppSlider, AppRangeSlider, AppSegmentedControl, AppListItem and AppCard(onClick).
findings.recommendation: Add the groups (including a 'Press feedback' group comparing indication, pressScale and bounceClick), add the disabled, readOnly and icon-size states, and add a generator unittest that fails when a public App*/Modifier.* in the design system is not referenced by the catalog.

findings.title: Foundations page misses tokens; captions claim a motion group, a status border and downloaded fonts that are not there
findings.evidence: Caption: 'content, a subtle fill and a border — always together', but StatusRow (167-191) never draws status.border. CatalogSection.kt:16 lists 'motion', but FoundationsSection has no motion group. Line 75 says 'Downloaded, not bundled.', which is false when googlefonts is off (the variant sets AppFontNames.Sans = "sans-serif"). 11 of 33 AppColors fields are missing (onAccent, scrim, focusRing, borderStrong, divider, contentDisabled ...), as are shapes none/xl/sheet, spacing xxs/xxxl/section, labelSmall and all AppSizes.
findings.recommendation: Draw the status border. Add Motion (durations, easings, springs, run live), Sizes and the missing tokens. Fence the font sentence with <opt:googlefonts>/<opt:!googlefonts>. Show weight, line height and tracking in TypeRow so the TypeVoice changes are visible.

findings.title: AppLoadingOverlay demo renders as a masonry tile instead of covering the screen
findings.evidence: AppLoadingOverlay is an in-layout AnimatedVisibility { Box(fillMaxSize) } (AppActionSheet.kt:134-155), emitted as a child of MasonryColumns. That layout measures each child with Constraints(minWidth = maxWidth = columnWidth) and unbounded height (CatalogLayout.kt:29), so the overlay becomes a column-wide scrim tile about 110dp tall placed in the shortest column. 'Block the screen' appears to do nothing. AppSnackbarHost (a BoxScope extension) cannot be demonstrated for the same reason.
findings.recommendation: Give SectionPage a Box with an overlay layer (a CompositionLocal slot) that sections can add AppLoadingOverlay and AppSnackbarHost to.

findings.title: Profile generator comment claims scrolling that never happens
findings.evidence: '// Scrolling is included because the first list frames are part of perceived startup.' is followed only by device.waitForIdle().
findings.recommendation: Implement the scroll in a separate journeys() collect, or delete the comment.

findings.title: Startup profile mixes startup and journey code (PeriFlow pattern)
findings.evidence: includeInStartupProfile = true is set on the single collect. PeriFlow kept it after adding the full walk, and its baseline-prof.txt and startup-prof.txt are both exactly 36,575 lines, so the dex layout optimisation gets no startup-only subset.
findings.recommendation: Split into startup() with includeInStartupProfile = true (launch to shell only) and journeys() with includeInStartupProfile = false.

findings.title: KDoc names Gradle tasks that do not exist
findings.evidence: `./gradlew :benchmark:generateBaselineProfile`: generateBaselineProfile is registered only by the consumer plugin (GenerateBaselineProfileTask.kt:31-49), which is applied to :app. StartupBenchmark.kt:14 `connectedBenchmarkAndroidTest`: AGP names it per variant (connectedBenchmarkReleaseAndroidTest) and the plugin adds no aggregate. PeriFlow corrected the first to :app:generateBaselineProfile.
findings.recommendation: Use ./gradlew :app:generateBaselineProfile and ./gradlew :benchmark:connectedBenchmarkReleaseAndroidTest, and add a short run-book to the generated README.

findings.title: Index↔page crossfade shows the fixed XML window background mid-transition
findings.evidence: fadeIn(tween(medium)) togetherWith fadeOut(tween(quick)) runs over two opaque scaffolds with nothing behind them. The window background is fixed at #F7F8FA / #0B0E14 (res/values*/colors.xml:3). Forcing the theme opposite to the system's, or using the Social, Editorial or Playful backgrounds, gives a visible flash. NavTransitions.tabSwitch (NavTransitions.kt:105-113) has the same partly-transparent overlap.
findings.recommendation: Put AppTheme.colors.background behind the AnimatedContent, or use the real push/pop transition once it lives in the design system. Flag the tabSwitch overlap to the navigation audit.

findings.title: No RTL, font-scale or reduce-motion preview; the deleted screenshot suite left dead config
findings.evidence: _TEMPLATE_ONLY = {"catalog/src/test/screenshots"} points at a folder removed in 7b1a97a, together with CatalogScreenshotTest (light, dark and fontScale 2.0). The catalog index only offers theme mode and design style (CatalogApp.kt:157-174). rememberReduceMotion reads Settings.Global with no override (ReduceMotion.kt:10-20). catalog/build.gradle.kts:17-18,33 keep the blank lines where the screenshot blocks were.
findings.recommendation: Add an environment bar applied via CompositionLocalProvider: LocalLayoutDirection, LocalDensity(fontScale 1.0/1.3/2.0), a new LocalReduceMotion and motion style. Remove the dead _TEMPLATE_ONLY entry. If screenshots come back, make them opt-in.

findings.title: Catalog drift: nothing keeps it in step with the design system (PeriFlow shows no glass)
findings.evidence: Section 5 never asks for a catalog entry and no test checks coverage. PeriFlow's catalog is the template's with two edits and references none of glass, GlassStage, ScreenEdgeBlur, AppGlassIcon, AppDetentSheet, AppCycleRing and 40+ other names. It never composes a GlassStage, so its BarTreatment.Glass bar has only rendered as the frosted fallback (Glass.kt:147-155). VitFleet did add CatalogFleet.kt and CatalogReports.kt.
findings.recommendation: Add generator/tests/test_catalog_coverage.py (public App* and token fields must appear in the catalog, with an allowlist) and one AGENTS.md line. With liquid glass, add a GlassStage-wrapped Glass section, a forced-fallback toggle and a JankStats readout in the catalog only.

findings.title: MasonryColumns uses place() and does not mirror in RTL
findings.evidence: placed.forEach { (placeable, x, y) -> placeable.place(x, y) }: place ignores LayoutDirection, placeRelative mirrors it.
findings.recommendation: Use placeable.placeRelative(x, y).

findings.title: Edge-to-edge insets: section bottoms hidden under the nav bar; demo bottom bar double-padded
findings.evidence: SectionPage pads only by gutter (16-32dp) after verticalScroll, and AppScaffold adds no nav-bar inset, so 3-button navigation (48dp) covers the end of every page. The index uses a fixed bottom padding of xxl (32dp, line 153). The bottom-bar demo (CatalogComponents.kt:367-379) does not consume navigationBars while AppBottomBar applies navigationBarsPadding (AppBottomBar.kt:117,141). The top-bar demo does consume its inset (281-285).
findings.recommendation: Add windowInsetsPadding(navigationBars.only(Bottom)) to the scroll content, use the nav-bar inset in the index contentPadding, and consumeWindowInsets(WindowInsets.navigationBars) around the bottom-bar demo.

findings.title: Catalog duplicates design-system text and constants that will drift
findings.evidence: AppMotionStyle.describe() restates the enum KDoc (AppMotion.kt:22-41), and PeriFlow had to add Fluid in both places. CatalogMotion.kt:229 STAGGER_STEP_MILLIS = 28 copies the internal AppTransitions.STAGGER_MILLIS (AppTransitions.kt:134) and feeds the 'Delayed by N ms' labels. CatalogGroup's header (CatalogSection.kt:67-80) duplicates AppSectionHeader (AppDataDisplay.kt:189-228). ShapeSwatch takes a needless @Composable () -> Shape.
findings.recommendation: Make the description a property of the enum (AppMotionStyle.summary). Expose the stagger step or drop the label. Build CatalogGroup on AppSectionHeader. Pass Shape directly to ShapeSwatch.

findings.title: Benchmark module hard-codes app id, SDK levels and JVM target and bypasses the conventions
findings.evidence: compileSdk = 37, minSdk = 28, targetSdk = 37 and JVM 17 are literals, while the generator rewrites only AppConfig.kt (render.py:284-308). PACKAGE_NAME = "com.base.app.dev" in both tests depends on the .dev suffix staying unchanged (AppConfig.kt:46).
findings.recommendation: Add a com.base.app.android.test convention plugin, or read AppConfig. Pass targetAppId from v.testedApks via androidComponents.onVariants and read it with InstrumentationRegistry.getArguments().

findings.title: Unused dependencies in benchmark and catalog
findings.evidence: androidx.test.ext.junit and espresso-core are never imported in benchmark sources, and espresso is used nowhere else (libs.versions.toml:58,170 exist only for it). catalog/build.gradle.kts:32 declares lifecycle-runtime-compose with no androidx.lifecycle import in the catalog.
findings.recommendation: Remove them, along with the espresso version catalogue entry.

findings.title: Catalog build file overrides AppConfig version, and the README falsely says :catalog has flavours
findings.evidence: readme.py:57 says 'Only `:app` and `:catalog` carry flavours', but catalog/build.gradle.kts:5-8 applies no flavour plugin (the comment saying so was deleted in 148d1d0). catalog/build.gradle.kts:14-15 hard-codes versionCode 1 / versionName 1.0.0, overriding AppConfig as set by AndroidApplicationConventionPlugin.kt:22-23.
findings.recommendation: Say only :app carries flavours, and delete the redundant version lines and leftover blank lines.

findings.title: Demo controls that look broken or contradict their captions
findings.evidence: AppCheckbox(false, {}, label = "Unchecked") ignores taps. 'Full name' and 'With an error' share one `text` state (162-174). The Feel page puts a non-scaling AppCard (AppCard.kt:61 scaleOnPress = false) under 'The pop on release is the part that matters' (CatalogFeel.kt:82-101).
findings.recommendation: Give each demo its own state, make the unchecked checkbox interactive or label it static, and caption the card as overlay-only feedback.

missed: CI never builds the benchmark test APK, which is how [0] shipped while CI is green. android-base/.github/workflows/ci.yml:136-142 runs `check assembleDevDebug assembleProdRelease`. :benchmark has no devDebug or prodRelease variant, and the `all` preset (ci.yml:106-107) does include baselineprofile (spec.py:298-305, not implied_only). `gh run list` shows the last five CI runs succeeded. The auditor's report mentions a compile-only step only as a fix line under B1, not as its own finding.

The generator never syncs window_background to the chosen design style, for the app or the catalog. template/app/src/main/res/values/colors.xml:4 and catalog/src/main/res/values/colors.xml:3 hard-code the Utility #F7F8FA/#0B0E14, and render.py:702-717 rewrites only launcher_background. Brand-tint, Paper and Cream backgrounds differ (StyleTones.kt:25,60,72,84,96), so the splash/window colour does not match the first Compose frame. This is the root cause behind [15]. Low severity.

The catalog index loses its scroll position every time a section is closed. CatalogApp.kt:84-92 swaps the index out through AnimatedContent with no SaveableStateHolder, so SectionIndex's LazyColumn (CatalogApp.kt:151, default rememberLazyListState) leaves composition and is recreated at the top. The list holds 14 entries plus the chip row and large title (about 1100dp), so on a phone it scrolls. Low severity.

Accuracy problem in the auditor's report (catalog-benchmark.md:466-473): it quotes PeriFlow's app/build.gradle.kts:131-137 as containing `dexLayoutOptimization = true`. The real block (periflow app/build.gradle.kts:135-137) holds only `mergeIntoMain = true`. In AGP 9.4.1, R8 dex-startup optimisation already defaults to true (ModulePropertyKeys.kt:67 in the gradle-9.4.1 sources), so a back-port does not need the flag.
adopt: periflow/benchmark/build.gradle.kts:18-20: missingDimensionStrategy("environment", "dev") with its why-comment; it fixes the template's broken benchmark module
periflow/app/build.gradle.kts:131-137: baselineProfile { mergeIntoMain = true } so every flavour ships the dev-generated profile (add dexLayoutOptimization = true)

periflow/benchmark/src/main/kotlin/com/jorwen/periflow/benchmark/BaselineProfileGenerator.kt:44-69: the journey shape (onboarding helper, per-tab visit, fling down/up with a gesture margin). Port it with asserting steps, By.res test tags and a separate startup collect, never the silent `?: return`

periflow/core/designsystem/.../foundation/Glass.kt:56-176: GlassDepth.Content (drawn) vs Chrome (one shared LayerBackdrop in GlassStage) plus the frosted fallback when !isRenderEffectSupported(), as the optional liquid-glass foundation; pair it with a GlassStage-wrapped catalog section and a GlassBenchmark
vitfleet/catalog/src/main/kotlin/com/vitfleet/app/catalog/CatalogFleet.kt and CatalogReports.kt: one catalog section per app domain as the design system grows; recommend it in the generated AGENTS.md
vitfleet/catalog/.../CatalogComponents.kt (CatalogToday = LocalDate.of(...)): pass a fixed 'today' into date components so catalog pages stay deterministic

Removed template CatalogScreenshotTest (git show 7b1a97a^:template/catalog/src/test/kotlin/com/base/app/catalog/CatalogScreenshotTest.kt): its light/dark/fontScale-2.0 parameterisation over CatalogSection.entries is the right coverage model; recreate it as in-app environment toggles, or as an opt-in feature

result.summary:
I audited web/frontend (the Next.js configurator plus /admin) read-only. I checked it against the generator's own Python (catalogue, validators, colour maths), the template's Kotlin, the Go API and PeriFlow's newer navigation and glass code. tsc and next build were not run because node_modules is absent and installing was not allowed.

The base is solid: the catalogue drives the feature list, the server records "generated" itself, the admin token lives in sessionStorage, there is a CSP, and no user string is ever rendered as HTML.

1. The configurator and the generator disagree on what a project contains and what is valid. Unticking a feature removes only direct dependents (it checks `requires`, not `implies`), so the generator silently re-adds what the UI shows as off. The site does not check versionName, colour hexes or targetSdk >= minSdk, and its reserved-word list is missing 19 words the generator rejects. Every one of these mismatches surfaces only as a 400 after the round trip.
2. The previews have drifted from the template. The colour ramp predates commit 99c4edf and draws the wrong text colour on the dark-theme accent for about 19% of accents, including the site's own Editorial accent. Font weights 800/900 are never loaded, and the landing showcase loads weights for only one of its four families. Feature modules become tabs in the generated app but not in the preview.
3. The design and motion styles are hand-written maps indexed by keys that come from the catalogue. If the generator adds a style (for example "Glass" in the overhaul), the Look and Motion steps crash.
4. Performance: every keystroke or colour-picker drag re-renders the whole landing page through the lifted report context. That is about 9 phone previews per input event. The whole page is a client component, the static catalogue is fetched after hydration, and the Look step fires 13 separate Google Fonts stylesheet requests.
5. Accessibility: the whole site has only 2 ARIA state attributes. Feature cards, presets and style pickers expose no selected state. The modal has no focus trap, framer-motion ignores reduced motion, and 36 low-contrast text usages fall below AA. On a 360px phone the 280px live preview is clipped. On desktop the "sticky" preview never sticks, because the card's overflow-hidden breaks it.
6. Admin: the header says "last 30 days", but success rate, durations, zip size and feature popularity are all-time. Features nobody picks can never appear in the popularity chart, which is that chart's stated purpose. The referrer is always the site's own origin, country is never written, and validation rejections are invisible. There are no date ranges, filters, pagination or CSV export, and a failed Refresh logs the admin out.

The report lists every metric that exists today, what is stored but never shown, what is missing in priority order (P0/P1/P2), a schema sketch, a proposed module split, and what liquid-glass support in the configurator and preview needs.

findings.title: Unticking a feature removes only direct dependents; generator re-adds features the UI shows as off
findings.evidence: `if (next.has(other.key) && other.requires.includes(key)) next.delete(other.key);` uses direct `requires`. Catalogue: push.requires=['firebase'], firebase.requires=['analytics','flags']. Unticking analytics drops firebase but leaves push ticked; ProjectSpec.validated() runs resolve_features and ships firebase+analytics+flags anyway. Same for network→database/googlesignin and forms→googlesignin. The request and generations.features record the unresolved list.
findings.recommendation: Use the transitive closure the catalogue already provides: `other.implies.includes(key)`. Show 'Also removed: …' with Undo, and on tick 'Also adds: …' from `implies`. Send and record resolved features.

findings.title: Catalogue style keys cast into hard-coded token maps: a new design or motion style crashes Look and Motion steps
findings.evidence: `const key = style.key as DesignStyleKey;` then `DESIGN_TRAITS[key].map` (162). AppPreview `DESIGN_TOKENS[config.designStyle]` (app-preview.tsx:94). `MOTION_TOKENS[styleKey]` (look-step.tsx:295, app-preview.tsx:102). Casts at configurator.tsx:168-169. Any catalogue key not in these Records gives undefined and throws, the same class of crash as commit b12122b.
findings.recommendation: Emit design and motion tokens (and traits) from the generator in the catalogue so the site holds no hand-mirrored numbers. Until then, filter catalogue styles to known keys and fall back to Utility/Standard. Add noUncheckedIndexedAccess.

findings.title: targetSdk state can fall below minSdk; select shows a value other than what is sent
findings.evidence: Target options are filtered with `.filter((level) => level.level >= minSdk)` but targetSdk is never clamped. Set target 30, then min 33: the controlled select has no matching option, Review shows '33 / 30', and the generator rejects it ('targetSdk cannot be lower than minSdk', spec.py:818-819).
findings.recommendation: Clamp in the minSdk setter (`setTargetSdk(t => Math.max(t, next))`) and add an sdk error to validate().

findings.title: No client validation for versionName or colour hexes; an invalid hex previews as a convincing blue
findings.evidence: `if (!/^[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/.test(clean)) return [0.17, 0.42, 0.93];` silently substitutes a colour. BrandColourRow (look-step.tsx:335-346) and the Version name input (configurator.tsx:952-958) have no error, and ReviewStep.problem ignores both. The generator requires `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$` (spec.py:829) and a 6-digit hex (spec.py:891-899). Clearing a secondary/tertiary field refills it with the derived value (value={resolved}).
findings.recommendation: Single validate(state, catalogue.rules) module, with regexes served by the catalogue. Keep raw field text locally and commit only valid hexes. Block Review on these errors.

findings.title: Package reserved-word list claims to mirror the generator but differs by 19 words; literals and Kotlin keywords pass both sides
findings.evidence: Comment 'Mirrors validate_package_name'. Running the generator: server-only rejections are and, async, await, boolean, def, del, elif, except, from, global, lambda, nonlocal, not, or, pass, raise, strictfp, with, yield. Both sides accept com.example.null/true/typealias (validate_package_name verified), which breaks the Java R class or Kotlin package.
findings.recommendation: Serve reservedPackageWords from the catalogue. In the generator, drop Python keywords and add null/true/false/typealias/typeof.

findings.title: Keyword module names (class, object, fun, when, null) accepted by site and generator; build fails
findings.evidence: moduleError only checks `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` and reserved dirs. ProjectSpec(feature_modules=('class',)).validated() is ACCEPTED (verified for class/object/fun/when/null/true/typealias). The name becomes a package segment: scaffold.py:27 `f"{spec.package_name}.feature.{name}"`, scaffold.py:127 `package {pkg}.data.{name}`.
findings.recommendation: Reuse the package-segment keyword check in validate_module_name (generator/genkit/spec.py:937) and expose it via catalogue rules.

findings.title: Preview colour ramp predates commit 99c4edf: wrong dark on-accent text for ~19% of accents
findings.evidence: ramp() hard-codes dark `on: "#06101f"`, compares light against pure black, and has no _legible darkening. render.py now uses brand_shades/_legible/_readable_on. Over 2000 random accents: 389 have generator white vs preview #06101f, 111 have shade differences, 66 have light on-colour differences. The site's own Editorial accent #1F4D3A (styles-showcase.tsx:13) gets white on #527365 in the app and near-black in the preview.
findings.recommendation: Port _legible, _dark_variant and _readable_on exactly. Add a golden fixture (generator emits ramps.json for ~50 accents) checked by a test so the two cannot drift again.

findings.title: Showcase loads weights for the last family only; 800/900 weights never loaded anywhere
findings.evidence: `families = STYLES.map(...).join("&family=")` then `family=${families}:wght@400;600;700`, so only Nunito gets weights and DM Sans, Plus Jakarta Sans and Fraunces load at 400 (faux bold). font-picker.tsx:17 loads 400;600;700 while typeFor uses 800 (bold voice) and 900 (rounded voice), app-preview.tsx:208-232. The 'heavier headlines / extra-bold' traits are invisible.
findings.recommendation: Append `:wght@400;600;700;800;900` per family before joining. Request 800/900 in loadGoogleFont.

findings.title: Feature modules become bottom-bar tabs in the generated app but not in the preview; no tab-count warning
findings.evidence: tabsFor() only knows sample/paging/search/profile/settings. Generator: scaffold.py:41 `shell_tabs = [shell_tab(name) for name in spec.feature_modules]` inserted at AppDestinations.kt:40 `<generated:shell-tabs>`. Everything preset plus 3 modules gives 8 tabs in the app and 5 in the preview.
findings.recommendation: Add modules to PreviewConfig and render module tabs. Warn above 5 tabs. Mention the tab in the modules hint (configurator.tsx:673).

findings.title: Every configurator input re-renders the whole landing page (≈9 phone previews per event)
findings.evidence: Home holds `reportContext` state. Configurator publishes on every change (configurator.tsx:256-271, deps include appName/accent/fontName). There are 0 memo() calls, so Hero, StylesShowcase (4 AppPreviews), Included, Faq and Creator re-render, plus 5 AppPreviews on the Look step. A colour-picker drag fires this continuously.
findings.recommendation: Keep the report context in a ref read by FeedbackButton when it opens (no Home state). Feed previews useDeferredValue(previewConfig). Memo AppPreview, or enable the React Compiler.

findings.title: Entire landing page is a client component; static catalogue fetched after hydration
findings.evidence: `"use client"` at the top of page.tsx ships Hero/Included/Faq/Creator/Footer copy as JS. fetchCatalogue runs in useEffect (lines 24-39), so the configurator shows a spinner and the hero count shows '—' until it arrives. Deploy skew between a cached catalogue and the bundle caused the b12122b crash.
findings.recommendation: Make the static sections Server Components and keep client islands. Have CI emit catalogue.json from the generator and import it at build, so page and catalogue deploy atomically. Keep /api/options for CLI and agents.

findings.title: 13 font stylesheet requests: one per suggestion on Look mount, plus render-blocking third-party site fonts
findings.evidence: `suggestions.forEach((family) => void loadGoogleFont(family));` creates 12 <link>s at wght 400;600;700 each. layout.tsx:47-51 loads the site fonts via a fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet.
findings.recommendation: One css2 request with all families and `&text=` subsets for chip labels; load the full family only for the chosen font. Use next/font/google for site fonts (self-hosted, no layout shift, no IP to Google).

findings.title: lg:sticky live preview never sticks because the Card's overflow-hidden becomes its scroll container
findings.evidence: `<Card className="mt-6 overflow-hidden">` wraps LivePreview's `className="lg:sticky lg:top-24"` (look-step.tsx:62). overflow:hidden creates the sticky scroll container, and it does not scroll.
findings.recommendation: Use `overflow-clip`, which clips without creating a scroll container and keeps the step slide clipped.

findings.title: Toggle-like controls expose no selected state; hidden check glyph read in both states; Space scrolls on motion cards
findings.evidence: Feature cards are motion.button with no aria-pressed or aria-checked. The '✓' span is always rendered (text-transparent when off) at 822-831. Presets (767-781), design cards (look-step.tsx:148), Segmented (primitives.tsx:143) and feedback options have no state either. Motion cards are `div role="button"` whose Space handler lacks preventDefault (look-step.tsx:252-258). The only ARIA state attributes in the tree are configurator.tsx:697 and primitives.tsx:110.
findings.recommendation: role=checkbox/aria-checked for features and radiogroup/radio for presets, styles and segments. aria-hidden on glyphs. aria-current=step on StepBar. Native buttons for motion cards.

findings.title: Site palette fails WCAG AA for hints, captions, warnings and primary button labels
findings.evidence: Computed in light theme: ink-500 #a89b85 on ink-950/900/850 = 2.32/2.49/2.67 (36 usages, e.g. configurator.tsx:801,838); ink-400 on 900 = 4.42; amber on 900 = 4.01 (signing warning); on-accent on accent = 4.41 (every primary button). The site claims the generated app is 'checked against WCAG AA' (included.tsx:51).
findings.recommendation: Darken light ink-500 to ~#857865, ink-400 to ~#71665a, amber to ~#94600f and accent to ~#c2401b. Add a contrast unit test for the token pairs.

findings.title: Hero says 'nothing stored' while the FAQ and DB store app name, package and features
findings.evidence: 'No sign-up, nothing stored, no email.' vs FAQ app/page.tsx:242-249 'The app name, package, and which features you picked' and migrations/0001_initial.sql:16-25 storing app_name, package_name, font, accent, modules.
findings.recommendation: Reword to 'No sign-up. We keep the name, package and features you pick, never your IP.'

findings.title: Admin claims 'last 30 days' but headline rates, durations, zip size and feature popularity are all-time
findings.evidence: 'Everything on this page is the last 30 days unless it says otherwise.' store.go:199-207 computes successRate/median/p95/zip over all generations with no WHERE; FeaturePopularity (store.go:304-311) has no date filter. The Success card subtitle shows a 30-day count next to an all-time rate.
findings.recommendation: Global date-range picker passing from/to to every endpoint; label each card's window.

findings.title: Feature popularity cannot show zero-adoption features and uses unresolved, preset-biased lists
findings.evidence: Copy: 'The ones nobody picks are candidates for deletion.' The SQL `FROM generations, unnest(features)` (store.go:306-311) yields only features picked at least once. features are raw client lists (see F1). There is no way to tell 'picked' from 'came with preset'.
findings.recommendation: Left-join against the catalogue to show 0% rows. Record resolved features plus preset_base/added/removed. Add a per-feature weekly trend.

findings.title: Referrer telemetry is always the site's own origin; UTM, country and device never captured
findings.evidence: track() sends only {step}. The API stores `trimReferrer(r.Header.Get("Referer"))` of the same-origin XHR (server.go:299), which under vercel.json's strict-origin-when-cross-origin is the page URL, trimmed to the site origin. record() never sets Country (server.go:283-300), so the column is always NULL.
findings.recommendation: On 'landed', send document.referrer origin, utm_* and a device/viewport bucket. Record x-vercel-ip-country. Add source/country/device columns to visits.

findings.title: Validation rejections invisible in admin; Recent shows time without date; fetched failure/zip fields unused
findings.evidence: `{new Date(row.at).toLocaleTimeString()}` has no date. The Recent type includes failure and zipBytes (43-52) but they are never rendered (597-617). Generator rejections are stored as failure_reason (server.go:182) and no widget shows them, so frontend/generator validation drift is undetectable. Rows use key={index}.
findings.recommendation: Top rejection reasons table. Split success rate into user rejections vs crashes. Make Recent a paginated, filterable table with date, preset, styles, failure reason and CSV export (formula-safe).

findings.title: Funnel lacks per-step data; 'Configured' actually means 'clicked Generate'; 'generated' counted on interrupted downloads
findings.evidence: track("configured") fires inside generate(). No wizard step events exist. The server records RecordVisit 'generated' after io.Copy even if the copy errored (server.go:227-236).
findings.recommendation: Track each wizard step (step_identity…step_review). Rename the funnel labels. Record 'generated' only on a completed copy and count interruptions separately.

findings.title: configurator.tsx god component: 1370 lines, 28 useState, 22-prop step components, untestable request building
findings.evidence: 28 useState in Configurator (152-192). BuildStep has 22 props (861-909) and ReviewStep 22 (1139-1197). The done type is written twice (187-192, 1182-1187) and the errors shape twice. generate() mixes state, side effects and spec building. There are no frontend tests.
findings.recommendation: useReducer ConfigState plus pure resolve.ts/validate.ts/request.ts modules (unit-tested). One file per step. Derive preset from the feature set.

findings.title: Feedback modal has no focus trap or focus return; role=dialog on the backdrop
findings.evidence: `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` is on the overlay motion.div that also handles onClick close. There is no trap and no restore; only autoFocus on the title.
findings.recommendation: Use a native <dialog> with showModal(), or a focus-trap hook, and return focus to the trigger.

findings.title: framer-motion ignores prefers-reduced-motion (only CSS transitions are disabled)
findings.evidence: The @media (prefers-reduced-motion) block zeroes CSS animation/transition only. Hero entrance, step slide (configurator.tsx:415-419), whileHover/whileTap, layout pills and preview springs still animate. No MotionConfig anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the app in <MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">.

findings.title: Any admin refresh failure logs the admin out; helpful network error unreachable
findings.evidence: catch sets setAuthed(false) for any error, including one 500 from /api/admin/health or the reload after a status change. fetch network errors are TypeError (an Error), so the DATABASE_URL explanation (122-123) never shows.
findings.recommendation: Log out only on 401. Keep the last data and show a banner on other failures.

findings.title: Admin mutations ignore response.ok, can reject unhandled, and reload all 7 endpoints
findings.evidence: onUpdate/onResolve `await fetch(...)` with no ok check or catch, then `void load(token, showResolved)`.
findings.recommendation: Optimistic update with error toast; refetch only the affected list.

findings.title: Feedback status filter is client-side over the newest 100, hiding older new reports
findings.evidence: page.tsx:93 fetches `/api/admin/feedback?limit=100` with no status. `items.filter(item => filter === "all" || item.status === filter)`. The API already supports ?status= (server.go:378-390).

findings.title: Generation error stack traces unreadable: detail is empty and the message is truncated to one line
findings.evidence: Message rendered with `truncate`. Expand requires `group.detail` (570), but generation errors are recorded with detail "" (server.go:191), so stderr is folded into the message. path and firstSeen are never shown.
findings.recommendation: Store stderr in detail server-side. Show the full message on expand, link to the affected generations, and show the feature combos involved.

findings.title: Site hides generator capabilities: staging URL forced to dev, deep-link host fixed to example.com, WebSocket URLs unsettable
findings.evidence: `staging: devUrl` (347), `deeplink_host: "example.com"` (356). web_socket_urls is never sent even with websocket on. Template default staging is https://staging.example.com/api/ (AppConfig.kt:54).

findings.title: Catalogue load failure has no Retry (cold-start container leaves the page dead)
findings.evidence: The catch sets a permanent failure message; the only action is 'Get the CLI instead' (58-68). generate() has no timeout or cancel, stale done/failure persist, and there is no aria-live.

findings.title: Motion and bar preview diverge from where the template is heading (PeriFlow push without dim, bar over content, layout-property animation)
findings.evidence: Push animates the list to `opacity: 0.72`. PeriFlow NavTransitions.kt:21-35 removed the fade ('a fade renders the whole screen, every piece of glass in it, into an offscreen copy each frame'). AppPreview lays the bar below the content (app-preview.tsx:108-150) while AppShell overlays it. The indicator animates `left: calc(...)` (773,795).
findings.recommendation: Update the preview in the same PR as the backport. Absolutely positioned bar over scrolling content (needed for glass). Animate x transforms. Glass via CSS backdrop-filter in the live phone only, with drawn-glass approximation in thumbnails.

findings.title: App name is ASCII-only but doubles as launcher label
findings.evidence: `/^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9 ._-]*$/` mirrors spec.py:702, so 'Café' or a Hindi name is impossible although hi is an offered language.
findings.recommendation: Split into a display name (Unicode, at most 30 characters) and a derived ASCII code name, in the generator and the form.

findings.title: /admin inherits robots index:true
findings.evidence: `robots: { index: true, follow: true }` in the root layout; there is no admin layout override.
findings.recommendation: app/admin/layout.tsx exporting `robots: { index: false, follow: false }`.

findings.title: Dead exports and computations, unused CSS, duplicated dark palette, dead lint script
findings.evidence: EASE_ENTER/EXIT/STANDARD are never imported while the same béziers are inlined five times (app-preview.tsx:130,135; motion-preview.tsx:75,81,91). secondary/tertiary/skeleton ramps and Ramp.pressed are computed and never read (84-103, 215-221). `.grain` is unused (globals.css:164). The dark palette is duplicated (globals.css:42-63 and 66-89). `"lint": "next lint"` has no ESLint and next lint is gone in Next 16.

findings.title: Comments contradict code or narrate history (against AGENTS.md)
findings.evidence: Field comment: 'The hint stays put when an error appears rather than being replaced by it', then line 74 `{hint && !error && …}` hides it. Press comment says 0.96 but code uses scale 0.97 (9 vs 15). configurator.tsx:71 '/** The reserved list is not written out here. */'. hero.tsx:176 'how the old one survived so long'. feedback.tsx:20 'does not record it yet'. primitives.tsx:150 explains layoutId basics.
