findings.title: Copy that the overhaul will make false: 'Its own ripple', 'Everything is MIT'
findings.evidence: 'Its own ripple, type scale, 80-odd components…'. app/page.tsx:254 'Everything is MIT.' PeriFlow's LiquidInteraction.kt:1-5 is adapted from Kyant0/AndroidLiquidGlass under Apache-2.0.
findings.recommendation: Update both in the PR that drops ripple or ports Kyant catalog code; add a third-party notice.

missed: No LICENSE file exists anywhere in the repo (`git ls-files` shows no LICENSE/COPYING; README has no licence section), yet the site states MIT three times: web/frontend/components/hero.tsx:33 'Open source · MIT', web/frontend/app/page.tsx:254 'Everything is MIT.', web/frontend/app/page.tsx:286 'MIT licensed.' Legally the code is all-rights-reserved, which AGENTS.md's 'must not over-promise' rule forbids claiming otherwise.

web/frontend/components/included.tsx:10 'Its own ripple' is false today: template/core/designsystem/.../foundation/AppIndication.kt:18-80 draws a flat fading alpha overlay, and the template has no ripple at all (README.md:314 repeats the claim).

Feedback and errors are truncated by bytes, which produces invalid UTF-8 that Postgres rejects. web/api/internal/store/store.go:483-488 `return s[:limit] + "…"` is applied at store.go:536 (title 200, body 8000) and store.go:150 (error message 1000). The client limits by characters (feedback.tsx:289 maxLength=200), so a 70-character Devanagari title (210 bytes) is cut mid-codepoint (verified: utf8.ValidString false). The INSERT then fails, SaveFeedback returns an error, and the visitor gets 'That could not be saved'. Hindi is an offered language. RecordError silently drops non-ASCII stderr rows the same way.

Admin 'Success rate', 'Projects generated' and the daily 'generated' bars count the visitor's own validation rejections as failed generations. server.go:182 records InvalidRequestError via s.record(..., false, ...), and store.go:199-208 computes count(*) and avg(succeeded) over every row. page.tsx:264-270 labels the total 'Projects generated' and turns the rate red below 95%, so a burst of mistyped package names looks like a generator outage, and rejected requests are counted as projects.
adopt: Backport PeriFlow push/pop without the dim fade (periflow-android/core/navigation/src/main/kotlin/com/jorwen/periflow/core/navigation/NavTransitions.kt:21-47) and update web/frontend/components/motion-preview.tsx:58-69 in the same change.

Use PeriFlow glass strength tokens (Glass.kt:113-121, blur 6/10/16dp; refraction 8/16/24) and its drawn-glass fallback (Glass.kt:146,179-200) as the spec for a CSS glass emulation in app-preview.tsx: real backdrop-filter only in the single live phone, the drawn approximation in thumbnails and the showcase.
Port generator/genkit/render.py brand_shades/_legible/_readable_on into lib/app-theme.ts ramp(), with a generator-emitted golden fixture (ramps.json) checked by a test.

Extend genkit/catalogue.py to emit validation rules (version/hex/url/font regexes, reservedPackageWords, minCompileSdk) plus design/motion tokens and traits, so web/frontend has no hand-mirrored copies (fixes F2-F6).
Emit catalogue.json at CI build time into web/frontend/lib and import it, keeping /api/options for the CLI and agents; removes the hydration waterfall and deploy skew (see commit b12122b).

Keep and extend: catalogue-driven feature rendering (configurator.tsx:792-855), server-side 'generated' step (server.go:262-266), ETag no-cache catalogue, in-view-only animation loops (styles-showcase.tsx:28-32, motion-preview.tsx:40-41), and signing off by default with generated passwords (configurator.tsx:178-183,292-300).

Admin P0: global date range, rejection-reasons table from generations.failure_reason, zero-inclusive feature adoption joined with the catalogue, paginated filterable generations table with formula-safe CSV; P1: per-feature weekly trends, failure rate by feature/combo/commit, wizard step funnel, referrer/UTM/country (x-vercel-ip-country)/device capture; P2: platform and generator_version columns for the KMP/SwiftUI generators, and client error reporting via app/error.tsx.

result.summary:
The Go API is small and mostly well built. It passes the spec on stdin, kills the whole process group on timeout, uses parameterized SQL, compares the admin token in constant time, and blocks the keystore `existing_path` field in both Go and Python. gofmt, go vet and go test all pass. staticcheck finds only dead code (`logger`, `logWriter`). The store, config and handler code paths have no tests.

The serious problems:
- **Cheap DoS:** no limit on feature-module count or name/package length. A 35 KB request took 29 s, 358 MB RAM and produced a 29 MB zip; four can run at once.
- **Temp-dir leak:** every timeout or abandoned download leaves Python's own staging directory in /tmp (619 MB reproduced after a SIGKILL), including signing keys and plaintext passwords when keys were requested. The fix is to give the child process an explicit environment with TMPDIR set to Go's work directory.
- **Bugs hidden as user errors:** real generator failures (RenderError, OSError, any exception) come back as HTTP 400, never reach the admin error list, and their traceback is dropped.
- **CI gaps:** the `standard` preset (the site's default, and the only one with auth on and Google sign-in off) is never built. The headless zip path users actually download is never exercised. The Docker image is never built or smoke-tested before a production deploy. There is no concurrency group on deploy, so an older commit can finish last.

Telemetry is partly wrong:
- The referrer column always holds the site's own origin.
- The country and error-detail columns are never written.
- User cancellations are recorded as bugs and keep re-opening resolved errors.
- Interrupted downloads count as successes.
- The IPv6 visitor hash drops the last group of the address.
- Long Hindi feedback hits a 500 because truncation splits UTF-8.

Telemetry writes are synchronous and cost 3 database round trips per generation. Small JSON responses (including the page-load `/api/options`) are held until those writes finish (probe: 402 ms for 400 ms of work), and a database outage at boot takes the generator down.

The Go toolchain is out of support and inconsistent: 1.24 in go.mod and CI, 1.25 in Docker, while 1.27.2 and 1.26.9 are current. pgx and x/crypto are well behind.

The Docker image carries a 188 MiB JRE only for keytool (the comment says 55 MB). It also recompiles Python on every spawn, about 150 ms per request, because the official image strips .pyc files and the process runs as nobody.

Architecturally, the Android-shaped Go request struct silently drops unknown fields. Each new spec option has needed edits in four places, so the three-target plan (android, cmp, swift) needs an opaque passthrough with `/api/v1/{target}`, a per-target catalogue and semaphore, a `target` column with a jsonb spec, versioned migrations, and macOS CI jobs. Liquid glass needs no API change as long as it is added as a feature key, not a new top-level field.

findings.title: Unbounded feature_modules/app/package length allows CPU/RAM/disk exhaustion per request
findings.evidence: spec.py validates each module name but not count; _APP_NAME (702) and package segments unbounded; Go (web/api/internal/generate/generate.go:19-45, server.go:155) only caps body at 64KB. Measured: 35KB body with 4000 modules -> 29.4s wall, 358MB RSS, 29MB zip; SIGKILL after 5s left 619MB staging dir. MAX_CONCURRENT_GENERATIONS=4, rate limit per IPv6 address.
findings.recommendation: Add caps in spec.validated (MAX_FEATURE_MODULES≈12, app_name<=50, package<=100, segments<=8), expose them in the catalogue, and add a Go precheck (counts, lengths, control chars) before acquiring the semaphore. Add MemoryMax/TasksMax to the VPS unit.

findings.title: Staging dir (with keystores/passwords) leaks in /tmp on every timeout or client abort
findings.evidence: Go removes only its androidgen-out-* dir (126-130); Python stages in its own tempfile.TemporaryDirectory (generator/genkit/build.py:42); cancel/timeout sends SIGKILL to the pgid (process_unix.go:233) so Python never cleans up. Reproduced: 619MB androidgen-* left after kill. Frontend passes AbortSignal (lib/api.ts:157) so ordinary aborts trigger it; keys/*.jks + keystore.properties with plaintext passwords persist.
findings.recommendation: Build cmd.Env explicitly with TMPDIR=workDir and HOME=workDir (plus PATH, JAVA_HOME, LANG, PYTHON* vars) so all child output lives under the dir Go RemoveAll()s; this also stops leaking DATABASE_URL/ADMIN_TOKEN/IP_SALT to the child.

findings.title: Internal generator failures are classified as user errors (400), never recorded as errors, traceback dropped
findings.evidence: generate_headless.py:108-113 uses fail() for RenderError/OSError/any Exception; Go maps any {"error"} JSON to InvalidRequestError; server.go:176-185 answers 400 and skips RecordError. failure.Detail parsed then discarded; RecordError always called with detail "" (server.go:191,364,495) so errors.detail is never written. Server paths leak to users (render.py:222 'Missing variant directory ... /app/generator/variants/...').
findings.recommendation: Emit kind: invalid|internal from generate_headless (only SpecError/TypeError are invalid); Go maps internal to 500 + RecordError with the traceback in detail + generic user message.

findings.title: CI never builds the site's default 'standard' preset nor the headless zip path users download
findings.evidence: matrix preset: [none, lean, everything, all]; PRESETS are lean/standard/everything (spec.py:574-612) and catalogue default is 'standard' (catalogue.py:197). Only standard has auth on + googlesignin off, stripping <opt:googlesignin> from feature/auth SignIn.kt, AuthRepository.kt, AuthDto.kt, build.gradle.kts. CI uses create_project.py --no-zip (124) + test -x gradlew; generate_headless.py and render.zip_project are never executed by CI or unit tests.
findings.recommendation: Derive the matrix from PRESETS (+none,+all) via a setup job; generate through generate_headless.py, unzip, then check gradlew bit and build.

findings.title: Synchronous telemetry blocks responses (3+ sequential DB round trips) and DB outage kills the generator
findings.evidence: observe inserts after each handler; generate does RecordGeneration+RecordVisit+RecordRequest (server.go:232-237); each with 5s budget (server.go:45-47). Probe: small JSON response + 400ms post-handler work -> client receives headers after 402ms, contradicting commit 11377ec's 'after the last byte is on the wire'. main.go:55-60 makes store.Open failure fatal.
findings.recommendation: Collect a request's writes into one pgx.Batch (single round trip), ~1s budget; aggregate request metrics in memory per route/minute instead of a row per request; open the store lazily so generation works without Postgres.

findings.title: Validation regexes accept a trailing newline; API returns 200 with a project whose build-logic won't compile
findings.evidence:
re.match with $ accepts 'com.example.app
', '1.0.0
' (829), URL/font/host/scheme/module with trailing 
 — all verified ACCEPTED via ProjectSpec(...).validated(). render.py:292-298,323-324 splice them into Kotlin string literals (APPLICATION_ID, VERSION_NAME, fonts) -> unterminated string literal.
findings.recommendation: Use re.fullmatch (or \Z) throughout spec.py; reject control characters in Go before spawning Python.

findings.title: Go request struct silently drops unknown spec fields; every new option needs 4 synced edits
findings.evidence: Body decoded into typed generateRequest and re-marshalled (generate.go:121); an option added to spec.py + generate_headless.py allow-list (69-76) + frontend but not generate.go is dropped invisibly (Python's ignoredFields never sees it). Commits 5931457, f0fa4c0, 8e3461d each edited generate.go alongside generate_headless.py.
findings.recommendation: Pipe raw JSON through after generic guards; extract only telemetry fields with a narrow struct; derive Python's allowed set from dataclasses.fields(ProjectSpec); record ignoredFields.

findings.title: Admin telemetry is wrong: referrer is always self, country/detail never written, cancels recorded as bugs
findings.evidence: Referer of same-origin fetch('/api/generate') is the configurator page -> every row stores the site origin. store.Generation.Country never set; errors.detail never set. Client abort while queued (generate.go:117-118, ctx.Err()) or running ('signal: killed', not DeadlineExceeded) -> RecordError('generation') and resolved=FALSE reset (store.go:146). io.Copy failure (227) still recorded succeeded=true + 'generated'. Percentiles (store.go:199-208) include rejections, all-time.
findings.recommendation: Capture document.referrer/UTM on 'landed'; read x-vercel-ip-country/region; add outcome taxonomy (ok|invalid|internal_error|timeout|abandoned|download_interrupted); store queue_ms/python_ms/stream_ms; window and filter percentiles to ok rows.

findings.title: No container build, smoke test, deploy concurrency or token permissions in CI
findings.evidence: Docker image only built remotely by `npx vercel@59 deploy --prod` (179) after gates; no concurrency: block so two main pushes can deploy out of order (older finishing last); no permissions: block; vercel@59 vs 63.1.0 current.
findings.recommendation: Add a buildx job with gha cache that runs the container and smoke-tests /api/health and a minimal /api/generate; deploy preview -> smoke -> promote; concurrency group 'production' with cancel-in-progress false; permissions: contents: read.

findings.title: Go toolchain unsupported and inconsistent (1.24 go.mod/CI, 1.25 Docker); deps far behind
findings.evidence: go 1.24; ci.yml:47 go-version 1.24; Dockerfile:15 golang:1.25-alpine; go.dev lists only 1.27.2 and 1.26.9 as supported. go list -m -u: pgx v5.7.2 [v5.11.0], x/crypto v0.31.0 [v0.57.0]. install.sh:82 apt golang-go (1.22) auto-downloads toolchain. Zero Renovate commits in history.
findings.recommendation: go 1.27 + toolchain line; CI go-version-file: web/api/go.mod; golang:1.27-alpine; bump pgx; add govulncheck and staticcheck to the API job; verify Renovate app is installed.

findings.title: Leftmost X-Forwarded-For trust and per-address IPv6 rate limiting are spoofable/bypassable
findings.evidence: clientIP takes leftmost XFF; safe on Vercel (overwrites) and Caddy (header_up), but the generic Dockerfile behind appending proxies (Cloud Run, Fly, ALB, Railway) lets clients forge it; limiter keyed by full IPv6 address (139) so a /64 gives 2^64 keys; comment still says 'behind Caddy'.
findings.recommendation: TRUSTED_PROXY config (vercel | hops=N rightmost | none); key limiter and visitor hash on /64 for IPv6.

findings.title: Migrations re-run every boot with no version table or advisory lock
findings.evidence: migrate() Execs every embedded .sql on each cold start; no schema_migrations; concurrent cold starts on a fresh DB race CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS; future non-idempotent ALTERs/backfills impossible (needed for telemetry overhaul).
findings.recommendation: pg_advisory_lock + schema_migrations(name) with per-file transaction, or run migrations from the deploy job and only check version at boot.

findings.title: Unauthenticated unlimited DB inserts and no retention on any table
findings.evidence: /api/health, /api/options, /api/track not rate limited; each writes a requests row (middleware.go:58-62), track also writes visits; no DELETE anywhere in internal/store; requests kept 'for every request' (0001_initial.sql:78-79).
findings.recommendation: Rate-limit track; aggregate request metrics; daily prune of requests/visits and a retention policy for generations.

findings.title: Cross-site simple POSTs accepted on generate/track/feedback
findings.evidence: Handlers never check Content-Type; a third-party page can POST text/plain JSON with mode:'no-cors' (no preflight) and the server runs generations, records funnel steps and stores feedback; CORS only blocks reading.
findings.recommendation: Require application/json (415 otherwise) to force preflight; optionally reject Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site from non-allowed origins.

findings.title: Byte truncation splits UTF-8; long Hindi feedback fails with 500
findings.evidence: truncate returns s[:limit] bytes; SaveFeedback truncates body to 8000 bytes (536) while the form allows maxLength 8000 UTF-16 units (web/frontend/components/feedback.tsx:304); Devanagari is 3 bytes/char so >~2667 chars is cut mid-rune -> Postgres 22021 invalid byte sequence -> 500 'could not be saved'.
findings.recommendation: Back off to a rune boundary (utf8.RuneStart) or strings.ToValidUTF8 before slicing; same for generate.truncate.

findings.title: Runtime image: 188MiB JRE for keytool and Python recompiles on every spawn
findings.evidence: apk add openjdk21-jre-headless: Alpine lists Installed size 187.9MiB (comment says ~55MB). Official python:3.12-alpine deletes all *.pyc (docker-library Dockerfile:122-125), .dockerignore drops __pycache__, USER nobody can't write bytecode -> stdlib+genkit compiled per spawn: measured 0.18-0.20s vs 0.03s, vs 0.32s for a full generation.
findings.recommendation: RUN python -m compileall -q -j0 stdlib + /app/generator before USER nobody; precompute catalogue.json at build; jlink java.base,jdk.crypto.ec (~40MB) or move key generation to the browser; golang:1.27 with cache mounts and -trimpath.

findings.title: VPS deploy path has drifted from production and is untested
findings.evidence: Says 'No Docker' while production is the Dockerfile; apt Go 1.22; no JRE (no keystores); never writes generator/COMMIT; prints https://$DOMAIN/admin/overview (209) but routes are /api/admin/*; no CI coverage.
findings.recommendation: Delete web/deploy or reduce it to running the same image behind Caddy.

findings.title: Child processes inherit all server secrets; keytool passwords on argv
findings.evidence: cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), ...) passes DATABASE_URL, ADMIN_TOKEN, IP_SALT to Python/keytool; generator/genkit/render.py:485-496 passes -storepass/-keypass on argv, readable via /proc/<pid>/cmdline.
findings.recommendation: Explicit minimal env (see the staging-dir fix); keytool -storepass:env/-keypass:env.

findings.title: VisitorHash drops the last IPv6 hextet
findings.evidence: Strips at last ':' assuming a port, but clientIP already removed ports; probe: '2001:db8::1' and '2001:db8::2' both hash '2001:db8:'.
findings.recommendation: Hash the full IPv4 and the /64 for IPv6 using net/netip; no port stripping.

findings.title: Admin write endpoints map all errors to 404, echo err text; status not validated; notes cannot be cleared
findings.evidence: handleFeedbackUpdate/handleResolveError return 404 with err.Error() for DB failures too (413-415, 485-487); UpdateFeedback accepts any status unlike handleFeedbackList (385); notes=COALESCE(NULLIF($3,''),notes) (store.go:617).
findings.recommendation: Sentinel ErrNotFound -> 404, else 500 generic; validate status against the closed set; explicit clear semantics.

findings.title: Dead code and minor handler issues
findings.evidence: staticcheck U1000: logger() and logWriter (server.go:535-537) unused; /api/health hard-codes keystores:false (server.go:119); any ReadAll error answered as 413 (155-158); handleTrack uses r.Context() unlike other writes (259); recorder lacks Unwrap/ReadFrom so zip streaming loses sendfile.
findings.recommendation: Delete dead code; report real keystore availability; use errors.As MaxBytesError; detached ctx in track; add Unwrap/ReadFrom to recorder.

findings.title: Shutdown window shorter than generation timeout; no load shedding on the semaphore queue
findings.evidence: Shutdown waits 30s but GENERATE_TIMEOUT is 90s, so run() returns an error and the process exits 1 'fatal'; children in own pgid not signalled; requests wait on the semaphore with no cap or deadline (generate.go:114-119).
findings.recommendation: Cancel in-flight generations on shutdown via a base context; 503+Retry-After when queue depth > 2x concurrency or wait > ~10s.

findings.title: Docs and config comments contradict reality
findings.evidence: README names Dockerfile.api (file is Dockerfile); ci.yml:11 says Vercel IS connected for previews vs ci.yml:147 'not connected on purpose'; Caddyfile:30-31 timeout comment above request_body max_size; README:179-180 promises temp dir deleted as download finishes (false under abort); renovate.json5:14-16 claims 3-day min age but best-practices only covers npm.
findings.recommendation: Correct the comments; add top-level minimumReleaseAge '3 days' to Renovate.

findings.title: Ignore files miss generated/test artefacts
findings.evidence: .vercelignore/.dockerignore omit out/, *.zip, .claude/, .agents/, .venv/, tools/ (all gitignored); AGENTS.md generates test projects into ../out; README instructs local `vercel --prod`.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the relevant .gitignore entries, plus future DerivedData/.build/xcuserdata/Pods for the Swift and CMP templates.

findings.title: No API versioning, prose-only error shape, hand-copied TS types, full-scan admin queries
findings.evidence: writeError returns {error: prose} only (server.go:508-510); no /v1; Go structs re-typed in web/frontend/app/admin/page.tsx:9-58; Overview/Daily/FeaturePopularity scan all history each admin load (store.go:199-311).
findings.recommendation: /api/v1/{target}/...; {error:{code,message,field,requestId}}; generate TS types; time-window queries or a daily rollup table.

missed: tools/feature_combinations.py:25: the docstring says 'Fixed, so CI builds the same sets on every run', but .github/workflows/ci.yml never runs this pairwise-combination tool (grep finds no reference in .github). The CI matrix (ci.yml:86) only builds none/lean/everything/all, so marker-pairing bugs the tool was written to catch, like finding 3's standard/googlesignin gap, ship unbuilt.

store.go:536 + web/frontend/components/feedback.tsx:291: the feedback title is byte-truncated to 200 while the input allows 200 UTF-16 units. A 67-character Hindi title (201 bytes) is cut mid-rune, giving invalid UTF-8, Postgres 22021 and a 500 'could not be saved'. Verified with a Go probe. This triggers far more easily than the body case in finding 14.

web/frontend/components/configurator.tsx:363 calls generateProject(request) without the AbortSignal that lib/api.ts:151 accepts. The UI cannot cancel a generation, and a superseded click keeps a semaphore slot until Python finishes (generate.go:114-119).
adopt: Explicit child env with TMPDIR=workDir in web/api/internal/generate/generate.go: one change that fixes the staging leak (including keystore passwords left in /tmp) and stops secret env inheritance

Failure taxonomy kind=invalid|internal in generator/generate_headless.py mapped to 400/500 in generate.go, plus an outcome column (ok|invalid|internal_error|timeout|abandoned|download_interrupted) in generations
Spec caps (MAX_FEATURE_MODULES, name/package length) in generator/genkit/spec.py, exposed through the catalogue, plus a Go precheck before the semaphore; switch spec.py regexes to re.fullmatch

Opaque spec passthrough in web/api (raw JSON to Python after generic guards), with Python's allowed set derived from dataclasses.fields(ProjectSpec): the prerequisite for /api/v1/{target} and the cmp/swift generators

result.summary: PeriFlow (generated from android-base at commit a2da27c, and the template has not drifted since) is the best source of improvements for the overhaul. Its liquid glass has already been through three measured optimisation passes on a Redmi Note 10 Pro: jank went from 67% (median 61 ms) to about 6% (median 16 ms). The architecture is worth porting: one recorded scene in GlassStage, only floating chrome samples it, everything inside screens is drawn glass, and the lens samples a tiny layer at rest. Reading the Kyant backdrop 2.0.1 sources shows where the remaining FPS loss comes from: moments when the glass chrome animates, not steady scrolling. Every tab tap drives a press spring that scales the whole bar, so for about 0.5 s every frame re-samples, blurs and refracts the bar and re-renders Kyant's offscreen 24 dp BlurMaskFilter shadow (about 0.5 MP); the lens adds a scene replay, 7-tap dispersion and a per-frame BlurEffect inner shadow. That is about 8 offscreen passes per frame. The bar is also disposed and rebuilt by AnimatedVisibility on every return to a tab root, which recompiles AGSL shaders on the main thread and fades an alpha layer over a live backdrop. This is the clearest code-level cause of the 'pushy, glitchy' bar. Other costs: the background is filled 3 times full-window before content (window background, stage aura and per-screen aura); the aura repaints a CPU bitmap every frame while its colours animate, which happens on every launch; the voice orb keeps the frame loop running at 120 Hz; and hidden kept tabs keep ticking skeleton and Lottie loops. There are no quality tiers beyond Kyant's API checks: no power-save, low-RAM, thermal or frame-time fallback. On Android 11 (minSdk 30) the frosted bar still samples the scene, and glass top bars get no fade at all, so content scrolls illegibly under the title. Navigation fixes worth porting: kept tabs with a lifecycle cap and a per-tab back dispatcher, BackHold, linear predictive pop, slide-only push/pop, content-under-chrome insets, and sheets as Navigation 3 OverlayScene. Remaining navigation defects: a sheet double-pop on rapid Back, a detent sheet that re-measures its content every frame, a static LocalTopBarInset fed an animating height (the 'Saved' and 'typing…' subtitles recompose the whole screen every frame), Back swallowed for the ~0.5 s spring tail after each push, and bar motion decoupled from the screens. The report gives a prioritised optimisation plan with code sketches: bar kept composed and slide-only, no press swell on tap, a lens tint by clipped layer instead of a second composed row, cached outer-only shadows, a record-once SceneBackdrop, a DstIn scroll fade that works on all APIs, an aura crossfade, and a GlassQuality policy with FrameMetrics GPU-time adaptation. It also gives a generator design for an optional 'glass' feature with a fallback matrix, and lists dead or duplicate code not to port: ProgressiveBlur.kt, the unreachable live branch of Modifier.glass, and the roughly 90% duplicated bar and rail.

findings.title: Every tab tap re-renders the whole glass bar (backdrop, blur, lens, 0.5MP blurred shadow) for ~0.5s
findings.evidence: `LaunchedEffect(drag)` (:160-162) calls `animateToValue`, which calls press() then release() (LiquidInteraction.kt:185-196). The bar body's `layerBlock` scales by `drag.pressProgress` (:188-192). The lens reads pressProgress in effects, highlight, shadow, innerShadow and surface (:258-281). The layer change fires onGloballyPositioned, and Kyant's neverEqualPolicy coordinates make it re-record (KB DrawBackdropModifier.kt:260,337-341). Its ShadowNode is an Offscreen (w+4r)x(h+4r) ≈ 0.5MP target with BlurMaskFilter, re-recorded on every draw (KB ShadowModifier.kt:73-111). The lens switches to the combined scene backdrop with 7-tap dispersion, and InnerShadow builds a new BlurEffect every frame. That is about 8 offscreen passes per frame.
findings.recommendation: A tap should animate only the lens position (stretch from Animatable velocity): no press swell and no bar scale. Delete the bar body layerBlock. Reserve swell and live lens for a real drag. Drop innerShadow and chromaticAberration, or enable them only in the top tier while dragging.

findings.title: Glass bar is disposed and rebuilt on every return to a tab root (AGSL compile, new layers, press blip)
findings.evidence: `AnimatedVisibility(visible = showBar)` with `showBar = alwaysShowBar || onRoot` (:196-197, 287-302) removes GlassBar on every push from a root. On every pop to root the bar is rebuilt: rememberLayerBackdrop (GlassBottomBar.kt:107), BoxWithConstraints subcomposition, `RuntimeShader(GlowShader)` (LiquidInteraction.kt:218), and per-node refraction and highlight shaders (KB RuntimeShaderCache is per node; RuntimeShader.kt:10-14 constructs android.graphics.RuntimeShader). The LaunchedEffect then runs animateToValue, so press() starts for a frame before release() reverses it.
findings.recommendation: Keep the bar composed for the shell's lifetime. Hide it with graphicsLayer translationY, and set alpha 0 only when fully hidden so HWUI skips it and nothing is sampled. Clear semantics and input while hidden. Use a process-wide RuntimeShader cache, and skip the collector's first emission.

findings.title: Bar enter/exit fades an ancestor of a live backdrop
findings.evidence: `slideInVertically(...) + fadeIn(...)` and `slideOutVertically(...) + fadeOut(...)` on the glass bar (:292-295). Alpha < 1 on an ancestor forces the whole bar subtree offscreen on top of its own Offscreen and RenderEffect layers. The slide re-places it, so the backdrop re-records and re-samples every frame. PF removed fades from glass screens for exactly this reason (commit a8aedb0) but kept one on the bar.
findings.recommendation: Slide only. If a fade is wanted, fade the bar's tint and content, never an ancestor of drawBackdrop.

findings.title: No glass quality tiers: no power-save, low-RAM, thermal or frame-time fallback
findings.evidence: The only gating is `isRenderEffectSupported()` (Glass.kt:149, GlassBottomBar.kt:102) plus Kyant's API 31/33 checks (KB Platform.kt:6-10). A grep for isPowerSaveMode, isLowRamDevice, ThermalStatus and FrameMetrics in PF finds nothing.
findings.recommendation: Add a GlassQuality policy (Live / LiveNoLens / Frosted / Solid). Inputs: API 31/33, isLowRamDevice, power save (ACTION_POWER_SAVE_MODE_CHANGED), thermal listener, MEDIA_PERFORMANCE_CLASS, a user 'Reduce transparency' toggle, and FrameMetrics GPU_DURATION over 120-frame windows. The verdict is sticky per session and persisted per Build.FINGERPRINT plus version code. Sketch is in report section 3.6.

findings.title: Three full-window background fills before any content
findings.evidence: Three fills happen per frame: windowBackground (app/src/main/res/values/themes.xml), the stage `aura = { AppAura(...) }` (AppShell.kt:220,255,285 → Glass.kt:89), and each screen's AuraBackground (AppScaffold.kt:63-67). On phones the nav host is full-window and slide-only push with 25% parallax never exposes the stage. HWUI has no occlusion culling. That is about 7.8 MP per frame at 1080x2400 (about 10 MP during push), and every backdrop replays both auras again.
findings.recommendation: Drop the stage aura in the bottom-bar branch. In the rail branch, draw it only in the strip under the rail. Remove the window background after the first frame, and check there is no launch flash.

findings.title: Aura repaints a CPU bitmap every frame while its colours animate (every cold start)
findings.evidence: Three animateColorAsState calls (:60-62) feed AuraSpec (:67). Each frame's spec misses AuraPictures (:113-118), so a new 270x600 ImageBitmap is painted with 3 radial gradients on the main thread (:121-132) and uploaded. KEEP=2 (:135) evicts the light/dark pictures, and several AppAura instances thrash it. The phase starts Neutral and changes right after launch.
findings.recommendation: Animate a crossfade between two cached target pictures (no painting during animation). Keep 4 entries, and hold one shared AuraState instead of per-surface animations.

findings.title: Every GlassBar recomposition rebuilds the RenderEffect chain and re-records shadow and highlight layers
findings.evidence: Kyant allocates a new ShapeProvider per drawBackdrop call (KB DrawBackdropModifier.kt:94) and compares it by identity (:207-209), so update() runs invalidateDrawCache and builds a new effect chain (:174-188, 354-368). AppShell rebuilds `items = tabs.map { BottomNavItem(...) }` on every recomposition (:204-211), and it recomposes on every stack change (`state.current.size`, :196) and every tab change. The List param is compared by instance, so GlassBar never skips.
findings.recommendation: Remember the items (or use an ImmutableList), and remember the bar's drawBackdrop modifier chain keyed on colors and backdrop, so the element instance is reused.

findings.title: Voice orb keeps the frame loop alive at display rate at every tab root
findings.evidence: Four infiniteRepeatable animations (:61-86). The sonar (:101-112), ring (`rotate(turn)` :146) and core (`rotate(-turn)` :177) canvases read animated values while drawing, so they are re-recorded every frame and allocate gradients each time (:148,176,179). PLAUSIBLE: where HWUI's render-effect snapshot cache is off, the bar's blur and lens filter is re-applied on every composited frame even when nothing under it changed.
findings.recommendation: Animate only graphicsLayer properties (rotationZ, scale, alpha) over canvases recorded once. Build brushes in drawWithCache. Add Modifier.preferredFrameRate(FrameRateCategory.Normal), and stop ambient loops when idle. Verify the filter re-application with Perfetto.

findings.title: Hidden kept tabs are measured every pass and keep ticking infinite animations
findings.evidence: `val placeable = measurable.measure(constraints)` runs for every opened tab, with `if (active) placeable.place(0, 0)` (:62-64). The CREATED cap pauses only lifecycle-aware collectors. rememberInfiniteTransition in AppSkeleton.kt:43-52, AppCompanion.kt:41-46/71-85 and looping Lottie keep requesting frames in hidden tabs. `opened` never shrinks and is mutated during composition (:49-50).
findings.recommendation: Measure only the active child (legal in a custom layout). Provide LocalTabVisible and stop shared ambient animations when it is false. Key `opened` by session and trim it on resetAll.

findings.title: Drawn glass allocates and draws a blurred path shadow on every draw (all cards, chips, fields, icon buttons)
findings.evidence: `Modifier.glass` is `composed {}` (:137). The rim Brush is created in composition (:185-187), and a new Brush.radialGradient is created per draw (:193-201). outerShadow allocates a Path and a framework Paint, calls setShadowLayer, and adds a ClipOp.Difference path clip per draw (:210-225). HWUI also replays these ops every composited frame, and again inside the bar backdrop.
findings.recommendation: Make it a ModifierNodeElement using currentValueOf for tokens, built with drawWithCache. Bake the outer-only shadow once per size into an Alpha8 ImageBitmap with the inside cleared, and draw it as an image. Sketch is in report 3.6. Compose 1.12's dropShadow caches the same way but does not punch out the inside.

findings.title: Android 11 (minSdk 30): glass top bar has no fade or background over scrolled content
findings.evidence: `if (edge <= 0.dp || Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < Build.VERSION_CODES.S) return this` because the fade uses RenderEffect.createBlendModeEffect (:63-79). In glass, AppTopBar is transparent (AppTopBarDefaults.background) and AppScaffold lays content under it (AppScaffold.kt:82-107), so title and content overlap on API 30.
findings.recommendation: Record the strip into an Offscreen GraphicsLayer and drawRect(mask, blendMode = BlendMode.DstIn) after drawLayer(content). It works on every API at the same cost; sketch in report 3.6.

findings.title: Frosted fallback still samples the scene every frame
findings.evidence: Without RenderEffect only the tint changes (`container = if (isRenderEffectSupported()) colors.glass.clear else colors.glass.fallback`, :102; GlassRail.kt:114). drawBackdrop is still applied (:180, GlassRail.kt:175). Effects are no-ops (KB Blur.kt:13), but the scene is replayed sharply under a 90% tint every scroll frame, plus the Offscreen content layer, shadow and highlight.
findings.recommendation: The Frosted tier renders a drawn bar (tint, cached rim and shadow) with no backdrop.

findings.title: Sheet can pop twice on rapid Back or scrim taps
findings.evidence: `BackHandler { scope.launch { state.hide(); onBack() } }` is always enabled (:60-65). AppDetentSheet's `dismiss` (AppDetentSheet.kt:184-189) and scrim `detectTapGestures { dismiss() }` (:229) have no guard. `animateTo` uses `animate()` with no mutex (:146-153). A second Back or tap during the ~300 ms hide runs a second hide and onBack, which pops the screen under the sheet.
findings.recommendation: Add a `dismissing` flag to DetentSheetState (`dismiss(onGone)` returns early if already dismissing). Use BackHandler(enabled = !state.dismissing), and guard animations with MutatorMutex.

findings.title: Detent sheet re-measures its whole content every frame of open, drag and settle
findings.evidence: `.layout { ... val height = (full - top)...; measurable.measure(Constraints.fixed(constraints.maxWidth, height)) }` reads state.offset in layout (:235-239). Every offset change re-measures the sheet content (for example the Log form). Drags hard-stop at `large` (dragBy :120-125) with no rubber band.
findings.recommendation: Measure once at the large height and place at the offset. A pinned footer reads a LocalSheetVisibleHeight state in its own layout and offsets itself, so only the footer re-places per frame. Add rubber-banding past the top detent.

findings.title: BackHold swallows predictive Back for the ~510 ms navigation spring tail after each push
findings.evidence: `BackHandler(enabled = hold.holding || stackMotion.isMoving)` (:132) stays on until every entry reports at rest. The Fluid navigation spring (k=340, ζ=1) needs ωt≈9.4, about 510 ms, to come within 1 px over 1080 px. Swipes in that window get no finger tracking and replay later as plain pops.
findings.recommendation: Shorten the settle: stiffness ≈500-550, or visibilityThreshold IntOffset(2,2). Alternatively, report 'moving' only until about 90% of the transition's totalDurationNanos.

findings.title: Glass bar motion is decoupled from screen motion (fade and drop in 150 ms vs a 510 ms slide; appears only after predictive back commits)
findings.evidence: Bar visibility is a function of stack depth (`showBar = alwaysShowBar || onRoot`, :196-197), animated independently with tween(quick) over 1/3 height (:287-302). Commit dec4ff5 had to make the return 'quicker' because the bar arrived after the screen.
findings.recommendation: Option A: drive the bar's translationX from the root entry's transition, as iOS hidesBottomBarWhenPushed does. Option B: render the bar inside each kept tab's root entry, with a per-root SceneBackdrop, so it slides with the screen and follows the finger in predictive back.

findings.title: Tab bar and rail are ~90% duplicate, and the tab row is composed twice only to tint the lens
findings.evidence: GlassBottomBar.kt (337 lines) and GlassRail.kt (307 lines) duplicate the lens, drag, highlight and backdrop code. A hidden `alpha(0f).layerBackdrop(tabsBackdrop)...graphicsLayer(colorFilter = ColorFilter.tint(accent))` copy of every tab is composed, measured and offscreen-rendered (:224-239; GlassRail.kt:215-228).
findings.recommendation: Build one LiquidTabs(orientation). Record the tab row once into a GraphicsLayer and draw a cached accent-tinted copy clipped to the lens rounded rect, so only a tiny display list re-records per frame. At rest the lens is drawn glass.

findings.title: AppShell has three layout branches, each with its own GlassStage; the stage is used even for non-glass bars
findings.evidence: There are separate GlassStage plus TabbedNavHost call sites at :218, :253 and :283. A width-class change disposes every kept tab and the stage. The stage (scene recording plus aura) is applied regardless of AppTheme.style.bar.
findings.recommendation: Use one stage and one TabbedNavHost call site, switching only chrome and paddings. Create the stage and scene recording only for BarTreatment.Glass.

findings.title: Outer glass shadows get clipped by entrance fades ('square shadow corners')
findings.evidence: appAppear and AppAppear use `graphicsLayer { alpha = progress.value ... }` with the default compositing strategy (:152-185), and appAnimateItem fades with animateItem. Alpha < 1 renders offscreen within node bounds, so shadows drawn outside the bounds (Glass.kt:210-225, Kyant Shadow) are cut. Commit 03277f0 reports square shadow corners on glass bubbles.
findings.recommendation: Use CompositingStrategy.ModulateAlpha for single-element entrance fades: there is no offscreen buffer, so it is cheaper and nothing is clipped.

findings.title: Dead glass code: ProgressiveBlur.kt, the live branch of Modifier.glass, GlassStrength refraction fields
findings.evidence: A grep shows ScreenEdgeBlur and BlurEdge are referenced only in their own file (removed from the shell in e9dd952). GlassDepth.Chrome is never passed (only Glass.kt:56,134), so Glass.kt:147-170 is unreachable. GlassStrength.blur, refractionHeight and refractionAmount (:114-122) are used only there, and GlassStrength.Strong is unused.
findings.recommendation: Do not port them; delete them in PF.

findings.title: Scene recorded twice by Kyant layerBackdrop
findings.evidence: GlassStage uses `Modifier.layerBackdrop(sceneLayer)` (:88). Kyant's LayerBackdropNode.draw calls drawContent() and then records drawContent again into the layer (KB LayerBackdropModifier.kt:55-58), so the un-layered part of the scene is recorded twice per invalidation.
findings.recommendation: Use a custom SceneBackdrop implementing Backdrop that records once and draws the layer by reference (sketch in report 3.6).

findings.title: Drag lens launches a coroutine per pointer event and per animation frame, and captures a stale tabWidth/isLtr
findings.evidence: updateValue launches per event (:178-183). updateVelocity launches per frame and runs a VelocityTracker on animation output (:198-202). snapTo is launched per move (:249; GlassBottomBar.kt:155). `remember(scope, tabsCount)` captures tabWidth and isLtr (GlassBottomBar.kt:137-158).
findings.recommendation: Use one target state with snapshotFlow{target}.collectLatest{animateTo}, Animatable.velocity for stretch, plain float state for finger-tracked values, and rememberUpdatedState for tabWidth and isLtr.

findings.title: No depth cue on push after the fade was removed
findings.evidence: push and pop are slide-only (:26-47). The outgoing dim and the incoming edge shadow that iOS uses are gone. Modal predictive back still falls back to the spring popForStyle (:132-139). The comment 'Three shapes, and only three' (:19) sits above seven functions.
findings.recommendation: Draw a cheap scrim in each entry's drawWithContent from transition progress (no offscreen), plus a static 12dp edge gradient. Add a linear modal predictive dismiss.

findings.title: PeriFlow comments narrate history and brand words leaked into generic tokens
findings.evidence: Examples: 'It used to be painted per screen…' (AppAura.kt:103-109); 'The hold used to be a fixed 420 ms…' (BackHold.kt:32-35); 'No backdrop of its own: sampling the screen here too meant…' (GlassBottomBar.kt:222-223); measurement anecdotes (Glass.kt:139-145, ScrollEdge.kt:36-38). The AppScaffold KDoc is orphaned above LocalSheetSurface (AppScaffold.kt:34-46). 'PeriFlow's own' appears in AppMotionStyle.Fluid and AppDesignStyle.Glass.
findings.recommendation: When porting, keep a single 'why' sentence and move numbers into commit messages or docs, as AGENTS.md requires. Neutralise brand wording.

result.summary: VitFleet's first commit (25db943) is the generator's output untouched; I checked it against template 99c4edf, which has not changed since. So `git diff 25db943 HEAD` on generic paths is exactly the hand work done on top of the template: about 110 of 265 commits, 288 files. I found 33 template or generator defects that VitFleet had to fix by hand, and every one is still present in the template. The most serious: Ktor's cached bearer token is never cleared, so after sign-out the next account's requests carry the previous user's token (critical). A 408 or 429 from the refresh endpoint signs the user out and, because the offline queue is session-scoped, deletes their unsent writes. The replayer also deletes queued entries on any 4xx, including 401, 408 and 429. The WebSocket never connects because the client has no WebSockets plugin. The generator's monochrome-icon regex writes malformed XML whenever a custom icon is supplied; VitFleet carries a patch for it, and no generator test covers icons. The navigation fixes explain the "pushy" transitions: every pushed entry is transparent while push and pop fade it, so two screens show through each other; predictive back scrubs a spring; and rotation moves the tab host to a second call site, which loses every tab's state and ViewModels. Two VitFleet changes rest on a wrong diagnosis. Its `.underneath()` z-index call is dead code, because NavDisplay 1.1.7 sets its own z-index and already lowers it on pop. Its remembered entry provider is harmless but does not fix what its comment claims. Links and notifications create a second MainActivity, and the shared navigator Channel then splits commands between the two, so every other tap does nothing. VitFleet fixed this with singleTop, a LinkActivity trampoline, `PendingDeepLink` and a lifecycle-aware `applyWhileStarted`. In the design system it fixed the 48 dp touch target, disabled toggles stealing row taps, confirm dismissing before acting, a pull-to-refresh with a stale closure and a coroutine per scroll delta, a bottom sheet that neither scrolls nor stops at the keyboard, status icons that ignore the in-app theme, and accent-as-text contrast. The generator's palette math gives 2.3–3.8:1 for navy brands in dark theme and 1.6:1 for a yellow brand in light theme, and no test checks it. Ports worth taking: SessionTokens, the outbox replayer, ApiSignals, AllPages, ObjectStorage, FileShare, sharedHero, LocalCanNavigateUp, FullScreenKey, DestinationCatalog, a composable `:core:applock` with LocalOverlaysHidden, and about 20 tests. VitFleet has no liquid glass. Two of its patterns would defeat a glass bar: content is padded away from under the bar, and an opaque status-bar strip covers the top.

findings.title: Ktor bearer token cache never cleared: next user's requests carry the previous user's token
findings.evidence: loadTokens{} result is cached by BearerAuthProvider until clearToken(); grep for clearToken/authProvider in template finds nothing. VitFleet 53da40b: 'Ktor's bearer plugin kept the old company's token in memory after the new one was saved'. Fixed in VF core/network/.../auth/BearerTokenCache.kt
findings.recommendation: Port KtorBearerTokenCache (clearToken via Provider<HttpClient>), register it as a SessionScopedStore, and call drop() after every tokenStore.save in AuthRepository.persist.

findings.title: Refresh 408/429 ends the session and wipes the offline queue
findings.evidence: `if (result.code in REFUSED_RANGE) endSession(...)` with REFUSED_RANGE = 400..499 (:198) -> SessionCoordinator.kt:44 signOut -> :51 clears every store, including RoomRequestQueue (ResponseCache.kt:162-164 `: RequestQueue, SessionScopedStore`). VitFleet b445966/c61f279 fixed both.
findings.recommendation: Port VF SessionTokens.kt (Mutex, stale-token short-circuit, only 401 ends the session). Stop wiping the queue on involuntary expiry, or tag entries with their owner (VF QueueOwnership.kt + Room v2 migration).

findings.title: Offline replayer deletes entries on any 4xx including 401/408/426/429, and replays only on an offline->online edge
findings.evidence: `if (result.code !in REFUSED_RANGE) return ... queue.remove(queued.id)`; KDoc :208 'A request the server answers with a 4xx is dropped'; :221 replays only on isOnline.distinctUntilChanged().filter{it}
findings.recommendation: Port VF ResponseCache.kt:352-451: refusesEntry() treats 401/408/426/429 as momentary, marks refused entries instead of deleting them, wakes on queue growth and app foreground with a 30 s→5 min backoff, and serialises passes with a Mutex. Add an optional outbox screen.

findings.title: WebSocket never connects: plain client lacks install(WebSockets)
findings.evidence: AppWebSocket uses @PlainClient (websocket/AppWebSocket.kt:50); providePlainClient never installs WebSockets; webSocketSession throws 'Plugin WebSockets is not installed', caught at :93 and retried forever. VF HttpClientModule.kt:57-59 adds install(WebSockets).
findings.recommendation: Use a dedicated realtime client with install(WebSockets){pingInterval}. Skip ResponseObserver for websocket calls (VF NetworkRecording.kt:20), reset backoff only after a frame (VF AppWebSocket.kt:101), and synchronise connect/disconnect (VF :72,:116,:130,:136).

findings.title: Push/pop transitions alpha-fade the whole screen (full-screen offscreen buffer) and mix a tween fade with a spring slide
findings.evidence: push(): `slideOutOfContainer(...) + fadeOut(animationSpec = tween(motion.medium, easing = motion.standard), targetAlpha = 1f - motion.outgoingDim)` (lines 26-33); pop() mirrors with fadeIn (43-46). The CompositingStrategy.Auto source in Compose ui-graphics 1.12.1 says that whenever alpha < 1 'a compositing layer is created automatically to first render the contents fully opaque, then draw this offscreen buffer'. The slide uses motion.navigation() (a spring) while the dim uses a 250 ms tween, so the two desynchronise.
findings.recommendation: Remove alpha from screen transitions. Slide incoming 100% and outgoing about 30% on one spring (e.g. spring(1f, ~320f), roughly iOS duration 0.35). Dim with a scrim drawn in the top screen's drawBehind, driven by LocalNavAnimatedContentScope.current.transition.animateFloat (one drawRect, no offscreen buffer). Sketch in research.md §3.5.

findings.title: Tab switch fades and scales two full screens after a delay; iOS switches tabs instantly
findings.evidence: tabSwitch(): `fadeIn(tween(motion.medium, delayMillis = motion.instant, ...)) + scaleIn(..., initialScale = TAB_ENTER_SCALE)) togetherWith fadeOut(...)`, used by `AnimatedContent(targetState = state.selectedIndex ...)` in AppNavHost.kt:99-106. Both screens get alpha < 1 (offscreen buffers), and the 90 ms delay reads as lag.
findings.recommendation: Use EnterTransition.None togetherWith ExitTransition.None, or compose only the selected tab with a SaveableStateHolder. If an animation is wanted, use a crossfade of 150 ms or less on the incoming tab only, with no scale and no delay.

findings.title: check_versions.py cannot see the Gradle wrapper or new artifact groups (e.g. androidx.room3)

findings.title: Kyant drawBackdrop draws an UNBLURRED copy of the background below API 31, so a fallback is mandatory for minSdk 26
findings.evidence: `private fun updateEffects() { if (!isRenderEffectSupported()) return ... }` leaves graphicsLayer.renderEffect null while drawBackdropLayer() still records and draws the backdrop. androidMain Platform.kt: `isRenderEffectSupported() = SDK_INT >= S`, `isRuntimeShaderSupported() = SDK_INT >= TIRAMISU`. Template MIN_SDK = 26 (build-logic/.../AppConfig.kt:13).
findings.recommendation: In the generator's optional liquidglass feature, branch on isRenderEffectSupported() and on a missing stage (dialogs, popups; see issue #91) and draw a frosted tint with the same rim and shadow, as PeriFlow does (Glass.kt:149-155).

findings.title: Kyant lens() throws UnsupportedOperationException for non-rounded shapes, but only on API 33+
findings.evidence: `val cornerRadii = cornerRadii; ... else { throwUnsupportedSDFException() }` with the message 'Only RoundedRectangularShape or CornerBasedShape is supported in lens effects.' It is reached only after `if (!isRuntimeShaderSupported()) return`, so testing on API 31-32 never crashes.
findings.recommendation: Type the generator's glass modifier parameter as com.kyant.shapes.RoundedRectangularShape (Capsule, RoundedRectangle) or CornerBasedShape so arbitrary shapes cannot compile.

findings.title: PeriFlow glass indicator animates effects/highlight/shadow/innerShadow per frame, rebuilding RenderEffects every frame
findings.evidence: `effects = { val progress = drag.pressProgress; lens(10.dp.toPx() * progress, 14.dp.toPx() * progress, chromaticAberration = true) }`, `highlight = { Highlight.Default.copy(alpha = lerp(0.45f, 1f, drag.pressProgress)) }`, `shadow = { Shadow(alpha = drag.pressProgress) }`, `innerShadow = { InnerShadow(radius = 8.dp * drag.pressProgress, ...) }` (lines 258-265). Kyant source: DrawBackdropNode.observeReads { updateEffects() } rebuilds the chain on every observed change; InnerShadowNode creates a new BlurEffect whenever the radius changes; Highlight and Shadow nodes re-record a layer on every draw. GlassRail.kt:236-247 has the same pattern.
findings.recommendation: When porting to the generator: keep effects static (a top-level val lambda), show the press through layerBlock scale and onDrawSurface alpha, drop the animated innerShadow, and pass shadow = null at rest.

findings.title: PeriFlow Modifier.glass uses composed {} and outerShadow allocates Path + Paint + setShadowLayer on every draw
findings.evidence: Line 137: `): Modifier = composed {`. Lines 210-225: `drawBehind { val outline = shape.createOutline(...); val path = Path().apply { addOutline(outline) } ... val paint = Paint().asFrameworkPaint().apply { ... setShadowLayer(radius, 0f, radius * SHADOW_DROP, color.toArgb()) }`. Google docs: 'composed {} is no longer recommended due to performance concerns'.
findings.recommendation: Port it as a @Composable modifier factory or Modifier.Node, not composed. Replace outerShadow with Compose UI 1.12's Modifier.dropShadow(shape, Shadow(...)), which needs no graphicsLayer and caches painters in ShadowContext.

findings.title: BasicTextField(value,onValueChange) and VisualTransformation are deprecated in foundation 1.13.0-alpha03
findings.evidence: AppTextField.kt:127 `BasicTextField(value = value, onValueChange = { ... })`; AppOtpField.kt:98 uses TextFieldValue; AppFieldVariants.kt:63 `PasswordVisualTransformation()`. Compose foundation release notes: 1.13.0-alpha03 deprecates the value/onValueChange BasicTextField overloads and VisualTransformation in favour of TextFieldState/OutputTransformation.
findings.recommendation: During the design-system overhaul, move inputs to the TextFieldState overloads and BasicSecureTextField so the template does not start emitting deprecations when the Compose BOM reaches 1.13.

findings.title: Unused kotlin-android plugin alias (AGP 9 has built-in Kotlin)

findings.title: android.disallowKotlinSourceSets=false is a documented temporary AGP 9 workaround

findings.evidence: KSP 2.3.10 release notes: 'Deprecate the ksp(...) Gradle configuration in Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) projects in favor of target-specific configurations'. Template ksp = 2.3.12.

findings.title: AGP 9 KMP: Android app must be a separate module; shared modules use com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library with kotlin { android {} } (no variants/BuildConfig)
findings.evidence: Template convention applies `com.android.library` (line 17). kotlinlang: with AGP 9 'the Kotlin Multiplatform Gradle plugin stops being compatible with the com.android.application and the com.android.library plugins'. developer.android.com: the plugin is com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library; `androidLibrary{}` is deprecated since AGP 9.1.0-alpha09 in favour of `android{}`; build variants, BuildConfig, data/view binding are unsupported.

result.summary: I generated the spec_full project into .overhaul/out/Full and built devRelease (R8, non-debuggable, debug-signed by fallback; 234 s cold, 999 tasks executed) and devDebug (74 s). Sizes: arm64 release 3.89 MB, debug 25.06 MB. I measured both on the Redmi Note 10 Pro (Android 17, display locked at 120 Hz, so an 8.33 ms frame budget, Skia GL). To get past sign-in I wrote a fake DataStore session through run-as on the debug build and installed the release over it. Cold start median is 468 ms as installed and 366 ms after speed-profile; no app baseline profile ships. Plain list scrolling is excellent (0.07–0.22 % janky, GPU p90 6 ms). The cost sits in navigation: tab switching 1.6–1.9 % janky (p99 36–57 ms), push/pop 4.2–5.3 % (p99 36–48 ms). Per-frame traces show every tab switch spends 21–52 ms of UI time on its first frame and drops 1–5 vsyncs, because AnimatedContent recomposes the destination tab from nothing; each pop recomposes the root list (26–33 ms over two frames). Frame-by-frame recordings show the tab switch as a double-exposed cross-fade with both tabs visible. The floating bar moves on its own vertical axis at the wrong time: it sits over the incoming page on push, springs up over the outgoing page on a Back-key pop, and after a back gesture rises into an empty reserved strip 100–200 ms after the page settles. Root screens are clipped above the bar by that strip. I built a devtools variant and confirmed on device that the badge cannot be dragged: a 503x1038 px drag moved it 7x14 px, due to a stale capture in DevBadge.kt. The inspector also shows 0 kB for chunked responses. PeriFlow was not installed, so I installed its prebuilt dev benchmarkRelease APK, read only from its build output, and onboarded it as a guest with dummy values. Its Kyant glass is GPU-bound on this phone: scrolling 6.8 % janky, GPU p90 20 ms, RenderThread 14–33 ms per frame, PSS 108 MB against 63 MB. Its navigation choices are clearly better and worth porting: tabs stay composed (KeptTabs, first frame 8–12 ms), the bar fades in place, content runs under the bar, and the gesture back tracks the finger. One process slip: while checking a manifest I once ran ./gradlew (-q :app:tasks) in out/Full outside the gradle lock. It was killed immediately by a closed pipe, built nothing, and left no process behind. The debug build measures 10x worse (20.6 % janky tab switching, 2.4–3.0 s cold start), so smoothness must be judged on a release or benchmarkRelease build.

findings.title: Every tab switch recomposes the whole destination tab (21-52 ms first frame, 1-5 dropped vsyncs)
findings.evidence: AnimatedContent(targetState = state.selectedIndex) { index -> StackDisplay(entries = tabEntries[index]) } disposes the old tab's NavDisplay and composes the new one. Device framestats over 6 runs per direction: first-frame UI median 20.9 / 22.3 ms (max 45.8, one sample 52.4 ms: compose 19.5 + layout/draw 32.9), with the next frame 25-58 ms later. PeriFlow (KeptTabs) measures 7.9-12.2 ms.
findings.recommendation: Port PeriFlow's KeptTabs (periflow-android/core/navigation/.../KeptTabs.kt:43-72): keep opened tabs composed, do not place hidden ones, give each tab its own lifecycle and back dispatcher. Switch content instantly and animate only the bar indicator.

findings.title: Tab-switch transition double-exposes both tabs (cross-fade + 0.985 scale, 90 ms delay)
findings.evidence: tabSwitch = fadeIn(delay=instant 90ms)+scaleIn(0.985) togetherWith fadeOut(135ms). Recorded frames #15-#17 (Home to Feed) and #200-#204 (Orders to Home) show both screens' titles and cards overlapping (audit/frames/full_tab_crossfade_double_exposure_3up.png). RenderThread rises to 14-19 ms per frame during the fade (alpha+scale over shadowed cards).
findings.recommendation: No cross-fade between peer tabs: swap instantly as on iOS, or fade in only the incoming tab in 100 ms or less via graphicsLayer alpha. Remove tabSwitch and TAB_ENTER_SCALE.

findings.title: Bottom bar animates out of sync with push/pop and on a different axis
findings.evidence: AnimatedVisibility(visible = showBar = onRoot) with exit slideOutVertically(tween(280, easing = exit = CubicBezier(0.3,0,0.8,0.15))) and enter slideInVertically(sheet spring). Frames: on push the bar stays over the incoming page for 100-150 ms (#9-#21); on a Back-key pop it springs up over the outgoing page from frame 1 (#62-#68); on a gesture pop the page settles with an empty strip and the bar rises 100-200 ms later (#183-#213). See audit/frames/full_bar_glitches_4up.png.
findings.recommendation: Use PeriFlow's approach (AppShell.kt:287-295 there): a short in-place fade with tween(motion.quick) and no vertical slide. Alternatively move the bar with the root page via a NavEntryDecorator on root entries (iOS hidesBottomBarWhenPushed). Derive visibility from the scene on screen, not the back stack, so gesture and button pops match.

findings.title: Root tab screens clipped above floating bar by a reserved padding strip
findings.evidence: The root entry is wrapped in Box(Modifier.background(...).padding(bottom = inset)) with inset = AppBottomBarDefaults.occupiedHeight() (64dp + 2x12dp + nav bar). On device every list ends at a hard cut about 13% above the bottom. During push/pop and gesture back this strip shows as a blank band (content jumping by the inset height).
findings.recommendation: Pass the bar height as contentPadding via a CompositionLocal (for example LocalShellInsets) that root lists add to their LazyColumn contentPadding, so content scrolls under the floating bar. PeriFlow uses rootBottomInset = 0.dp.

findings.title: Pop recomposes the root screen from scratch (26-33 ms over the first 2 frames)
findings.evidence: NavDisplay keeps only the top entry composed. framestats for a Back-key pop: frame 1 compose 8.25 + layout/draw 19.06 ms, frame 2 5.25 + 13.22 ms, then 2 vsyncs skipped. 6-run medians 11.5 ms then 18.3 ms (max 25.7). gfxinfo push/pop: 4.2-5.3% janky, p99 36-48 ms.
findings.recommendation: Ship a generated app baseline profile covering the startup, tab, push and pop journeys (none exists; only the 11 KB library profile is merged). Make list rows cheaper. Longer term, keep the previous entry composed underneath with a custom scene.

findings.title: No app baseline profile shipped despite baselineprofile feature: about 100 ms slower cold start
findings.evidence: baselineProfile(project(":benchmark")) is declared, but find app/src -name '*baseline*' returns nothing; the APK has only assets/dexopt/baseline.prof at 11 KB from libraries. Cold start medians: 468 ms as installed (status=verify) against 366 ms after cmd package compile -m speed-profile (6 runs each).
findings.recommendation: Generate and commit a baseline profile in the template (Macrobenchmark journeys: startup, tab switch, push/pop, scroll) so every generated app starts at speed-profile performance on Play installs. Add FrameTimingMetric journeys to the benchmark module as a regression gate.

findings.title: Devtools badge cannot be dragged (stale captured offset in pointerInput)
findings.evidence: pointerInput(bounds, badge) { detectDragGestures { offsetX = (x + drag.x) ... } } where x is read in composition and never refreshed inside the coroutine. On device: input swipe 97,162 to 600,1200 moved the badge from [44,132][151,193] to [51,146][158,207]; a second slow swipe moved it back to [47,139]. A recorded drag shows it stuck at the top-left (audit/frames/fulldevtools_badge_drag_sequence.png).
findings.recommendation: Accumulate from state inside the lambda: offsetX = ((if (offsetX.isNaN()) startX else offsetX) + drag.x).coerceIn(0f, maxX), and likewise for Y.

findings.title: Debug build is about 10x jankier and is the only run path generated projects document
findings.evidence: devDebug: tabs 20.59% janky, p99 200 ms; cold start 2.4-3.0 s; APK 25.06 MB. devRelease: 1.88%, p99 36 ms; 0.37-0.47 s; 3.89 MB. Next-steps output, readme.py:26 and template/AGENTS.md:35 only mention installDevDebug.
findings.recommendation: Document installDevBenchmarkRelease (profileable, R8, debug-signed, created by the baselineprofile plugin) as the way to judge motion and perf. Ship a small perf script (gfxinfo reset, scripted taps, parse) in generated projects.

findings.title: Liquid glass (Kyant backdrop in PeriFlow) is GPU-bound on a mid-range 120 Hz phone
findings.evidence: GlassStage records the entire scene (aura + content) into a layerBackdrop every frame. GlassBottomBar.kt:180-186 adds vibrancy+blur(8dp)+lens(24dp) and :228 a second tabs layer redrawn every frame; ProgressiveBlur.kt:79-84 adds another blur. Device: Today scroll 6.83% janky, p90 38 ms, GPU p90 20 ms (plain list: 0.07%, GPU p90 6 ms). Tabs 3.99%, push/pop 6.1-6.5%. RenderThread 14-33 ms per frame. PSS 108 MB against 63 MB.
findings.recommendation: Make glass an opt-in design-system variant with a measured budget (GPU p90 at or under 8 ms during scroll on this class of device). Sample only the bar's bounds rather than recording a full-screen layer. Draw the lens and second tabs layer only during press or drag. Lower the blur radius. Skip progressive blur on Skia GL. Fall back to a frosted opaque tint when RenderEffect is unsupported or on low-RAM or 60 Hz devices.

findings.title: Navigation spring leaves a lingering sliver at the end of every pop
findings.evidence: navigationDamping=1f, navigationStiffness=400f. Pop frames #74-#86 show a 10-15% strip of the old page at the right edge for about 100 ms. A push/pop renders about 50 frames (420 ms) before motion stops.
findings.recommendation: Use a stiffer page-travel spring (the Snappy style already uses 700) or an iOS-like response of about 0.35 s. Tune against screen recordings.

findings.title: Devtools inspector shows 0 kB for chunked/compressed responses
findings.evidence: responseBytes = response.contentLengthOrZero(). The on-device panel shows 'GET /posts 1035 ms · 0 kB · 200' for jsonplaceholder /posts (100 posts). DevToolsPanel.kt:159/206 also integer-divide by BYTES_PER_KB.
findings.recommendation: Count the bytes actually read from the body, and format kB with one decimal.

findings.title: Scaffolded feature modules all become tabs with identical Grid icon; 7 tabs truncate labels
findings.evidence: Emits ShellTab(..., icon = AppIcons.Grid) per feature module. spec_full gives 7 bottom tabs; on device 'Settings' renders as 'Settin...' and Orders and Wallet share the same glyph.
findings.recommendation: Cap the bar at 5 tabs with an overflow, do not auto-add every scaffolded module as a tab, and require a distinct icon.

findings.title: ABI splits generate 5 near-identical APKs for an app with ~84 KB of native code
findings.evidence: isEnable = explicit ?: assemblingRelease. Per-ABI APKs 3,887,724-3,890,120 bytes, universal 3,988,008. Only libandroidx.graphics.path.so and libdatastore_shared_counter.so (~10 KB each per ABI).
findings.recommendation: Default splits off. Enable via the existing abiSplits=true property only when native-heavy dependencies are added.

findings.title: Release APK ships META-INF LICENSE files and kotlin builtins
findings.evidence: unzip -l of the release APK: 21 META-INF/androidx/**/LICENSE.txt files (106 KB uncompressed) and 54 KB of kotlin/*.kotlin_builtins.
findings.recommendation: Add packaging.resources.excludes for META-INF/**/LICENSE.txt and kotlin/**.kotlin_builtins in the application convention plugin.

findings.title: Cached-data banner uses a Wi-Fi-off icon while online
findings.evidence: AppBanner(text = sample_showing_cached, icon = AppIcons.WifiOff) whenever state.isFromCache. KtorNetworkClient.kt:100 emits the cached copy first on every stream(). The banner was on screen in every capture of the Full build while the phone was on Wi-Fi.
findings.recommendation: Show 'Updated N min ago' with a neutral icon. Reserve the Wi-Fi-off treatment for an actual isOffline failure.

findings.title: Floating bar SlidingPill reads animated Dp in composition (recomposes every frame)
findings.evidence: val x by animateDpAsState(...); Modifier.offset(x = x). Composition during tab-switch frames is 0.8-1.1 ms against 0.3-0.4 ms during push.
findings.recommendation: Read the state in the layout or draw phase: Modifier.offset { IntOffset(x.value.roundToPx(), 0) } or graphicsLayer { translationX = ... }.
